1.41.s:
nārada uvāca
ākhyātaṃ bhavatā sarvaṃ mune tattvārtha kovida /
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi yugānāṃ sthitilakṣaṇam //
1.41.d:
नारद उवाच
आख्यातं भवता सर्वं मुने तत्त्वार्थ कोविद ।
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामि युगानां स्थितिलक्षणम् ॥

1.41.s:
sanaka uvāca
sādhu sādhu mahāprājña mune lokopakāraka /
yugadharmānprabakṣyāmi sarvalokopakārakān //
1.41.d:
सनक उवाच
साधु साधु महाप्राज्ञ मुने लोकोपकारक ।
युगधर्मान्प्रबक्ष्यामि सर्वलोकोपकारकान् ॥
1.41.m:
Sanaka said:
Well said, well said, O greatly wise sage, benefactor of the world!
I shall proclaim the dharmas of the yugas, which bring welfare to all the worlds.

1.41.s:
dharmo vivṛddhimāyāti kāle kasmiṃściduttama /
tathā vināsamāyāti dharṃma eva mahītale //
1.41.d:
धर्मो विवृद्धिमायाति काले कस्मिंश्चिदुत्तम ।
तथा विनासमायाति धर्ंम एव महीतले ॥
1.41.m:
At a certain time, O excellent one, dharma increases;
likewise, dharma comes to destruction on the surface of the earth.

1.41.s:
kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca kaliśceti caturyugam /
divyairdvādaśabhirjñeyaṃ vatsaraistatra sattama //
1.41.d:
कृतं त्रेता द्वापरं च कलिश्चेति चतुर्युगम् ।
दिव्यैर्द्वादशभिर्ज्ञेयं वत्सरैस्तत्र सत्तम ॥
1.41.m:
The cycle of four yugas consists of Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali;
know, O most virtuous one, that it is measured there by twelve divine years [multiplied by thousands].

1.41.s:
saṃdhyāsandhyāṃśayuktāni yugāni sadṛśāni vai /
kālato veditavyāni ityuktaṃ tattvā darśibhiḥ //
1.41.d:
संध्यासन्ध्यांशयुक्तानि युगानि सदृशानि वै ।
कालतो वेदितव्यानि इत्युक्तं तत्त्वा दर्शिभिः ॥
1.41.m:
The yugas, together with their twilights and twilight portions,
are to be known according to time; so it is declared by seers of truth.

1.41.s:
ādye kṛtayugaṃ prāhustatastretāvidhānakam /
tataśca dvāparaṃ prāhuḥ kalimantyaṃ viduḥ kramāt //
1.41.d:
आद्ये कृतयुगं प्राहुस्ततस्त्रेताविधानकम् ।
ततश्च द्वापरं प्राहुः कलिमन्त्यं विदुः क्रमात् ॥
1.41.m:
In the beginning, they speak of the Kṛta yuga; then the arrangement of Tretā;
then they speak of Dvāpara; and they recognize Kali as the last in order.

1.41.s:
devadānavagandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ /
nāsankṛtayuge vipra sarve devasamāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.41.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः ।
नासन्कृतयुगे विप्र सर्वे देवसमाः स्मृताः ॥
1.41.m:
Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents
did not exist [as distinct] in the Kṛta yuga, O twice-born; all were considered equal to gods.

1.41.s:
sarve hṛṣṭāśca dharmiṣṭā na tatra krayavikrayau /
vedānāṃ ca vibhāgaśca na yuge kṛtasaṃjñake //
1.41.d:
सर्वे हृष्टाश्च धर्मिष्टा न तत्र क्रयविक्रयौ ।
वेदानां च विभागश्च न युगे कृतसंज्ञके ॥
1.41.m:
All were joyful and righteous; there was neither buying nor selling there,
nor any division of the Vedas in the age known as Kṛta.

1.41.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāḥ svācāratatparāḥ /
sadā nārāyaṇaparāstapodhyānaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राः स्वाचारतत्पराः ।
सदा नारायणपरास्तपोध्यानपरायणाः ॥
1.41.m:
Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras were devoted to their own proper conduct,
always intent on Nārāyaṇa, devoted to asceticism and meditation,

1.41.s:
kāmādidoṣanirmuktāḥ śamādiguṇatatparāḥ /
dharmasādhanacittāśca gatāsūyā adāṃbhikāḥ //
1.41.d:
कामादिदोषनिर्मुक्ताः शमादिगुणतत्पराः ।
धर्मसाधनचित्ताश्च गतासूया अदांभिकाः ॥
1.41.m:
Free from defects such as desire, devoted to virtues such as tranquility,
their minds set on the practice of dharma, devoid of malice and free from hypocrisy.

1.41.s:
satyavākyaratāḥ sarve caturāśramadharmiṇaḥ /
vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ sarvaśāstravicakṣaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
सत्यवाक्यरताः सर्वे चतुराश्रमधर्मिणः ।
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नाः सर्वशास्त्रविचक्षणाः ॥
1.41.m: All were devoted to truthful speech, abiding by the duties of the four stages of life, / endowed with study of the Vedas, and proficient in all treatises.

1.41.s:
caturāśramayuktena karmaṇā kālayoninā /
akāmaphalasaṃyogāḥ prayānti paramāṃ gatim //
1.41.d:
चतुराश्रमयुक्तेन कर्मणा कालयोनिना ।
अकामफलसंयोगाः प्रयान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.41.m: Through action proper to the four stages of life, born of the right season, / free from attachment to fruits, they attain the supreme goal.

1.41.s:
nārāyaṇaḥ kṛtayuge śuklavarṇaḥ sunirmalaḥ /
tretādharmānpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ //
1.41.d:
नारायणः कृतयुगे शुक्लवर्णः सुनिर्मलः ।
त्रेताधर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्व सुसमाहितः ॥
1.41.m: In the Kṛta age, Nārāyaṇa is white-colored and purely stainless. / I shall now declare the duties of the Tretā age; listen with attentive mind:

1.41.s:
dharmaḥ pāṇḍuratāṃ yāti tretāyāṃ munisattama /
haristu raktātāṃ yāti kiñcitkleśānvitā janāḥ //
1.41.d:
धर्मः पाण्डुरतां याति त्रेतायां मुनिसत्तम ।
हरिस्तु रक्तातां याति किञ्चित्क्लेशान्विता जनाः ॥
1.41.m: Dharma becomes pale-white in the Tretā age, O best of sages, / while Hari takes on a red hue, and people are attended by a little suffering.

1.41.s:
kriyāyogaratāḥ sarve yajñakarmasu niṣṭitāḥ /
satyavratā dhyānaparāḥ sadādhyānaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
क्रियायोगरताः सर्वे यज्ञकर्मसु निष्टिताः ।
सत्यव्रता ध्यानपराः सदाध्यानपरायणाः ॥
1.41.m:
All were devoted to the yoga of action and established in sacrificial rites,
true to their vows, intent on meditation, ever dedicated to meditation.

1.41.s:
dvipādo vartate dharmo dvāpare ca munīśvara /
hariḥ pītatvamāyāti vedaścāpi vibhajyate //
1.41.d:
द्विपादो वर्तते धर्मो द्वापरे च मुनीश्वर ।
हरिः पीतत्वमायाति वेदश्चापि विभज्यते ॥
1.41.m:
In Dvāpara, O lord of sages, dharma stands on two feet;
Hari becomes yellow, and the Veda is divided.

1.41.s:
asatyaniratāścāpi kecittatra dvijottamāḥ /
brāhmaṇādyāśca varṇāḥ syuḥ kecidrāgādidurguṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
असत्यनिरताश्चापि केचित्तत्र द्विजोत्तमाः ।
ब्राह्मणाद्याश्च वर्णाः स्युः केचिद्रागादिदुर्गुणाः ॥
1.41.m:
Even some foremost of twice-born men there were addicted to falsehood,
and the varṇas beginning with the brāhmaṇas had some evil qualities such as passion.

1.41.s:
kecitsvargāpavargārthaṃ viprayajñānprakurvate /
keciddhanādikāmāśca kecitkalmaṣacetasaḥ //
1.41.d:
केचित्स्वर्गापवर्गार्थं विप्रयज्ञान्प्रकुर्वते ।
केचिद्धनादिकामाश्च केचित्कल्मषचेतसः ॥
1.41.m:
Some performed sacrifices of the twice-born for the sake of heaven and liberation,
while some desired wealth and the like, and some had contaminated minds.

1.41.s:
dharmādharmauṃ samau syātāṃ dvāpare viprasattama /
adharmasya prabhāveṇa kṣīyante ca prajāstathā //
1.41.d:
धर्माधर्मौं समौ स्यातां द्वापरे विप्रसत्तम ।
अधर्मस्य प्रभावेण क्षीयन्ते च प्रजास्तथा ॥
1.41.m:
Dharma and adharma were equal in Dvāpara, O best of twice-born men;
and by the power of adharma, creatures diminished.

1.41.s:
alpāyuṣo bhaviṣyanti keciñcāpi munīśvara /
kecitpuṇyaratān dṛṣṭvā asūyāṃ vipra kurvate //
1.41.d:
अल्पायुषो भविष्यन्ति केचिञ्चापि मुनीश्वर ।
केचित्पुण्यरतान् दृष्ट्वा असूयां विप्र कुर्वते ॥
1.41.m:
Some will be short-lived, O lord of sages,
and seeing those devoted to merit, O twice-born, some feel malice.

1.41.s:
kalisthitiṃ pravakṣyāmi tacchṛṇuṣva samāhitaḥ /
dharmaḥ kaliyuge prāpte pādenaikena vartate //
1.41.d:
कलिस्थितिं प्रवक्ष्यामि तच्छृणुष्व समाहितः ।
धर्मः कलियुगे प्राप्ते पादेनैकेन वर्तते ॥
1.41.m:
I shall proclaim the condition of Kali; hear that with an attentive mind:
When the Kaliyuga arrives, dharma stands on one foot alone.

1.41.s:
tāmasaṃ yugamāsādya hariḥ kṛṣṇatvameti ca /
yaḥ kaścidapi dharmātmā yajñācārānkaroti ca //
1.41.d:
तामसं युगमासाद्य हरिः कृष्णत्वमेति च ।
यः कश्चिदपि धर्मात्मा यज्ञाचारान्करोति च ॥
1.41.m:
Reaching the dark yuga, Hari becomes black.
Whoever may be righteous and perform sacrificial practices,

1.41.s:
yaḥ kaścidapi puṇyātmā kriyāyogarato bhavet /
naraṃ dharmarataṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve 'sūyāṃ prakurvate //
1.41.d:
यः कश्चिदपि पुण्यात्मा क्रियायोगरतो भवेत् ।
नरं धर्मरतं दृष्ट्वा सर्वे ऽसूयां प्रकुर्वते ॥
1.41.m:
or whoever may be meritorious and devoted to the yoga of action—
seeing a man devoted to dharma, all show malice toward him.

1.41.s:
vratācārāḥ praṇaśyanti jñānayajñādayastathā /
upadravā bhaviṣyanti hyadharmasya pravatanāt //
1.41.d:
व्रताचाराः प्रणश्यन्ति ज्ञानयज्ञादयस्तथा ।
उपद्रवा भविष्यन्ति ह्यधर्मस्य प्रवतनात् ॥
1.41.m:
Observances of vows and traditional practices perish, as do sacrifices of knowledge and the like;
calamities will arise due to the prevalence of adharma.

1.41.s:
asūyāniratāḥ sarve daṃbhācāraparāyaṇāḥ /
prajāścālpāyuṣaḥ sarvā bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge //
1.41.d:
असूयानिरताः सर्वे दंभाचारपरायणाः ।
प्रजाश्चाल्पायुषः सर्वा भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे ॥
1.41.m:
All will be intent on malice and dedicated to hypocritical conduct;
and all creatures will be short-lived in the Kaliyuga.

1.41.s:
nārada uvāca
yugadharmāḥ samākhyātāstvayā saṃkṣepato mune /
kaliṃ vistarato brūhi tvaṃ hi dharmavidāṃ varaḥ //
1.41.d:
नारद उवाच
युगधर्माः समाख्यातास्त्वया संक्षेपतो मुने ।
कलिं विस्तरतो ब्रूहि त्वं हि धर्मविदां वरः ॥
1.41.m:
Nārada said:
The dharmas of the yugas have been declared briefly by you, O sage.
Tell of Kali in detail, for you are the foremost of those who know dharma.

1.41.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāścamunisattama /
kimāhārāḥ kimācārāḥ bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge //
1.41.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राश्चमुनिसत्तम ।
किमाहाराः किमाचाराः भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे ॥
1.41.m:
Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O best of sages—
what will their food be, and what their conduct in the Kaliyuga?

1.41.s:
sanaka uvāca
śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla sarvalokopakāraka /
kalidharmānpravakṣyāmi vistareṇa yathātatham //
1.41.d:
सनक उवाच
शृणुष्व मुनिशार्दूल सर्वलोकोपकारक ।
कलिधर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यामि विस्तरेण यथातथम् ॥
1.41.m:
Sanaka said:
Hear, O tiger among sages, benefactor of all the world!
I shall describe the dharmas of Kali in detail, as they truly are.

1.41.s:
sarve dharmā vinaśyanti kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvamāgate /
tasmātkalirmahāghoraḥ sarvapātakasaṃkaraḥ //
1.41.d:
सर्वे धर्मा विनश्यन्ति कृष्णे कृष्णत्वमागते ।
तस्मात्कलिर्महाघोरः सर्वपातकसंकरः ॥
1.41.m:
All dharmas perish when Kṛṣṇa has become black;
therefore Kali is extremely dreadful, a mixture of all sins.

1.41.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā dharmaparāṅmukhāḥ /
ghore kaliyuge prāpte dvijā vedaparāṅmukhāḥ //
1.41.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा धर्मपराङ्मुखाः ।
घोरे कलियुगे प्राप्ते द्विजा वेदपराङ्मुखाः ॥
1.41.m:
Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras turn away from dharma;
when the dreadful Kaliyuga has arrived, the twice-born turn away from the Vedas.

1.41.s:
vyājadharmaratāḥ sarve asūyāniratāstathā /
vṛthāhṝṅkāraduṣṭāśca satyahīnāśca paṇḍitāḥ //
1.41.d:
व्याजधर्मरताः सर्वे असूयानिरतास्तथा ।
वृथाहॄङ्कारदुष्टाश्च सत्यहीनाश्च पण्डिताः ॥
1.41.m:
All are devoted to deceptive dharma and intent on malice;
and scholars are corrupted by empty pride and devoid of truth.

1.41.s:
ahamevādhika iti sarve 'pi vivadanti ca /
adharmalolupāḥ sarvale tathā vaitaṃhikā narāḥ //
1.41.d:
अहमेवाधिक इति सर्वे ऽपि विवदन्ति च ।
अधर्मलोलुपाः सर्वले तथा वैतंहिका नराः ॥
1.41.m:
They all dispute, saying, “I alone am superior!”;
men are all greedy for adharma and captious disputants.

1.41.s:
ataḥ svalpāyuṣaḥ sarve bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge /
alpāyuṣṭvānmanuṣyāṇāṃ na vidyāgrahaṇaṃ dvija //
1.41.d:
अतः स्वल्पायुषः सर्वे भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे ।
अल्पायुष्ट्वान्मनुष्याणां न विद्याग्रहणं द्विज ॥
1.41.m:
Hence all will be very short-lived in the Kaliyuga;
because of the short lifespan of men, O twice-born, there is no acquisition of knowledge.

1.41.s:
vidyāgrahaṇaśūnyatvādadharmo vartate punaḥ /
vyātkrameṇa prajāḥ sarvā mniyante pāpatatparāḥ //
1.41.d:
विद्याग्रहणशून्यत्वादधर्मो वर्तते पुनः ।
व्यात्क्रमेण प्रजाः सर्वा म्नियन्ते पापतत्पराः ॥
1.41.m:
Due to the absence of the acquisition of knowledge, adharma prevails again;
all creatures, devoted to sin, die out of proper order.

1.41.s:
brāhmaṇādyāstathā varṇāḥ saṃkīryante parasparam /
kāmakrodhaparā mūḍhā vṛthāsaṃtāpapīḍitāḥ //
1.41.d:
ब्राह्मणाद्यास्तथा वर्णाः संकीर्यन्ते परस्परम् ।
कामक्रोधपरा मूढा वृथासंतापपीडिताः ॥
1.41.m:
The varṇas beginning with brāhmaṇas become mutually mixed;
intent on lust and anger, foolish, they are afflicted with useless remorse.

1.41.s:
śūdratulyā bhaviṣyanti sarve varṇā kalau yuge /
uttamā nīcatāṃ yānti nīcāścottamatāṃ tathā //
1.41.d:
शूद्रतुल्या भविष्यन्ति सर्वे वर्णा कलौ युगे ।
उत्तमा नीचतां यान्ति नीचाश्चोत्तमतां तथा ॥
1.41.m:
All varṇas will become equal to śūdras in the Kaliyuga;
the high descend to lowness, and likewise the low rise to highness.

1.41.s:
rājano dravyaniratāstathā hyanyāyavarttinaḥ /
pīḍayanti prajāścaiva karairatyarthayojitaiḥ //
1.41.d:
राजनो द्रव्यनिरतास्तथा ह्यन्यायवर्त्तिनः ।
पीडयन्ति प्रजाश्चैव करैरत्यर्थयोजितैः ॥
1.41.m:
Kings are intent on wealth and behave unjustly;
they oppress their subjects with excessively imposed taxes.

1.41.s:
śavavāhābhaviṣyanti śūdrāṇāṃ ca dvijātayaḥ /
dharmastrīṣvapi gacchanti patayo jāradharmiṇaḥ //
1.41.d:
शववाहाभविष्यन्ति शूद्राणां च द्विजातयः ।
धर्मस्त्रीष्वपि गच्छन्ति पतयो जारधर्मिणः ॥
1.41.m:
And twice-born men will become corpse-bearers for śūdras;
husbands, behaving like paramours, go even to lawful wives [for mere lust].

1.41.s:
dviṣanti pitaraṃ putrā bhartāraṃ ca striyo 'khilāḥ /
paristrīnirataḥ sarve paradravyaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
द्विषन्ति पितरं पुत्रा भर्तारं च स्त्रियो ऽखिलाः ।
परिस्त्रीनिरतः सर्वे परद्रव्यपरायणाः ॥
1.41.m:
Sons hate their father, and all women hate their husbands;
all are intent on other men's wives and dedicated to other people's property.

1.41.s:
matsyāmiṣeṇa jīvanti duhṝntaścāpyajīvikām /
ghore kaliyuge vipra sarve pāparatā janāḥ //
1.41.d:
मत्स्यामिषेण जीवन्ति दुहॄन्तश्चाप्यजीविकाम् ।
घोरे कलियुगे विप्र सर्वे पापरता जनाः ॥
1.41.m:
They live on fish and meat, and daughters [are made] a source of livelihood;
in the dreadful Kaliyuga, O twice-born, all people are devoted to sin.

1.41.s:
satāmasūyāniratāṃ upahāsaṃ prakurvate /
sarittīreṣu kuddālairvāpayiṣyanti cauṣadhīḥ //
1.41.d:
सतामसूयानिरतां उपहासं प्रकुर्वते ।
सरित्तीरेषु कुद्दालैर्वापयिष्यन्ति चौषधीः ॥
1.41.m:
Intent on malice toward the virtuous, they ridicule them;
they will sow herbs on riverbanks with spades.

1.41.s:
pṛthvī niṣphalatāṃ yāti bījaṃ puṣpaṃ vinaśyati /
veśyālāvaṃyaśīleṣu spṛhā kurvanti yoṣitaḥ //
1.41.d:
पृथ्वी निष्फलतां याति बीजं पुष्पं विनश्यति ।
वेश्यालावंयशीलेषु स्पृहा कुर्वन्ति योषितः ॥
1.41.m:
The earth becomes barren, and seed and blossom perish;
women desire the beauty and conduct of courtesans.

1.41.s:
dharmavikrayiṇo viprāḥ striyaśca bhagavikrayāḥ /
vedavikrayakāścānye śūdrācāraratā dvijāḥ //
1.41.d:
धर्मविक्रयिणो विप्राः स्त्रियश्च भगविक्रयाः ।
वेदविक्रयकाश्चान्ये शूद्राचाररता द्विजाः ॥
1.41.m:
Twice-born men are sellers of dharma, and women sellers of their vaginas;
others are sellers of the Veda, and twice-born men are devoted to the conduct of śūdras.

1.41.s:
sādhūnāṃ vidhavānāṃ ca vittānya paharanti ca /
na vratāni cariṣyanti brāhmaṇā dravyalolupāḥ //
1.41.d:
साधूनां विधवानां च वित्तान्य पहरन्ति च ।
न व्रतानि चरिष्यन्ति ब्राह्मणा द्रव्यलोलुपाः ॥
1.41.m:
They seize the wealth of virtuous men and of widows;
greedy for wealth, brāhmaṇas will not observe vows.

1.41.s:
dharmācāraṃ parityajya vṛthāvādairviṣajjitāḥ /
dvijāḥ kurvanti daṃbhārthaṃ pitṛśrāddhādikāḥ kriyāḥ //
1.41.d:
धर्माचारं परित्यज्य वृथावादैर्विषज्जिताः ।
द्विजाः कुर्वन्ति दंभार्थं पितृश्राद्धादिकाः क्रियाः ॥
1.41.m:
Abandoning righteous conduct, engrossed in idle arguments,
the twice-born perform rites such as ancestral śrāddhas merely for ostentation.

1.41.s:
apātreṣveva dānāni prayacchanti narādhamāḥ /
dugdhalobhanimittena goṣu prītiṃ ca kurvate //
1.41.d:
अपात्रेष्वेव दानानि प्रयच्छन्ति नराधमाः ।
दुग्धलोभनिमित्तेन गोषु प्रीतिं च कुर्वते ॥
1.41.m:
Vile men bestow gifts only upon the unworthy;
and they show affection to cows solely out of greed for milk.

1.41.s:
na kurvanti tathā viprāḥ snānaśaucādikāḥ kriyāḥ /
apātreṣveva dānāni prayacchanti narādhamāḥ //
1.41.d:
न कुर्वन्ति तथा विप्राः स्नानशौचादिकाः क्रियाः ।
अपात्रेष्वेव दानानि प्रयच्छन्ति नराधमाः ॥
1.41.m:
Twice-born men do not perform rites such as bathing and purification;
vile men bestow gifts only upon the unworthy.

1.41.s:
sādhunindāparāścaiva vipranindāparāstathā /
na kasyāpi mano vipra viṣṇubhaktiparaṃ bhavet //
1.41.d:
साधुनिन्दापराश्चैव विप्रनिन्दापरास्तथा ।
न कस्यापि मनो विप्र विष्णुभक्तिपरं भवेत् ॥
1.41.m:
They are intent on reviling the virtuous and reviling the twice-born;
no one’s mind, O twice-born, is intent on devotion to Viṣṇu.

1.41.s:
yajvinaśca dvijānaiva dhanārtharājakiṅkarāḥ /
tāḍayanti dvijānduṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇatvamāgate //
1.41.d:
यज्विनश्च द्विजानैव धनार्थराजकिङ्कराः ।
ताडयन्ति द्विजान्दुष्टाः कृष्णे कृष्णत्वमागते ॥
1.41.m:
Royal servants, for the sake of wealth, do not [spare] sacrificial twice-born men;
wicked men beat the twice-born when Kṛṣṇa has become black.

1.41.s:
dānahīnā narāḥ sarve ghore kaliyuge mune /
pratigrahaṃ prakurvanti patitānāmapi dvijāḥ //
1.41.d:
दानहीना नराः सर्वे घोरे कलियुगे मुने ।
प्रतिग्रहं प्रकुर्वन्ति पतितानामपि द्विजाः ॥
1.41.m:
All men are devoid of charity in the dreadful Kaliyuga, O sage;
twice-born men engage in acceptance of gifts even from fallen outcasts.

1.41.s:
kaleḥ prathamapāde 'pi viṃnindanti hariṃ narāḥ /
yugānte ca harernāma naivakaścidvadiṣyati //
1.41.d:
कलेः प्रथमपादे ऽपि विंनिन्दन्ति हरिं नराः ।
युगान्ते च हरेर्नाम नैवकश्चिद्वदिष्यति ॥
1.41.m:
Even in the first quarter of Kali, men revile Hari;
and at the end of the yuga, no one will utter Hari's name at all.

1.41.s:
śūdrastrīsaṃganiratā vidhavāsaṃgalolupāḥ /
śūdrānnabhoganiratā bhaviṣyanti kalau dvijāḥ //
1.41.d:
शूद्रस्त्रीसंगनिरता विधवासंगलोलुपाः ।
शूद्रान्नभोगनिरता भविष्यन्ति कलौ द्विजाः ॥
1.41.m:
Twice-born men in Kali will be intent on union with śūdra women, greedy for union with widows,
and intent on eating the food of śūdras.

1.41.s:
vihāya vedasanmārgaṃ kupathācārasaṃgatāḥ /
pāṣaṇḍāścabhaviśaṣyanticaturāśramanindakāḥ //
1.41.d:
विहाय वेदसन्मार्गं कुपथाचारसंगताः ।
पाषण्डाश्चभविशष्यन्तिचतुराश्रमनिन्दकाः ॥
1.41.m:
Abandoning the good path of the Vedas, adhering to the conduct of bad paths,
heretics will arise who revile the four stages of life.

1.41.s:
na cadvijā tiśuśrūṣāṃ kurvanti caraṇodbhavāḥ /
dvijātidharmāngṛhṇanti pākhaṇḍaliṅgino 'dhamāḥ //
1.41.d:
न चद्विजा तिशुश्रूषां कुर्वन्ति चरणोद्भवाः ।
द्विजातिधर्मान्गृह्णन्ति पाखण्डलिङ्गिनो ऽधमाः ॥
1.41.m:
And those born from the feet [śūdras] do not render service to the twice-born;
vile men wearing heretical emblems adopt the duties of the twice-born.

1.41.s:
kāṣāyaparivītāśca jaṭilā bhasmadhūlitāḥ /
śūdrādharmānpravakṣyantī kūṭayuktaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
काषायपरिवीताश्च जटिला भस्मधूलिताः ।
शूद्राधर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यन्ती कूटयुक्तपरायणाः ॥
1.41.m:
Clad in ochre robes, wearing matted hair, smeared with ashes,
śūdras will expound dharmas, devoted to deceptive reasoning.

1.41.s:
dvijāḥsvācāramutḥsṛjyacaparapākānnabhojinaḥ /
bhaviṣyantidurātmānaḥ śūdrāḥ pravrajitāstathā //
1.41.d:
द्विजाःस्वाचारमुत्ःसृज्यचपरपाकान्नभोजिनः ।
भविष्यन्तिदुरात्मानः शूद्राः प्रव्रजितास्तथा ॥
1.41.m:
Twice-born men, abandoning their own conduct, will eat food cooked by others;
they will become wicked-minded, and śūdras will become renunciants.

1.41.s:
utkocajīvinastatra bhaviṣyanti kalau mune /
dharmaṭīnāstu pāṣaṇḍā kāpālā bhikṣavo 'dhamāḥ //
1.41.d:
उत्कोचजीविनस्तत्र भविष्यन्ति कलौ मुने ।
धर्मटीनास्तु पाषण्डा कापाला भिक्षवो ऽधमाः ॥
1.41.m:
Those living on bribes will arise there in Kali, O sage;
dharma-destroyers, heretics, Kāpālikas, and vile mendicants [will abound].

1.41.s:
dharmavidhvaṃsaśīlānāṃ dvijānāṃ dvijasattama /
śūdrā dharmānpravakṣyantihyadhiruhyottamāsanam //
1.41.d:
धर्मविध्वंसशीलानां द्विजानां द्विजसत्तम ।
शूद्रा धर्मान्प्रवक्ष्यन्तिह्यधिरुह्योत्तमासनम् ॥
1.41.m:
To twice-born men who are prone to destroying dharma, O best of twice-born men,
śūdras will expound dharmas, mounting the highest seat.

1.41.s:
ete cānyeca bahavo nagnaraktapaṭādikāḥ /
pāṣaṇḍāḥ pracāriṣyanti prāyo vedavidūṣakāḥ //
1.41.d:
एते चान्येच बहवो नग्नरक्तपटादिकाः ।
पाषण्डाः प्रचारिष्यन्ति प्रायो वेदविदूषकाः ॥
1.41.m:
These and many other heretics—naked ones, red-robed ones, and the like—
will generally wander about, revilers of the Veda.

1.41.s:
gītavāditrakuśalāḥ kṣudradharmasamāśrayāḥ /
bhaviṣyantikalau prāyo dharmavidhvaṃsakā narāḥ //
1.41.d:
गीतवादित्रकुशलाः क्षुद्रधर्मसमाश्रयाः ।
भविष्यन्तिकलौ प्रायो धर्मविध्वंसका नराः ॥
1.41.m:
Skilled in singing and playing instruments, resorting to mean religions,
men who destroy dharma will mostly arise in Kali.

1.41.s:
alpadravyā vṛthāliṅgā vṛthāhṝṅkāradūṣitāḥ /
hartāraṃ paravittānāṃ bhavitāro narādhamāḥ //
1.41.d:
अल्पद्रव्या वृथालिङ्गा वृथाहॄङ्कारदूषिताः ।
हर्तारं परवित्तानां भवितारो नराधमाः ॥
1.41.m:
Having little wealth, bearing false sectarian marks, corrupted by empty pride,
vile men will become thieves of others' property.

1.41.s:
pratigrahaparā nityaṃ jagadunmārgaśīlinaḥ /
ātmastutiparāḥ sarve paranindāparāstathā //
1.41.d:
प्रतिग्रहपरा नित्यं जगदुन्मार्गशीलिनः ।
आत्मस्तुतिपराः सर्वे परनिन्दापरास्तथा ॥
1.41.m:
Constantly intent on acceptance of gifts, prone to going astray in the world,
all are intent on self-praise and intent on reviling others.

1.41.s:
viśvastaghātinaḥ krūrā dayādharmavivarjitāḥ /
bhaviṣyanti narā vipra kalau cādharmabāndhavāḥ //
1.41.d:
विश्वस्तघातिनः क्रूरा दयाधर्मविवर्जिताः ।
भविष्यन्ति नरा विप्र कलौ चाधर्मबान्धवाः ॥
1.41.m: Betrayers of trust, cruel, destitute of compassion and righteousness, / men in the Kali age, O twice-born one, will be kin to unrighteousness.

1.41.s:
paramāyuśca bhavitā tadā varṣāṇi ṣoḍaśa /
ghore kaliyuge vipra pañcavarṣā prasūyate //
1.41.d:
परमायुश्च भविता तदा वर्षाणि षोडश ।
घोरे कलियुगे विप्र पञ्चवर्षा प्रसूयते ॥
1.41.m: The maximum lifespan will then be sixteen years; / in the dreadful Kali age, O twice-born one, a girl gives birth at five years of age.

1.41.s:
saptavarṣāṣṭavarṣāśca yuvāno 'taḥ pare jarā /
svakarmatyāginaḥ sarve kṛtaghnābhinnavṛttayaḥ //
1.41.d:
सप्तवर्षाष्टवर्षाश्च युवानो ऽतः परे जरा ।
स्वकर्मत्यागिनः सर्वे कृतघ्नाभिन्नवृत्तयः ॥
1.41.m: At seven or eight years they are youths, and beyond that comes old age. / All will abandon their own prescribed duties, ungrateful and fallen from conduct.

1.41.s:
yācakāścadvijā nityaṃ bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge /
parāvamānaniratāḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paraveśmani //
1.41.d:
याचकाश्चद्विजा नित्यं भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे ।
परावमाननिरताः प्रहृष्टाः परवेश्मनि ॥
1.41.m: The twice-born will constantly be beggars in the Kali age, / devoted to showing contempt for others, yet delighting in another’s house.

1.41.s:
tatraiva nindāniratā vṛthāviśraṃbhiṇo janāḥ /
nidāṃ kurvanti satataṃ pitṛmātṛsuteṣu ca //
1.41.d:
तत्रैव निन्दानिरता वृथाविश्रंभिणो जनाः ।
निदां कुर्वन्ति सततं पितृमातृसुतेषु च ॥
1.41.m: Right there, people devoted to censure, falsely trusting, / continually speak slander against father, mother, and children.

1.41.s:
vadanti vācā dharmāṃśca cetasā pāpalolupāḥ /
dhanavidyāvayomattāḥ sarvaduḥkhaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.41.d:
वदन्ति वाचा धर्मांश्च चेतसा पापलोलुपाः ।
धनविद्यावयोमत्ताः सर्वदुःखपरायणाः ॥
1.41.m: They speak of duties with their voice, yet in their heart they covet sin; / intoxicated by wealth, learning, and youth, given over to all miseries.

1.41.s:
vyādhitaskaradurbhikṣaiḥ pīḍitā atimāṃyinaḥ /
prapuṣyanti vṛthaivāmī na vicārya ca duṣkṛtam //
1.41.d:
व्याधितस्करदुर्भिक्षैः पीडिता अतिमांयिनः ।
प्रपुष्यन्ति वृथैवामी न विचार्य च दुष्कृतम् ॥
1.41.m: Afflicted by diseases, thieves, and famines, excessively deceitful, / these people nourish themselves in vain, never reflecting upon their misdeeds.

1.41.s:
dharmamārgapraṇetāraṃ tiraskurvanti pāpinaḥ /
dharmakārye rataṃ caiva vṛthāviśraṃbhiṇo janāḥ //
1.41.d:
धर्ममार्गप्रणेतारं तिरस्कुर्वन्ति पापिनः ।
धर्मकार्ये रतं चैव वृथाविश्रंभिणो जनाः ॥
1.41.m: Sinners revile the guide along the path of righteousness; / people falsely trusting [disparage] one devoted to righteous action.

1.41.s:
bhaviṣyanti kalau prāpte rājāno mlecchajātayaḥ /
śūdrā bhaikṣyaratāścaiva teṣāṃ śuśrūṣaṇe dvijāḥ //
1.41.d:
भविष्यन्ति कलौ प्राप्ते राजानो म्लेच्छजातयः ।
शूद्रा भैक्ष्यरताश्चैव तेषां शुश्रूषणे द्विजाः ॥
1.41.m: When the Kali age arrives, the kings will be of barbarian origin; / Śūdras will take up mendicancy, and the twice-born will attend upon them.

1.41.s:
na śiṣyo na guruḥ kaścinna putro lana pitā tathā /
na bhāryā na patiścaiva bhavitāro 'tra saṃkare //
1.41.d:
न शिष्यो न गुरुः कश्चिन्न पुत्रो लन पिता तथा ।
न भार्या न पतिश्चैव भवितारो ऽत्र संकरे ॥
1.41.m: No one will be a pupil, nor a guru; neither son, nor father; / neither wife, nor husband will exist in this mixture [of castes].

1.41.s:
kalau gate bhaviṣyanti dhanāḍhyā api yācakāḥ /
rasa vikrayiṇaścāpi bhaviṣyanti dvijātayaḥ //
1.41.d:
कलौ गते भविष्यन्ति धनाढ्या अपि याचकाः ।
रस विक्रयिणश्चापि भविष्यन्ति द्विजातयः ॥
1.41.m: In the course of the Kali age, even the wealthy will be beggars, / and the twice-born will become sellers of prohibited liquids.

1.41.s:
dharmakañcukasaṃvītā muniveṣadharā dvijāḥ /
apaṇyavikrayaratā agamyāgāminastathā //
1.41.d:
धर्मकञ्चुकसंवीता मुनिवेषधरा द्विजाः ।
अपण्यविक्रयरता अगम्यागामिनस्तथा ॥
1.41.m: Twice-born wearing the cloak of righteousness, adopting the garb of sages, / will be devoted to selling unsellable goods and consorting with forbidden women.

1.41.s:
vedanindāparāścaiva dharmaśāstravinindukāḥ /
śūdravṛttyaiva jīvanti narakārhā dvijā mune //
1.41.d:
वेदनिन्दापराश्चैव धर्मशास्त्रविनिन्दुकाः ।
शूद्रवृत्त्यैव जीवन्ति नरकार्हा द्विजा मुने ॥
1.41.m: Intent on reviling the Vedas and censuring the scriptures of dharma, / the twice-born will live by the occupation of a Śūdra, deserving of hell, O sage.

1.41.s:
anāvṛṣṭabhayaṃ prāptā gaganāsaktadṛṣṭayaḥ /
bhaviṣyanti kalau martyāsarve kṣudbhayakātarāḥ //
1.41.d:
अनावृष्टभयं प्राप्ता गगनासक्तदृष्टयः ।
भविष्यन्ति कलौ मर्त्यासर्वे क्षुद्भयकातराः ॥
1.41.m: Terrified by drought, with eyes fixed upon the sky, / all mortals in the Kali age will be distressed by the fear of hunger.

1.41.s:
kandaparṇaphalāhārāstāpaṃsā iva mānavāḥ /
ātmānaṃ tārayiṣyanti anāvṛṣṭyātidukhitāḥ //
1.41.d:
कन्दपर्णफलाहारास्तापंसा इव मानवाः ।
आत्मानं तारयिष्यन्ति अनावृष्ट्यातिदुखिताः ॥
1.41.m: Eating roots, leaves, and fruits like ascetics, / men will sustain themselves, sorely distressed by drought.

1.41.s:
kāmārtā hrasvadehāśca lubdhā ścādharmatatparāḥ /
kalau sarve bhaviṣyanti svalpabhāgyā bahuprajāḥ //
1.41.d:
कामार्ता ह्रस्वदेहाश्च लुब्धा श्चाधर्मतत्पराः ।
कलौ सर्वे भविष्यन्ति स्वल्पभाग्या बहुप्रजाः ॥
1.41.m: Tormented by lust, short in body, greedy, and devoted to unrighteousness, / all in the Kali age will have little fortune and many offspring.

1.41.s:
striyaḥ svapoṣaṇaparā veśyā lāvaṇyaśīlikāḥ /
pativākyamanādṛtya sadānyagṛhatatparāḥ //
1.41.d:
स्त्रियः स्वपोषणपरा वेश्या लावण्यशीलिकाः ।
पतिवाक्यमनादृत्य सदान्यगृहतत्पराः ॥
1.41.m: Women will be intent only on self-nourishment, wanton, proud of their charms, / disregarding their husband's word, and constantly visiting other houses.

1.41.s:
duḥśīlā duṣṭaśīleṣu kariṣyinti sadā spṛhām /
asadvṛttā bhaviṣyanti puruṣeṣu kulāṅganāḥ //
1.41.d:
दुःशीला दुष्टशीलेषु करिष्यिन्ति सदा स्पृहाम् ।
असद्वृत्ता भविष्यन्ति पुरुषेषु कुलाङ्गनाः ॥
1.41.m: Ill-behaved, women of good family will always lust after men of vicious conduct / and become unchaste toward men.

1.41.s:
caurādibhayabhītāśca kāṣṭayantrāṇi kurvate /
durbhikṣakarapīḍābhiratīvopadrutā janāḥ //
1.41.d:
चौरादिभयभीताश्च काष्टयन्त्राणि कुर्वते ।
दुर्भिक्षकरपीडाभिरतीवोपद्रुता जनाः ॥
1.41.m: Terrified by fear of thieves and the like, people fashion wooden locks; / excessively harassed are they by famine and taxes.

1.41.s:
godhūmānnayavānnāḍhye deśe yāsyanti duḥkhitāḥ /
nidhāya hṛdyakarmaṇi prerayanti vacaḥ śubham //
1.41.d:
गोधूमान्नयवान्नाढ्ये देशे यास्यन्ति दुःखिताः ।
निधाय हृद्यकर्मणि प्रेरयन्ति वचः शुभम् ॥
1.41.m: Distressed, they will migrate to a region rich in wheat and barley; / holding foul deeds in their heart, they utter pleasant words.

1.41.s:
svakāryasiddhiparyantaṃ bandhutāṃ kurvate janāḥ /
bhikṣavaścāva mitrādisnehasaṃbandhayantritāḥ //
1.41.d:
स्वकार्यसिद्धिपर्यन्तं बन्धुतां कुर्वते जनाः ।
भिक्षवश्चाव मित्रादिस्नेहसंबन्धयन्त्रिताः ॥
1.41.m: People maintain kinship only until their own ends are achieved; / and mendicants are bound by bonds of affection toward friends and others.

1.41.s: annopādhinimittena śiṣyāngṛhṇanti bhikṣavaḥ //
1.41.d: अन्नोपाधिनिमित्तेन शिष्यान्गृह्णन्ति भिक्षवः ॥
1.41.m: Mendicants accept pupils merely for the sake of food.

1.41.s:
ubhābhyāmatha pāṇibhyāṃ śiraḥkaṇḍūyanaṃ striyaḥ /
kurvantyo gurubhartṛāṇāmājñāmullaṅghayanti ca //
1.41.d:
उभाभ्यामथ पाणिभ्यां शिरःकण्डूयनं स्त्रियः ।
कुर्वन्त्यो गुरुभर्तृआणामाज्ञामुल्लङ्घयन्ति च ॥
1.41.m: Scratching their heads with both hands, / women disobey the command of elders and husbands.

1.41.s:
pāṣaṇḍālāpaniratāḥ pāṣaṇḍajanasaṃginaḥ /
yadā dvijā bhaviṣyanti tadā vṛddhiṃ kalirvrajet //
1.41.d:
पाषण्डालापनिरताः पाषण्डजनसंगिनः ।
यदा द्विजा भविष्यन्ति तदा वृद्धिं कलिर्व्रजेत् ॥
1.41.m: When the twice-born delight in conversing with heretics and keeping company with heretical people, / then the Kali age grows strong.

1.41.s:
yadā prajā na yakṣyanti na hoṣyanti dvijātayaḥ /
tadaiva tu kalervṛddhiranumeyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ //
1.41.d:
यदा प्रजा न यक्ष्यन्ति न होष्यन्ति द्विजातयः ।
तदैव तु कलेर्वृद्धिरनुमेया विचक्षणैः ॥
1.41.m: When the subjects offer no sacrifices, and the twice-born make no fire-oblations, / right then the advance of the Kali age is to be inferred by the wise.

1.41.s:
adharmavṛddhirbhavitā bāsamṛtyurapi dvijā /
sarvadharmeṣu naṣṭeṣu yāti niḥśrīkatāṃ jagat //
1.41.d:
अधर्मवृद्धिर्भविता बासमृत्युरपि द्विजा ।
सर्वधर्मेषु नष्टेषु याति निःश्रीकतां जगत् ॥
1.41.m: There will be an increase of unrighteousness, and premature death as well, O twice-born; / when all duties are destroyed, the world is stripped of splendour.

1.41.s:
evaṃ kaleḥ svarūpaṃ te kathitaṃ viprasattama /
haribhaktiparāneṣa na kalirbādhate kvacit //
1.41.d:
एवं कलेः स्वरूपं ते कथितं विप्रसत्तम ।
हरिभक्तिपरानेष न कलिर्बाधते क्वचित् ॥
1.41.m: Thus the true nature of the Kali age has been told to you, O best of the twice-born; / yet this Kali age never oppresses those devoted to devotion to Hari.

1.41.s:
tataḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyuge tretāyāṃ dhyānameva ca /
dvāpare yajñamevāhurdānamekaṃ kalau yuge //
1.41.d:
ततः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायुगे त्रेतायां ध्यानमेव च ।
द्वापरे यज्ञमेवाहुर्दानमेकं कलौ युगे ॥
1.41.m: Beyond that, in the Kṛta age, [it is said to be] meditation; in the Tretā age, sacrifices; / in the Dvāpara, worship; and in the Kali age, they say giving alone is [prescribed].

1.41.s:
yatkṛte daśabhirvarṣaistretāyāṃ śaradā ca yat /
dvāpare yañca māsena hyahorātreṇa tatkalau //
1.41.d:
यत्कृते दशभिर्वर्षैस्त्रेतायां शरदा च यत् ।
द्वापरे यञ्च मासेन ह्यहोरात्रेण तत्कलौ ॥
1.41.m: What is gained in the Kṛta age in ten years, in the Tretā in an autumn, / and what in the Dvāpara in a month, that is gained in the Kali age in a single day and night.

1.41.s:
dhyāyankṛte jayanyajñaistretāyāṃ dvāparer'cayan /
yadāpnoti tadāpnoti kalau saṃkīrtya keśavam //
1.41.d:
ध्यायन्कृते जयन्यज्ञैस्त्रेतायां द्वापरेर्ऽचयन् ।
यदाप्नोति तदाप्नोति कलौ संकीर्त्य केशवम् ॥
1.41.m: What one attains by meditating in the Kṛta, by performing sacrifices in the Tretā, and by worshipping in the Dvāpara, / that one attains in the Kali age by reciting the praises of Keśava.

1.41.s:
ahorātraṃ harernāma kīrtayanti ca ye narāḥ /
kurvanti haripūjāṃ vā na kalirbādhate ca tān //
1.41.d:
अहोरात्रं हरेर्नाम कीर्तयन्ति च ये नराः ।
कुर्वन्ति हरिपूजां वा न कलिर्बाधते च तान् ॥
1.41.m: Men who praise the name of Hari day and night, / or perform worship of Hari, are not oppressed by the Kali age.

1.41.s:
namo nārāyaṇāyeti kīrtayanti ca ye narāḥ /
niṣkāmā vā sakāmā vā na kalirbādhate ca tān //
1.41.d:
नमो नारायणायेति कीर्तयन्ति च ये नराः ।
निष्कामा वा सकामा वा न कलिर्बाधते च तान् ॥
1.41.m: Men who chant 'Salutations to Nārāyaṇa', / whether desireless or with desire, are not oppressed by the Kali age.

1.41.s:
harināmaparā ye tu ghore kaliyuge dvija /
ta eva kṛtakṛtyāśca na kalirbādhate hi tān //
1.41.d:
हरिनामपरा ये तु घोरे कलियुगे द्विज ।
त एव कृतकृत्याश्च न कलिर्बाधते हि तान् ॥
1.41.m: Those who are devoted to the name of Hari in the dreadful Kali age, O twice-born one, / have indeed accomplished their purpose; the Kali age does not torment them.

1.41.s:
.
haripūjāparā ye ca harināmaparāyaṇāḥ /
ta eva śivatulyāśca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.41.d:
.
हरिपूजापरा ये च हरिनामपरायणाः ।
त एव शिवतुल्याश्च नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.41.m:
[...]
Those who are devoted to the worship of Hari and intent upon the name of Hari / are equal to Śiva himself; no doubt should be entertained in this matter.

1.41.s:
samastajagadādhāraṃ paramārthasvarupiṇam /
ghore kaliyuge prāpte viṣṇuṃ dhyāyanna sīdati //
1.41.d:
समस्तजगदाधारं परमार्थस्वरुपिणम् ।
घोरे कलियुगे प्राप्ते विष्णुं ध्यायन्न सीदति ॥
1.41.m: When the dreadful Kali age has arrived, one who meditates on Viṣṇu, / the support of the entire universe, whose nature is the supreme reality, does not perish.

1.41.s:
aho ati subhāgyāste sakṛdvai keśavārcakāḥ /
ghore kaliyuge prāpte sarvadharmavivarjite //
1.41.d:
अहो अति सुभाग्यास्ते सकृद्वै केशवार्चकाः ।
घोरे कलियुगे प्राप्ते सर्वधर्मविवर्जिते ॥
1.41.m: Ah, very fortunate indeed are those worshippers of Keśava, even once, / when the dreadful Kali age arrives, bereft of all righteous duties!

1.41.s:
nyūnātiriktadoṣāṇāṃ kalau vedoktakarmaṇām /
harismaraṇamevātra saṃpūrṇatvavidhāyakam //
1.41.d:
न्यूनातिरिक्तदोषाणां कलौ वेदोक्तकर्मणाम् ।
हरिस्मरणमेवात्र संपूर्णत्वविधायकम् ॥
1.41.m: For rites taught in the Vedas that suffer from defects of deficiency or excess in the Kali age, / remembrance of Hari alone is the cause of completeness here.

1.41.s:
hare keśava govinda vāsudeva jaganmaya /
itīrayanti ye nityaṃ nahi tānbādhate kaliḥ //
1.41.d:
हरे केशव गोविन्द वासुदेव जगन्मय ।
इतीरयन्ति ये नित्यं नहि तान्बाधते कलिः ॥
1.41.m: Those who continually say, 'O Hari, O Keśava, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O pervader of the universe!', / are not oppressed by the Kali age.

1.41.s:
śiva śaṅkara rudreśa nīlakaṇṭha trilocana /
iti jalpanti ye vāpi kalistānnāpi bādhate //
1.41.d:
शिव शङ्कर रुद्रेश नीलकण्ठ त्रिलोचन ।
इति जल्पन्ति ये वापि कलिस्तान्नापि बाधते ॥
1.41.m: Or those who utter, 'O Śiva, O Śaṅkara, O Lord of Rudras, O Blue-throated One, O Three-eyed One!', / are likewise not oppressed by the Kali age.

1.41.s:
mahādeva virūpākṣa gaṅgādhara mṛḍāvyaya /
itthaṃ vadanti ye vipra te kṛtārthā na saṃśayaḥ //
1.41.d:
महादेव विरूपाक्ष गङ्गाधर मृडाव्यय ।
इत्थं वदन्ति ये विप्र ते कृतार्था न संशयः ॥
1.41.m: Those who say, 'O Mahādeva, O Odd-eyed One, O bearer of the Gaṅgā, O gracious, imperishable One!', / have achieved their purpose, O twice-born one; there is no doubt.

1.41.s:
janārdana jagannāta pītāṃbaradharācyuta /
iti vāpyuñcarantīha na ca teṣāṃ kalerbhayam //
1.41.d:
जनार्दन जगन्नात पीतांबरधराच्युत ।
इति वाप्युञ्चरन्तीह न च तेषां कलेर्भयम् ॥
1.41.m: Or those who utter here, 'O Janārdana, O Lord of the world, O yellow-robed Acyuta!', / have no fear of the Kali age.

1.41.s:
saṃsāre sulabhāḥ puṃsāṃ putradāradhanādayaḥ /
ghore kaliyuge vipra haribhaktastu durlabhā //
1.41.d:
संसारे सुलभाः पुंसां पुत्रदारधनादयः ।
घोरे कलियुगे विप्र हरिभक्तस्तु दुर्लभा ॥
1.41.m: Sons, wives, wealth, and the like are easily attained by men in this worldly existence; / but devotion to Hari, O twice-born one, is rare in the dreadful Kali age.

1.41.s:
karmaśraddhāvihīnā ye pāṣaṇḍā vedanindakāḥ /
adharmaniratā naiva narakārhā harismṛteḥ //
1.41.d:
कर्मश्रद्धाविहीना ये पाषण्डा वेदनिन्दकाः ।
अधर्मनिरता नैव नरकार्हा हरिस्मृतेः ॥
1.41.m: Even those who lack faith in rituals, heretics who revile the Vedas, / and those intent upon unrighteousness, do not deserve hell because of the remembrance of Hari.

1.41.s:
vedamārgabahiṣṭānāṃ janānāṃ pāpakarmaṇām /
manaḥ śuddhivihīnānāṃ harināmnaiva niṣkṛtiḥ //
1.41.d:
वेदमार्गबहिष्टानां जनानां पापकर्मणाम् ।
मनः शुद्धिविहीनानां हरिनाम्नैव निष्कृतिः ॥
1.41.m: For people outside the Vedic path, of sinful deeds, / and bereft of purity of mind, deliverance comes through the name of Hari alone.

1.41.s:
daivādhīnaṃ jagatsarvamidaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam /
yathāpreritametena tathaiva kuruteṃ dvija //
1.41.d:
दैवाधीनं जगत्सर्वमिदं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
यथाप्रेरितमेतेन तथैव कुरुतें द्विज ॥
1.41.m: This entire world, both immovable and moving, is subject to fate; / as prompted by it, O twice-born one, so it acts.

1.41.s:
śaktitaḥ sarvakarmāṇi vedoktāni vidhāya ca /
samarpayenmahāviṣṇau nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.41.d:
शक्तितः सर्वकर्माणि वेदोक्तानि विधाय च ।
समर्पयेन्महाविष्णौ नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.41.m: And having performed all rites prescribed in the Vedas to the best of one's ability, / devoted to Nārāyaṇa, one should surrender them to Mahāviṣṇu.

1.41.s:
samarpitāni karmāṇi mahaviṣṇau parātmani /
saṃpūrṇatāṃ prayāntyeva harismaraṇamātrataḥ //
1.41.d:
समर्पितानि कर्माणि महविष्णौ परात्मनि ।
संपूर्णतां प्रयान्त्येव हरिस्मरणमात्रतः ॥
1.41.m: Actions surrendered to Mahāviṣṇu, the supreme Self, / attain completion merely by remembering Hari.

1.41.s:
haribhaktiratānāṃ ca pāpabandho na jāyate /
ato 'tidurlabhā loke haribhaktirdurātmanām //
1.41.d:
हरिभक्तिरतानां च पापबन्धो न जायते ।
अतो ऽतिदुर्लभा लोके हरिभक्तिर्दुरात्मनाम् ॥
1.41.m: And for those delighting in devotion to Hari, no bondage of sin arises; / therefore devotion to Hari is extremely difficult to attain in the world for wicked souls.

1.41.s:
aho hariparā ye tu kalau ghore bhayaṅkare /
te subhāgyā mahātmānaḥ satsaṃgara hitā api //
1.41.d:
अहो हरिपरा ये तु कलौ घोरे भयङ्करे ।
ते सुभाग्या महात्मानः सत्संगर हिता अपि ॥
1.41.m: Ah, those who are devoted to Hari in the fierce, terrifying Kali [age], / they are greatly fortunate, great-souled, even if devoid of the company of the good!

1.41.s:
harismaraṇaniṣṭānāṃ śivanāmaratātmanām /
satyaṃ samastakarmāṇi yānti saṃpūrṇatāṃ dvija //
1.41.d:
हरिस्मरणनिष्टानां शिवनामरतात्मनाम् ।
सत्यं समस्तकर्माणि यान्ति संपूर्णतां द्विज ॥
1.41.m: For those steadfast in remembering Hari, whose souls delight in the name of Śiva, / all rites truly attain completion, O twice-born!

1.41.s:
aho bhāgyamaho bhāgyaṃ harināma ratātmanām /
tridarśerapi te pūjyāḥ kimanyairbahubhāṣitaiḥ //
1.41.d:
अहो भाग्यमहो भाग्यं हरिनाम रतात्मनाम् ।
त्रिदर्शेरपि ते पूज्याः किमन्यैर्बहुभाषितैः ॥
1.41.m: Ah, what fortune! Ah, what fortune for those whose souls delight in the name of Hari! / They are worthy of worship even by the gods; what need of many other words?

1.41.s:
tasmātsamastalokānāṃ hitameva mayocyate /
harināmaparānmartyānna kalirbādhartakvacit //
1.41.d:
तस्मात्समस्तलोकानां हितमेव मयोच्यते ।
हरिनामपरान्मर्त्यान्न कलिर्बाधर्तक्वचित् ॥
1.41.m: Therefore only the welfare of all worlds is spoken by me: / Kali never afflicts mortals devoted to the name of Hari.

1.41.s:
harernāmaiva nāmaiva nāmaiva mama jīvanam /
kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā //
1.41.d:
हरेर्नामैव नामैव नामैव मम जीवनम् ।
कलौ नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरन्यथा ॥
1.41.m: Only the name of Hari, only the name, only the name is my life! / In Kali there is no other recourse, none at all, none otherwise.

1.41.s:
sūta uvāca
evaṃ sa nārado viprāḥ sanakena prabodhitaḥ /
parāṃ nirvṛttimāpannaḥ punaretaduvāca ha //
1.41.d:
सूत उवाच
एवं स नारदो विप्राः सनकेन प्रबोधितः ।
परां निर्वृत्तिमापन्नः पुनरेतदुवाच ह ॥
1.41.m: Sūta said: / Thus enlightened by Sanaka, O brāhmaṇas, Nārada, / having attained supreme serenity, spoke this once more:

1.41.s:
nārada uvāca
bhagavansarvaśāstrajña svayātikaruṇātmanā /
prakāśitaṃ jagajjyotiḥ paraṃ brahma sanātanam //
1.41.d:
नारद उवाच
भगवन्सर्वशास्त्रज्ञ स्वयातिकरुणात्मना ।
प्रकाशितं जगज्ज्योतिः परं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥
1.41.m: Nārada said: / O Lord, knower of all scriptures, by you of very compassionate nature / the light of the universe, the supreme eternal Brahman, has been revealed.

1.41.s:
etadeva paraṃ puṇyametadeva paraṃ tapaḥ /
yaḥ smaretpuṇḍarīkākṣaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam //
1.41.d:
एतदेव परं पुण्यमेतदेव परं तपः ।
यः स्मरेत्पुण्डरीकाक्षं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ॥
1.41.m: This alone is supreme merit, this alone is supreme austerity, / that one remembers the lotus-eyed Lord, the destroyer of all sins.

1.41.s:
brahmannānājagañcaitadekacitsaṃprakāśitam /
tvayoktaṃ tatpratīye 'haṃ kathaṃ dṛṣṭāntamantarā //
1.41.d:
ब्रह्मन्नानाजगञ्चैतदेकचित्संप्रकाशितम् ।
त्वयोक्तं तत्प्रतीये ऽहं कथं दृष्टान्तमन्तरा ॥
1.41.m: O Brahman, that this manifold universe is illuminated by a single consciousness / has been spoken by you; how can I comprehend that without an illustration?

1.41.s:
tasmādyena yathā brahma pratītaṃ bodhitena tu /
tadākhyāhi yathā cittaṃ sīdatsthitimavāpnuyāt //
1.41.d:
तस्माद्येन यथा ब्रह्म प्रतीतं बोधितेन तु ।
तदाख्याहि यथा चित्तं सीदत्स्थितिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.41.m: Therefore tell me how and by what [means] Brahman is comprehended by one instructed, / so that my faltering mind may attain stability.

1.41.s:
etacchrutvā vaco viprā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ /
sanakaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ smarannārāyaṇaṃ param //
1.41.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो विप्रा नारदस्य महात्मनः ।
सनकः प्रत्युवाचेदं स्मरन्नारायणं परम् ॥
1.41.m: Having heard this speech of the great-souled Nārada, O brāhmaṇas, / Sanaka replied this, remembering the supreme Nārāyaṇa:

1.41.s:
sanaka uvāca
brahmannahaṃ dhyānaparo bhaveyaṃ sanandanaṃ pṛccha yathābhilāṣam /
vedāntaśāstre kuśalastavāyaṃ nivartayedvā paramāryavandyaḥ //
1.41.d:
सनक उवाच
ब्रह्मन्नहं ध्यानपरो भवेयं सनन्दनं पृच्छ यथाभिलाषम् ।
वेदान्तशास्त्रे कुशलस्तवायं निवर्तयेद्वा परमार्यवन्द्यः ॥
1.41.m: Sanaka said: / O brāhmaṇa, I am intent upon meditation; ask Sanandana according to your wish. / Skilled in the Vedānta scripture, worthy of worship by the foremost noble ones, he will resolve [your doubt].

1.41.s:
itīritaṃ samākarṇya sanakasya sa nāradaḥ /
sanandanaṃ mokṣadharmānpraṣṭuṃ samupacakrame //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde nāmamahātmyannāmaikacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.41.d:
इतीरितं समाकर्ण्य सनकस्य स नारदः ।
सनन्दनं मोक्षधर्मान्प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे नाममहात्म्यन्नामैकचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.41.m:
Hearing this spoken by Sanaka, Nārada / proceeded to ask Sanandana about the principles of liberation.

Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named 'The Eulogy of Greatness of the Name', in the first quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.42.s:
śrīnārada uvāca
kutaḥ sṛṣṭamidaṃ brahmañjagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
pralaye ca kamabhyeti tanme brūhi sanandana //
1.42.d:
श्रीनारद उवाच
कुतः सृष्टमिदं ब्रह्मञ्जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
प्रलये च कमभ्येति तन्मे ब्रूहि सनन्दन ॥
1.42.m: Glorious Nārada said: / Whence was this world of moving and unmoving beings created, O brāhmaṇa, / and to whom does it go in the cosmic dissolution? Tell me that, O Sanandana!

1.42.s:
sasāgaraḥ sagaganaḥ saśailaḥ sabalāhakaḥ /
sabhūmiḥ sāgnipavano loko 'yaṃ kena nirmitaḥ //
1.42.d:
ससागरः सगगनः सशैलः सबलाहकः ।
सभूमिः साग्निपवनो लोको ऽयं केन निर्मितः ॥
1.42.m: Together with oceans, skies, mountains, and clouds, / together with earth, fire, and wind, by whom was this world fashioned?

1.42.s:
kathaṃ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni kathaṃ varṇavibhaktayaḥ /
śaucāśaucaṃ kathaṃ teṣāṃ dharmādharmavidhiḥ katham //
1.42.d:
कथं सृष्टानि भूतानि कथं वर्णविभक्तयः ।
शौचाशौचं कथं तेषां धर्माधर्मविधिः कथम् ॥
1.42.m: How were the beings created? How the divisions of class? / What of their purity and impurity? How the rules of righteousness and unrighteousness?

1.42.s:
kīdṛśo jīvatāṃ jīvaḥ kva vā gacchanti ye mṛtāḥ /
asmāllokādamuṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ śaṃsatu me bhavān //
1.42.d:
कीदृशो जीवतां जीवः क्व वा गच्छन्ति ये मृताः ।
अस्माल्लोकादमुं लोकं सर्वं शंसतु मे भवान् ॥
1.42.m: What is the individual soul of living beings? Where do they go who die / from this world to the world beyond? Explain everything to me!

1.42.s:
sanandana uvāca
śṛṇu nārada vakṣyāmi cetihāsaṃ purātanam /
bhṛguṇābhihitaṃ śāstraṃ bharadvājāya pṛcchate //
1.42.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
शृणु नारद वक्ष्यामि चेतिहासं पुरातनम् ।
भृगुणाभिहितं शास्त्रं भरद्वाजाय पृच्छते ॥
1.42.m: Sanandana said: / Listen, Nārada, I shall tell an ancient history / of the teaching proclaimed by Bhṛgu to Bharadvāja when he inquired.

1.42.s:
kailāsaśikhare dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānaṃ mahaujasam /
bhṛgumaharṣimāsīnaṃ bharadvājo 'nvapṛcchata //
1.42.d:
कैलासशिखरे दृष्ट्वा दीप्यमानं महौजसम् ।
भृगुमहर्षिमासीनं भरद्वाजो ऽन्वपृच्छत ॥
1.42.m: Having seen the great sage Bhṛgu, radiant and of great splendor, / seated upon the peak of Kailāsa, Bharadvāja questioned him:

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
kathaṃ jīvo vicarati nānāyoniṣu saṃtatam /
kathaṃ muktiśca saṃsārājjāyate tasya mānada //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
कथं जीवो विचरति नानायोनिषु संततम् ।
कथं मुक्तिश्च संसाराज्जायते तस्य मानद ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / How does the individual soul wander continuously in various wombs? / And how does liberation from saṃsāra arise for it, O honor-giver?

1.42.s:
yaśca nārāyaṇaḥ sraṣṭā svayaṃbhūrbhagavansvayam /
sevyasevakabhāvena vartete iti tau sadā //
1.42.d:
यश्च नारायणः स्रष्टा स्वयंभूर्भगवन्स्वयम् ।
सेव्यसेवकभावेन वर्तेते इति तौ सदा ॥
1.42.m: And the creator Nārāyaṇa, the self-born Lord himself— / do the two always exist in the relation of worshipped and worshipper?

1.42.s:
praviśanti laye sarve yamīśaṃ sacarācarāḥ /
lokānāṃ ramaṇaḥ so 'yaṃ nirguṇaśca nirañjanaḥ //
1.42.d:
प्रविशन्ति लये सर्वे यमीशं सचराचराः ।
लोकानां रमणः सो ऽयं निर्गुणश्च निरञ्जनः ॥
1.42.m: The Lord into whom all moving and unmoving beings enter at the dissolution, / he is the delight of the worlds, devoid of qualities and taintless.

1.42.s:
anīrdaśyo 'pratarkyaśca kathaṃ jñāyeta kairmune /
kathamenaṃ parātmānaṃ kālaśaktiduranvayam //
1.42.d:
अनीर्दश्यो ऽप्रतर्क्यश्च कथं ज्ञायेत कैर्मुने ।
कथमेनं परात्मानं कालशक्तिदुरन्वयम् ॥
1.42.m: Indescribable and unthinkable—how can he be known, and by whom, O sage? / How [can one know] this supreme Self, whose power of time is difficult to follow?

1.42.s:
atarkyacaritaṃ vedāḥ stuvanti kathamādarāt /
jīvo jīvatvamullaṅghya kathaṃ brahma samanvayāt //
1.42.d:
अतर्क्यचरितं वेदाः स्तुवन्ति कथमादरात् ।
जीवो जीवत्वमुल्लङ्घ्य कथं ब्रह्म समन्वयात् ॥
1.42.m: How do the Vedas devoutly praise him whose conduct is beyond thought? / Transcending individuality, how does the individual soul attain Brahman?

1.42.s:
etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ tanme brūhi kṛpānirgha /
evaṃ sa bhagavānpṛṣṭo bharadvājena saṃśayam //
1.42.d:
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि कृपानिर्घ ।
एवं स भगवान्पृष्टो भरद्वाजेन संशयम् ॥
1.42.m: I wish to hear this; tell it to me, O compassionate, sinless one! / When the Lord was thus asked about his doubt by Bharadvāja,

1.42.s:
maharṣirbrahmasaṃkāśaḥ sarvaṃ tasmai tato 'bravīt /
bhṛguruvāca
mānaso nāma yaḥ pūrvo viśruto ve maharṣibhiḥ //
1.42.d:
महर्षिर्ब्रह्मसंकाशः सर्वं तस्मै ततो ऽब्रवीत् ।
भृगुरुवाच
मानसो नाम यः पूर्वो विश्रुतो वे महर्षिभिः ॥
1.42.m: the great sage, resembling Brahmā, then told him everything. / Bhṛgu said: / He who was called 'the Mind-born' first, celebrated among the great sages,

1.42.s:
anādinidhano devastathā tebhyo 'jarāmaraḥ /
avyakta iti vikhyātaḥ śāśvato 'thākṣayo 'vyayaḥ //
1.42.d:
अनादिनिधनो देवस्तथा तेभ्यो ऽजरामरः ।
अव्यक्त इति विख्यातः शाश्वतो ऽथाक्षयो ऽव्ययः ॥
1.42.m: is the God without beginning or end, and unaging and immortal to them, / renowned as the unmanifest, eternal, imperishable, and immutable.

1.42.s:
yataḥ sṛṣṭāni bhūtāni jāyante ca mriyanti ca /
so 'mṛjatprathamaṃ devo mahāntaṃ nāma nāmataḥ //
1.42.d:
यतः सृष्टानि भूतानि जायन्ते च म्रियन्ति च ।
सो ऽमृजत्प्रथमं देवो महान्तं नाम नामतः ॥
1.42.m: From whom created beings are born and die, / that God first created that known by the name of Mahat.

1.42.s:
ākāśamiti vikhyātaṃ sarvabhūtadharaḥ prabhuḥ /
ākāśādabhavadvāri salilādagnimārutau //
1.42.d:
आकाशमिति विख्यातं सर्वभूतधरः प्रभुः ।
आकाशादभवद्वारि सलिलादग्निमारुतौ ॥
1.42.m: The Lord, bearer of all beings, [created] that renowned as space; / from space water arose, and from water fire and wind;

1.42.s:
agnimārutasaṃyogāttataḥ samabhavanmahī /
tatastejo mayaṃ divyaṃ padmaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ svayaṃbhuvā //
1.42.d:
अग्निमारुतसंयोगात्ततः समभवन्मही ।
ततस्तेजो मयं दिव्यं पद्मं सृष्टं स्वयंभुवा ॥
1.42.m: from the conjunction of fire and wind the earth then arose. / Then a divine lotus consisting of light was created by the self-born [Lord].

1.42.s:
tasmātpadmātsamabhavadvrahmā vedamayo vidhiḥ /
ahṝṅkāra iti khyātaḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtakṛt //
1.42.d:
तस्मात्पद्मात्समभवद्व्रह्मा वेदमयो विधिः ।
अहॄङ्कार इति ख्यातः सर्वभूतात्मभूतकृत् ॥
1.42.m: From that lotus arose Brahmā, the creator consisting of the Vedas, / known as the ego-sense, the maker of the beings who constitute all elements.

1.42.s:
brahmā vai sa mahātejā ya ete pañca dhātavaḥ /
śailāstasyāsthisaṃdhāstu medo masiṃ ca medinī //
1.42.d:
ब्रह्मा वै स महातेजा य एते पञ्च धातवः ।
शैलास्तस्यास्थिसंधास्तु मेदो मसिं च मेदिनी ॥
1.42.m: Brahmā indeed is of great splendor, from whom are these five elements: / the mountains are his bone-joints; the earth is his fat and flesh;

1.42.s:
samudrāstasya rudhiramākāśamudaraṃ tathā /
pavanaścaiva niśvāsastejo 'gnirnimnagāḥ śirāḥ //
1.42.d:
समुद्रास्तस्य रुधिरमाकाशमुदरं तथा ।
पवनश्चैव निश्वासस्तेजो ऽग्निर्निम्नगाः शिराः ॥
1.42.m: the oceans are his blood, and space is his belly; / the wind is his breath; fire is his energy; the rivers are his veins;

1.42.s:
agnīṣomau ca candrākārai nayane tasya viśrute /
nabhaścordhvaśirastasya kṣitiḥ padau bhujau diśaḥ //
1.42.d:
अग्नीषोमौ च चन्द्राकारै नयने तस्य विश्रुते ।
नभश्चोर्ध्वशिरस्तस्य क्षितिः पदौ भुजौ दिशः ॥
1.42.m: Agni and Soma, the sun and the moon, are renowned as his eyes; / the sky is his head above, the earth his feet, and the directions his arms.

1.42.s:
durvijñeyo hyacintyātmā siddhairapi na saṃśayaḥ /
sa eṣa bhagavānviṣṇurananta iti viśrutaḥ //
1.42.d:
दुर्विज्ञेयो ह्यचिन्त्यात्मा सिद्धैरपि न संशयः ।
स एष भगवान्विष्णुरनन्त इति विश्रुतः ॥
1.42.m: He is difficult to know and unthinkable in nature, even by perfected beings, without doubt. / This is the Lord Viṣṇu, celebrated as Ananta,

1.42.s:
sarvabhūtātmabhūtastho durvijñeyo 'kṛtātmabhiḥ /
ahṝṅkārasya yaḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtabhaghavāyavai /
tataḥ samabhavadviśvaṃ pṛṣṭo 'haṃ yadiha tvayā //
1.42.d:
सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थो दुर्विज्ञेयो ऽकृतात्मभिः ।
अहॄङ्कारस्य यः स्रष्टा सर्वभूतभघवायवै ।
ततः समभवद्विश्वं पृष्टो ऽहं यदिह त्वया ॥
1.42.m: dwelling in all beings as their inner self, difficult to know by the undisciplined. / He who is the creator of the ego-sense, the Lord of all beings, / from him the universe arose, concerning which I was asked here by you.

1.42.s:
bhagdvāja uvāca
gaganasya diśāṃ caiva bhūtalasvānilasya ca /
kānyatra parimāṇāni saṃśayaṃ chindhi tattvataḥ //
1.42.d:
भग्द्वाज उवाच
गगनस्य दिशां चैव भूतलस्वानिलस्य च ।
कान्यत्र परिमाणानि संशयं छिन्धि तत्त्वतः ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / Of the sky and the directions, of the surface of the earth and the wind, / what are the measurements here? Sever my doubt according to truth!

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
anantametadākāśaṃ siddhadaivatasovitam /
ramyaṃ nānāśrayākīrṇaṃ yasyāṃ to nādhigamyate //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
अनन्तमेतदाकाशं सिद्धदैवतसोवितम् ।
रम्यं नानाश्रयाकीर्णं यस्यां तो नाधिगम्यते ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / Infinite is this space, frequented by perfected beings and gods, / delightful, filled with various abodes, whose end is not reached.

1.42.s:
ūrdhvaṃ gateradhastāttu candrādityau na paśyataḥ /
tatra devāḥ svayaṃ dīptā bhāskarābhāgnivarcasaḥ //
1.42.d:
ऊर्ध्वं गतेरधस्तात्तु चन्द्रादित्यौ न पश्यतः ।
तत्र देवाः स्वयं दीप्ता भास्कराभाग्निवर्चसः ॥
1.42.m: Above the reach of their course, the sun and moon do not behold down below; / there the gods shine by themselves, possessing the splendor of the sun and fire.

1.42.s:
te cāpyantaṃ na paśyanti nabhasaḥ prathitaujasaḥ /
durgamatvādanantatvāditi me vada mānada //
1.42.d:
ते चाप्यन्तं न पश्यन्ति नभसः प्रथितौजसः ।
दुर्गमत्वादनन्तत्वादिति मे वद मानद ॥
1.42.m: And they too, though celebrated in splendor, do not see the end of the sky, / because of its impassability and infinitude—tell me this, O honor-giver!

1.42.s:
upariṣṭopariṣṭāttu pjvaladbhiḥ svayaṃprabhaghaiḥ /
niruddhametadākāśaṃ hyaprameyaṃ surairapi //
1.42.d:
उपरिष्टोपरिष्टात्तु प्ज्वलद्भिः स्वयंप्रभघैः ।
निरुद्धमेतदाकाशं ह्यप्रमेयं सुरैरपि ॥
1.42.m: Above and still above, it is occupied by blazing [deities] shining by themselves; / this space is indeed immeasurable even by the gods.

1.42.s:
prathivyante samudrāstu samudrānte tamaḥ smṛtam /
tamasoṃ'te jalaṃ prāhurjalasyānte 'gnireva ca //
1.42.d:
प्रथिव्यन्ते समुद्रास्तु समुद्रान्ते तमः स्मृतम् ।
तमसोंऽते जलं प्राहुर्जलस्यान्ते ऽग्निरेव च ॥
1.42.m: At the end of the earth are the oceans, and at the end of the oceans darkness is recorded; / at the end of darkness they speak of water, and at the end of water, fire indeed.

1.42.s:
rasātalānte salilaṃ jalānte pannagādhipāḥ /
tadante punarākāśamākāśānte punarjalam //
1.42.d:
रसातलान्ते सलिलं जलान्ते पन्नगाधिपाः ।
तदन्ते पुनराकाशमाकाशान्ते पुनर्जलम् ॥
1.42.m: At the end of Rasātala is water, and at the end of the water are the serpent lords; / at their end is space once more, and at the end of space is water again.

1.42.s:
evamantaṃ bhagavataḥ pramāṇaṃ salilasya ca /
agnimārutatoyebhyo durjñeyaṃ daivatairapi //
1.42.d:
एवमन्तं भगवतः प्रमाणं सलिलस्य च ।
अग्निमारुततोयेभ्यो दुर्ज्ञेयं दैवतैरपि ॥
1.42.m: In this way the limit and the measure of the blessed lord and of water / are difficult to comprehend even for the gods, because of fire, wind, and water.

1.42.s:
agnimārutatoyānāṃ varṇā kṣititalasya ca /
ākāśasadṛśā hyete bhidyante tattvadaśanāt //
1.42.d:
अग्निमारुततोयानां वर्णा क्षितितलस्य च ।
आकाशसदृशा ह्येते भिद्यन्ते तत्त्वदशनात् ॥
1.42.m: The colors of fire, wind, water, / and of the surface of the earth resemble space, but they are distinguished by perceiving truth.

1.42.s:
paṭhanti caiva munayaḥ śāstreṣu vividheṣu ca /
trailokye sāgare caiva pramāṇaṃ vihitaṃ yathā //
1.42.d:
पठन्ति चैव मुनयः शास्त्रेषु विविधेषु च ।
त्रैलोक्ये सागरे चैव प्रमाणं विहितं यथा ॥
1.42.m: Sages also recite in various treatises / the measure that has been laid down for the three worlds and for the ocean.

1.42.s:
adṛśyo yastvagamyo yaḥ kaḥ pramāṇa mudīrayet /
siddhānāṃ devatānāṃ ca parimītā yadā gatiḥ //
1.42.d:
अदृश्यो यस्त्वगम्यो यः कः प्रमाण मुदीरयेत् ।
सिद्धानां देवतानां च परिमीता यदा गतिः ॥
1.42.m: Who can declare the measure of that which is invisible and inaccessible, / when the reach of the perfected beings and the deities is limited?

1.42.s:
tadāgaṇyamanantasya nāmānanteti viśrutam /
nāmadheyānurupasya mānasasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.42.d:
तदागण्यमनन्तस्य नामानन्तेति विश्रुतम् ।
नामधेयानुरुपस्य मानसस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.42.m: Therefore, the name of the immeasurable, boundless one is famed as Ananta, / appropriate to the name of the great-souled mind-born lord.

1.42.s:
yadā tu divyaṃ yadrūpaṃ hrasate varddhate punaḥ /
ko 'nyastadvedituṃ śakyo yo 'pi syāttadvidho 'paraḥ //
1.42.d:
यदा तु दिव्यं यद्रूपं ह्रसते वर्द्धते पुनः ।
को ऽन्यस्तद्वेदितुं शक्यो यो ऽपि स्यात्तद्विधो ऽपरः ॥
1.42.m: When his divine form diminishes and then expands again, / who else could know that, even if another were similar to him?

1.42.s:
tataḥ puṣkarataḥ saṣṭaḥ sarvajño mūrtimānprabhuḥ /
brahmā dharmamayaḥ pūrvaḥ prajāpatiranuttamaḥ //
1.42.d:
ततः पुष्करतः सष्टः सर्वज्ञो मूर्तिमान्प्रभुः ।
ब्रह्मा धर्ममयः पूर्वः प्रजापतिरनुत्तमः ॥
1.42.m: Then from the lotus the omniscient, embodied Lord was created— / Brahmā, full of righteousness, the first, unsurpassed lord of creatures.

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
puṣkaro yadi saṃbhūto jyeṣṭaṃ bhavati puṣkaram /
brahmāṇaṃ pūrvajaṃ cāha bhavānsaṃdeha eva me //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
पुष्करो यदि संभूतो ज्येष्टं भवति पुष्करम् ।
ब्रह्माणं पूर्वजं चाह भवान्संदेह एव मे ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / If the lotus was created, the lotus must be the eldest, / and you say that Brahmā is the first-born; herein lies my doubt.

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
mānasasyeha yā mūrtirbrahmatvaṃ samupāgatā /
tasyāsanavidhānārthaṃ pṛthivī padmamucyate //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
मानसस्येह या मूर्तिर्ब्रह्मत्वं समुपागता ।
तस्यासनविधानार्थं पृथिवी पद्ममुच्यते ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / That form of the mind-born lord which attained the status of Brahmā here— / the earth is called the lotus to serve as a seat for him.

1.42.s:
karṇikā tasya padmasya merurgaganamucchritaḥ /
tasya madhye sthito lokānsṛjatyeṣa jagadvidhiḥ //
1.42.d:
कर्णिका तस्य पद्मस्य मेरुर्गगनमुच्छ्रितः ।
तस्य मध्ये स्थितो लोकान्सृजत्येष जगद्विधिः ॥
1.42.m: The pericarp of that lotus is Meru, elevated into the sky; / standing in its center, this ordainer of the universe creates the worlds.

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ kathaṃ sa sṛjati prabhuḥ /
merumadhye sthito brahmā tadvahirdvijasattama //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
प्रजाविसर्गं विविधं कथं स सृजति प्रभुः ।
मेरुमध्ये स्थितो ब्रह्मा तद्वहिर्द्विजसत्तम ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / How does that Lord, standing in the center of Meru, / create the diverse emission of creatures outside it, O best of the twice-born?

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
prajāvisargaṃ vividhaṃ mānaso manasāsṛjat /
saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ bhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
प्रजाविसर्गं विविधं मानसो मनसासृजत् ।
संरक्षणार्थं भूतानां सृष्टं प्रथमतो जलम् ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / The mind-born lord created the diverse emission of creatures with his mind. / First water was created for the protection of all beings,

1.42.s:
yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ prathamato jalam /
yatprāṇāḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ varddhante yena ca prajāḥ //
1.42.d:
यत्प्राणाः सर्वभूतानां सृष्टं प्रथमतो जलम् ।
यत्प्राणाः सर्वभूतानां वर्द्धन्ते येन च प्रजाः ॥
1.42.m: water was created first, which is the breath of life of all beings, / and by which creatures thrive.

1.42.s:
parityaktāśca na śyanti tenadaṃ sarvamāvṛttam /
pṛthivī parvatā meghā mūrtimantaśca ye pare /
sarvaṃ tadvāruṇaṃ jñeyamāpastastaṃbhire punaḥ //
1.42.d:
परित्यक्ताश्च न श्यन्ति तेनदं सर्वमावृत्तम् ।
पृथिवी पर्वता मेघा मूर्तिमन्तश्च ये परे ।
सर्वं तद्वारुणं ज्ञेयमापस्तस्तंभिरे पुनः ॥
1.42.m: Abandoned by it, they perish; by it all this is pervaded. / The earth, mountains, clouds, and whatever other embodied forms exist— / all that is to be known as watery; the waters then solidified.

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
kathaṃ salilamutpannaṃ kathaṃ caivāgnimārutau /
kathaṃ vā medinī sṛṣṭetyatra me saṃśayo mahān //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
कथं सलिलमुत्पन्नं कथं चैवाग्निमारुतौ ।
कथं वा मेदिनी सृष्टेत्यत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / How was water produced, and how were fire and wind? / And how was the earth created? In this I have great doubt.

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
brahmakalpe purā brahman brahmarṣīṇāṃ samāgame /
lokasaṃbhavasaṃdehaḥ samutpanno mahātmanām //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
ब्रह्मकल्पे पुरा ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मर्षीणां समागमे ।
लोकसंभवसंदेहः समुत्पन्नो महात्मनाम् ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / In a former Brahma-kalpa, O brahmin, at an assembly of brahmin seers, / a doubt concerning the origin of the world arose among those great-souled ones.

1.42.s:
te 'tiṣṭandhyānamālaṃbya maunamāsthāya niścalāḥ /
tyaktāhārāḥ sparddhamānā divyaṃ virṣaśataṃ dvijāḥ //
1.42.d:
ते ऽतिष्टन्ध्यानमालंब्य मौनमास्थाय निश्चलाः ।
त्यक्ताहाराः स्पर्द्धमाना दिव्यं विर्षशतं द्विजाः ॥
1.42.m: Resorting to meditation, observing silence, motionless, / abandoning food, and striving eagerly, those twice-born stayed for a hundred divine years.

1.42.s:
teṣāṃ brahmamayī vāṇī sarveṣāṃ śrotramāgamat /
divyā sarasvatī tatra saṃbabhūva nabhastalāt //
1.42.d:
तेषां ब्रह्ममयी वाणी सर्वेषां श्रोत्रमागमत् ।
दिव्या सरस्वती तत्र संबभूव नभस्तलात् ॥
1.42.m: A voice consisting of Brahman reached the ears of all of them; / the divine Sarasvatī appeared there from the vault of heaven:

1.42.s:
purāstimitamākāśamanantamacalopamam /
naṣṭacandrārkapavanaṃ prasuptamiva saṃbabhau //
1.42.d:
पुरास्तिमितमाकाशमनन्तमचलोपमम् ।
नष्टचन्द्रार्कपवनं प्रसुप्तमिव संबभौ ॥
1.42.m: ‘Formerly, space was motionless, boundless, like a mountain; / bereft of moon, sun, and wind, it appeared as though asleep.

1.42.s:
tataḥ salilamutpannaṃ tamasīva tamaḥ param /
tasmāñca salilotpīḍādudatiṣṭata mārutaḥ //
1.42.d:
ततः सलिलमुत्पन्नं तमसीव तमः परम् ।
तस्माञ्च सलिलोत्पीडादुदतिष्टत मारुतः ॥
1.42.m: Then water arose, like supreme darkness within darkness; / and from that compression of water, wind arose.

1.42.s:
yathābhavanamacchidraṃ niḥśabdamiva lakṣyate /
tañcābhasā pūryamāṇaṃ saśabdaṃ kurute 'nilaḥ //
1.42.d:
यथाभवनमच्छिद्रं निःशब्दमिव लक्ष्यते ।
तञ्चाभसा पूर्यमाणं सशब्दं कुरुते ऽनिलः ॥
1.42.m: Just as a hollow space without an opening appears to be silent, / but when being filled with water, the wind makes a sound,

1.42.s:
tathā salilasaṃruddhe nabhasoṃ'taṃ nirantare /
bhittvārṇavatalaṃ vāyuḥ samutpatati ghoṣavān //
1.42.d:
तथा सलिलसंरुद्धे नभसोंऽतं निरन्तरे ।
भित्त्वार्णवतलं वायुः समुत्पतति घोषवान् ॥
1.42.m: so, when the interior of space was enclosed by water without gap, / the wind, bursting through the floor of the ocean, rose up roaring.

1.42.s:
eṣu vā carate vāyurarṇavotpīḍasaṃbhavaḥ /
ākāśasthānamāsādya praśāntiṃ nādhigacchati //
1.42.d:
एषु वा चरते वायुरर्णवोत्पीडसंभवः ।
आकाशस्थानमासाद्य प्रशान्तिं नाधिगच्छति ॥
1.42.m: This wind, born from the pressure of the ocean, moves about; / having reached the realm of space, it finds no rest.

1.42.s:
tasminvāyvambusaṃgharṣe dīptatejā mahābalaḥ /
prādurāsīdūrdhvaśikhaḥ kṛtvā nistimiraṃ tamaḥ //
1.42.d:
तस्मिन्वाय्वम्बुसंघर्षे दीप्ततेजा महाबलः ।
प्रादुरासीदूर्ध्वशिखः कृत्वा निस्तिमिरं तमः ॥
1.42.m: In that friction between wind and water, [fire] of blazing brilliance and great power / appeared with upward flames, dispelling the gloom of darkness.

1.42.s:
agniḥ pavanasaṃyuktaḥ khaṃ samākṣipate jalam /
tadagnivāyusaṃparkāddhanatvamupapadyate //
1.42.d:
अग्निः पवनसंयुक्तः खं समाक्षिपते जलम् ।
तदग्निवायुसंपर्काद्धनत्वमुपपद्यते ॥
1.42.m: Fire, combined with wind, hurled water into the sky; / through contact with fire and wind, it attained solidity.

1.42.s:
tasyākāśaṃ nipatitaḥ snehāttiṣṭati yo 'paraḥ /
sa saṃghātatvamāpanno bhūmitvamanugacchati //
1.42.d:
तस्याकाशं निपतितः स्नेहात्तिष्टति यो ऽपरः ।
स संघातत्वमापन्नो भूमित्वमनुगच्छति ॥
1.42.m: That which fell from the sky and remained other[wise] through moisture, / having attained compactness, developed into the condition of earth.

1.42.s:
rasānāṃ sarvagandhānāṃ snehānāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā /
bhūmiryo niriyaṃ jñeyā yasyāḥ sarvaṃ prasūyate //
1.42.d:
रसानां सर्वगन्धानां स्नेहानां प्राणिनां तथा ।
भूमिर्यो निरियं ज्ञेया यस्याः सर्वं प्रसूयते ॥
1.42.m: The earth is to be known as the womb of tastes, of all fragrances, / of moistures, and likewise of living beings; from it everything is brought forth.’

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
ya ete dhātavaḥ pañca rakṣyā yānasṛjatprabhuḥ /
āvṛtā yairime lokā mahābhūtābhisaṃjñitaiḥ //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
य एते धातवः पञ्च रक्ष्या यानसृजत्प्रभुः ।
आवृता यैरिमे लोका महाभूताभिसंज्ञितैः ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / These five elements to be protected which the Lord created, / by which these worlds are enveloped, designated as the great elements—

1.42.s:
yadāsṛjatsahasrāṇi bhūtānāṃ sa mahāmatiḥ /
paścātteṣveva bhūtatvaṃ kathaṃ samupapadyate //
1.42.d:
यदासृजत्सहस्राणि भूतानां स महामतिः ।
पश्चात्तेष्वेव भूतत्वं कथं समुपपद्यते ॥
1.42.m: when that wise one created thousands of beings, / how thereafter does the nature of elements apply to them?

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
amitāni mahāṣṭāni yānti bhūtāni saṃbhavam /
atasteṣāṃ mahābhūtaśabdo 'yamupapadyate //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
अमितानि महाष्टानि यान्ति भूतानि संभवम् ।
अतस्तेषां महाभूतशब्दो ऽयमुपपद्यते ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / Countless beings of great magnitude come into existence; / therefore, the term ‘great element’ (mahābhūta) applies to them.

1.42.s:
ceṣṭā vāyuḥ khamākāśamūṣmāgniḥ salilaṃ dravaḥ /
pṛthivī cātra saṃghātaḥ śarīraṃ pāñcabhautikam //
1.42.d:
चेष्टा वायुः खमाकाशमूष्माग्निः सलिलं द्रवः ।
पृथिवी चात्र संघातः शरीरं पाञ्चभौतिकम् ॥
1.42.m: Movement is wind, space is void, heat is fire, fluid is water, / and earth is the solid mass here; the body consists of the five elements.

1.42.s:
ityataḥ pañcabhiryuktairyuktaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam /
śrotre ghrāṇo rasaḥ sparśo dṛṣṭiścendriyasaṃjñitāḥ //
1.42.d:
इत्यतः पञ्चभिर्युक्तैर्युक्तं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
श्रोत्रे घ्राणो रसः स्पर्शो दृष्टिश्चेन्द्रियसंज्ञिताः ॥
1.42.m: Thus, the stationary and the moving are endowed with the five elements; / the ear, nose, taste, touch, and sight are designated as the sense faculties.

1.42.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
pañcabhiryadi bhūtaistu yuktāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ /
sthāvarāṇāṃ na dṛśyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
1.42.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
पञ्चभिर्यदि भूतैस्तु युक्ताः स्थावरजङ्गमाः ।
स्थावराणां न दृश्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः ॥
1.42.m: Bharadvāja said: / If stationary and moving beings are endowed with the five elements, / the five elements are not perceived in the body of stationary beings.

1.42.s:
anūṣmaṇāmaceṣṭānāṃ ghanānāṃ caiva tattvataḥ /
vṛkṣāṇāṃ nopalabhyante śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
1.42.d:
अनूष्मणामचेष्टानां घनानां चैव तत्त्वतः ।
वृक्षाणां नोपलभ्यन्ते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः ॥
1.42.m: Since they lack heat and motion, and are completely solid, / the five elements are not observed in the bodies of trees.

1.42.s:
va śṛṇvanti na paśyanti na gandharasavedinaḥ /
na ca sparśaṃ hi jānanti te kathaṃ pañca dhātavaḥ //
1.42.d:
व शृण्वन्ति न पश्यन्ति न गन्धरसवेदिनः ।
न च स्पर्शं हि जानन्ति ते कथं पञ्च धातवः ॥
1.42.m: They do not hear, they do not see, nor do they perceive smell or taste; / nor indeed do they feel touch. How can they consist of the five elements?

1.42.s:
adravatvādanignitvādabhūmitvādavāyutaḥ /
ākāśasyāprameyatvādṛkṣāṇāṃ nāsti bhautikam //
1.42.d:
अद्रवत्वादनिग्नित्वादभूमित्वादवायुतः ।
आकाशस्याप्रमेयत्वादृक्षाणां नास्ति भौतिकम् ॥
1.42.m: Because they lack liquidity, fire, earth, and wind, / and because space cannot be grasped, trees have no elemental nature.

1.42.s:
bhṛguruvāca
ghanānāmapi vṛkṣaṇāmākāśo 'sti na saṃśayaḥ /
teṣāṃ puṣpapalavyaktirnityaṃ samupapadyate //
1.42.d:
भृगुरुवाच
घनानामपि वृक्षणामाकाशो ऽस्ति न संशयः ।
तेषां पुष्पपलव्यक्तिर्नित्यं समुपपद्यते ॥
1.42.m: Bhṛgu said: / Even in dense trees there is space, without doubt; / the emergence of their flowers and fruits occurs perpetually.

1.42.s:
ūṣmato mlāyate parṇaṃ tvakphalaṃ puṣpameva ca /
mlāyate śīryate cāpi sparśastenātra vidyate //
1.42.d:
ऊष्मतो म्लायते पर्णं त्वक्फलं पुष्पमेव च ।
म्लायते शीर्यते चापि स्पर्शस्तेनात्र विद्यते ॥
1.42.m: Leaf, bark, fruit, and flower wither from heat; / they wither and fall, and therefore touch exists in them.

1.42.s:
vāyyagnyaśaninirdhoṣaiḥ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ viśīryate /
śrotreṇa gṛhyate śabdastasmācchṛṇvanti pādapāḥ //
1.42.d:
वाय्यग्न्यशनिनिर्धोषैः फलं पुष्पं विशीर्यते ।
श्रोत्रेण गृह्यते शब्दस्तस्माच्छृण्वन्ति पादपाः ॥
1.42.m: By the sounds of wind, fire, and thunder, fruit and flower fall; / sound is grasped by the ear, therefore trees hear.

1.42.s:
vallī veṣṭayate vṛkṣānsarvataścaiva gacchati /
nahyadṛṣṭaśca mārgo 'sti tasmātpaśyanti pādapāḥ //
1.42.d:
वल्ली वेष्टयते वृक्षान्सर्वतश्चैव गच्छति ।
नह्यदृष्टश्च मार्गो ऽस्ति तस्मात्पश्यन्ति पादपाः ॥
1.42.m: A creeper twines around trees and moves in every direction; / and there is no path without sight, therefore trees see.

1.42.s:
puṇyāpuṇyaistathā gadhairdhūpaiśca vividhairapi /
arogāḥ puṣpitāḥ saṃti tasmājjighranti pādapāḥ //
1.42.d:
पुण्यापुण्यैस्तथा गधैर्धूपैश्च विविधैरपि ।
अरोगाः पुष्पिताः संति तस्माज्जिघ्रन्ति पादपाः ॥
1.42.m: By pleasant and unpleasant fragrances, as well as various incenses, / they become free of disease and bloom; therefore trees smell.

1.42.s:
sukhaduḥkhayorgrahaṇācchinnasya ca virohaṇāt /
jīvaṃ paśyāmi vṛkṣāṇāmacaitanyaṃ na vidyate //
1.42.d:
सुखदुःखयोर्ग्रहणाच्छिन्नस्य च विरोहणात् ।
जीवं पश्यामि वृक्षाणामचैतन्यं न विद्यते ॥
1.42.m: From their apprehension of pleasure and pain, and from the healing of what is cut, / I see life in trees; they are not devoid of consciousness.

1.42.s:
tena tajjalamādatte jarayatyagnimārutau /
āhārapariṇāmāñca snaho vṛddhiśca jāyate //
1.42.d:
तेन तज्जलमादत्ते जरयत्यग्निमारुतौ ।
आहारपरिणामाञ्च स्नहो वृद्धिश्च जायते ॥
1.42.m: Thereby it drinks that water, and digests it through fire and wind; / and from the digestion of food, moisture and growth are produced.

1.42.s:
jaṅgamānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ śarīre paṃñca dhātavaḥ /
pratyekaśaḥ prabhidyante yaiḥ śarīraṃ viceṣṭate //
1.42.d:
जङ्गमानां च सर्वेषां शरीरे पंञ्च धातवः ।
प्रत्येकशः प्रभिद्यन्ते यैः शरीरं विचेष्टते ॥
1.42.m: And in the bodies of all moving beings the five elements / are individually differentiated, by means of which the body moves.

1.42.s:
tvak ca māṃsaṃ tathāsthīni majjā snāyuśca pañcamaḥ /
ityetadiha saṃghātaṃ śarīre pṛthivīmaye //
1.42.d:
त्वक् च मांसं तथास्थीनि मज्जा स्नायुश्च पञ्चमः ।
इत्येतदिह संघातं शरीरे पृथिवीमये ॥
1.42.m: Skin, flesh, bones, marrow, and sinew as the fifth— / such is the aggregate here in the body made of earth.

1.42.s:
tejo hyagnistathā krodhaścakṣuruṣmā tathaiva ca /
agnirjanayate yañca pañcāgneyāḥ śarīriṇaḥ //
1.42.d:
तेजो ह्यग्निस्तथा क्रोधश्चक्षुरुष्मा तथैव च ।
अग्निर्जनयते यञ्च पञ्चाग्नेयाः शरीरिणः ॥
1.42.m: Splendour, fire, anger, the eye, and warmth, / and that which fire digests—these five in the embodied soul originate from fire.

1.42.s:
śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ tathāsyaṃ ca hṛdayaṃ koṣṭameva ca /
ākāśātprāṇināmete śarīre pañca dhātavaḥ //
1.42.d:
श्रोत्रं घ्राणं तथास्यं च हृदयं कोष्टमेव च ।
आकाशात्प्राणिनामेते शरीरे पञ्च धातवः ॥
1.42.m: The ear, the nose, and the mouth, the heart and the internal cavity— / these five elements in the body of living beings arise from space.

1.42.s:
śleṣmā pittamatha svedo vasā śoṇitameva ca /
ityāpaḥ pañcadhā dehe bhavanti prāṇināṃ sadā //
1.42.d:
श्लेष्मा पित्तमथ स्वेदो वसा शोणितमेव च ।
इत्यापः पञ्चधा देहे भवन्ति प्राणिनां सदा ॥
1.42.m: Phlegm, bile, sweat, fat, and blood— / in these five ways water is constantly present in the body of living beings.

1.42.s: prāṇātprīṇayate prāṇī vyānāvdyāyacchate tathā //
1.42.d: प्राणात्प्रीणयते प्राणी व्यानाव्द्यायच्छते तथा ॥
1.42.m: Through the prāṇa the creature is gratified, and through the vyāna it exerts itself.

1.42.s:
gacchatyapāno 'dhaścaiva samāno hyadyavasthitaḥ /
udānāducchvasitīti pañca (prati)bhadāñca bhāṣate /
ityete vāyavaḥ pañca veṣṭayantīhadehinam //
1.42.d:
गच्छत्यपानो ऽधश्चैव समानो ह्यद्यवस्थितः ।
उदानादुच्छ्वसितीति पञ्च (प्रति)भदाञ्च भाषते ।
इत्येते वायवः पञ्च वेष्टयन्तीहदेहिनम् ॥
1.42.m: The apāna moves downward, and the samāna resides within. / Through the udāna it exhales; thus are spoken the five distinctions. / In this way, these five vital airs envelop the embodied soul here.

1.42.s:
bhūmergandhaguṇānvetti rasaṃ cādūbhyaḥ śarīravān /
tasya gandhasya vakṣyāmi vistarābhihitānguṇān //
1.42.d:
भूमेर्गन्धगुणान्वेत्ति रसं चादूभ्यः शरीरवान् ।
तस्य गन्धस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तराभिहितान्गुणान् ॥
1.42.m: The embodied soul knows the quality of smell from earth, and taste from water. / I shall explain in detail the declared qualities of that smell:

1.42.s:
iṣṭaścānuṣṭagandhaśca madhuraḥ kaṭureva ca /
nirhārī saṃhataḥ snigdho rukṣo viśada eva ca //
1.42.d:
इष्टश्चानुष्टगन्धश्च मधुरः कटुरेव च ।
निर्हारी संहतः स्निग्धो रुक्षो विशद एव च ॥
1.42.m: Pleasant and unpleasant smell, sweet and pungent, / diffusive, compact, oily, dry, and pure.

1.42.s:
evaṃ navavidho jñeyaḥ pārthivo gandhavistaraḥ /
jyotiḥ paśyati cakṣurbhyaḥ sparśaṃ vetti ca vāyunā //
1.42.d:
एवं नवविधो ज्ञेयः पार्थिवो गन्धविस्तरः ।
ज्योतिः पश्यति चक्षुर्भ्यः स्पर्शं वेत्ति च वायुना ॥
1.42.m: Thus, the extension of earthy smell is known to be ninefold. / One sees fire through the eyes and knows touch by means of air.

1.42.s:
śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca rasaścāpi guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
rasajñānaṃ tu vakṣyāmi tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu //
1.42.d:
शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसश्चापि गुणाः स्मृताः ।
रसज्ञानं तु वक्ष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
1.42.m: Sound, touch, form, and taste are recorded as qualities. / But I shall explain the knowledge of taste; listen to that as I speak.

1.42.s:
raso bahuvidhaḥ prokta ṛṣibhiḥ prathitātmabhiḥ /
madhuro lavaṇastiktaḥ kaṣāyo 'mlaḥ kaṭustathā //
1.42.d:
रसो बहुविधः प्रोक्त ऋषिभिः प्रथितात्मभिः ।
मधुरो लवणस्तिक्तः कषायो ऽम्लः कटुस्तथा ॥
1.42.m: Taste has been declared to be manifold by celebrated sages: / sweet, salty, bitter, astringent, sour, and pungent.

1.42.s:
eṣa ṣaḍidhavistāro raso vārimayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaśca triguṇaṃ jyotirucyate //
1.42.d:
एष षडिधविस्तारो रसो वारिमयः स्मृतः ।
शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपश्च त्रिगुणं ज्योतिरुच्यते ॥
1.42.m: This sixfold expansion of taste is recorded as watery. / Fire is said to have three qualities: sound, touch, and form.

1.42.s:
jyotiḥ paśyati rūpāṇi rūpaṃ ca bahudhā smṛtam /
hrasvo dīrdhastathā sthūlaścaturasro 'ṇuvṛttavān //
1.42.d:
ज्योतिः पश्यति रूपाणि रूपं च बहुधा स्मृतम् ।
ह्रस्वो दीर्धस्तथा स्थूलश्चतुरस्रो ऽणुवृत्तवान् ॥
1.42.m: Fire perceives forms, and form is recorded as manifold: / short, long, gross, square, subtle, round,

1.42.s:
śuklaḥ kṛṣṇastathā rakto nīlaḥ pīto 'ruṇastathā /
kaṭhinaścikkaṇaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ picchilo mṛdu dāruṇaḥ //
1.42.d:
शुक्लः कृष्णस्तथा रक्तो नीलः पीतो ऽरुणस्तथा ।
कठिनश्चिक्कणः श्लक्ष्णः पिच्छिलो मृदु दारुणः ॥
1.42.m: white, black, red, blue, yellow, and reddish-brown, / hard, smooth, polished, slimy, soft, and rough.

1.42.s:
evaṃ ṣoḍaśavistāro jyotīrupaguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tatraikaguṇamākāśaṃ śabda ityeva tatsmṛtam //
1.42.d:
एवं षोडशविस्तारो ज्योतीरुपगुणः स्मृतः ।
तत्रैकगुणमाकाशं शब्द इत्येव तत्स्मृतम् ॥
1.42.m: Thus the quality of form belonging to fire is remembered as sixteenfold. / In that respect, space possesses a single quality; it is remembered as sound alone.

1.42.s:
tasya śabdasya vakṣyāmi vistaraṃ vividhātmakam /
ṣaḍjo ṛṣabhagāndhārau madhyamodhaivatastathā //
1.42.d:
तस्य शब्दस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तरं विविधात्मकम् ।
षड्जो ऋषभगान्धारौ मध्यमोधैवतस्तथा ॥
1.42.m: I shall explain the diverse extension of that sound: / ṣaḍja, ṛṣabha, gāndhāra, madhyama, and dhaivata,

1.42.s:
pañcamaścāpi vijñeyastathā cāpi niṣādavān /
eṣa saptavidhaḥ prokto guṇa ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.42.d:
पञ्चमश्चापि विज्ञेयस्तथा चापि निषादवान् ।
एष सप्तविधः प्रोक्तो गुण आकाशसंभवः ॥
1.42.m: pañcama should also be known, as well as niṣāda. / This quality arising from space is declared to be sevenfold.

1.42.s:
aiśvaryyeṇa tu sarvatra sthito 'pi payahādiṣu /
mṛdaṅgabherīśaṅkhānāṃ stanayitno rathasya ca //
1.42.d:
ऐश्वर्य्येण तु सर्वत्र स्थितो ऽपि पयहादिषु ।
मृदङ्गभेरीशङ्खानां स्तनयित्नो रथस्य च ॥
1.42.m: Yet by its sovereignty, though residing everywhere—in clouds and so on— / of mṛdaṅga-drums, bherī-drums, conches, thunder, and chariots,

1.42.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhākāraḥ śabda ākāśasaṃbhavaḥ /
vāyavyastu guṇaḥ sparśaḥ sparśaśca bahudhā smṛtaḥ //
1.42.d:
एवं बहुविधाकारः शब्द आकाशसंभवः ।
वायव्यस्तु गुणः स्पर्शः स्पर्शश्च बहुधा स्मृतः ॥
1.42.m: sound arising from space has such manifold forms. / Touch is the quality belonging to wind, and touch is recorded as manifold:

1.42.s:
uṣṇaḥ śītaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ snigdho viśada eva ca /
tathā kharo mṛduḥ ślakṣṇo lavurgurutaro 'pi ca //
1.42.d:
उष्णः शीतः सुखं दुःखं स्निग्धो विशद एव च ।
तथा खरो मृदुः श्लक्ष्णो लवुर्गुरुतरो ऽपि च ॥
1.42.m: hot, cold, pleasant, painful, oily, and pure, / likewise rough, soft, polished, light, and heavier.

1.42.s:
śabdasparśau tu vijñeyau dviguṇau vāyurityuta /
evamekādaśavidho vāyavyo guṇa ucyate //
1.42.d:
शब्दस्पर्शौ तु विज्ञेयौ द्विगुणौ वायुरित्युत ।
एवमेकादशविधो वायव्यो गुण उच्यते ॥
1.42.m: Sound and touch are to be known as having two qualities in air. / Thus the quality belonging to air is said to be elevenfold.

1.42.s:
ākāśajaṃ śabdamāhurebhirvāyuguṇaiḥ saha /
avyāhataiścetayate naveti viṣamā gatiḥ //
1.42.d:
आकाशजं शब्दमाहुरेभिर्वायुगुणैः सह ।
अव्याहतैश्चेतयते नवेति विषमा गतिः ॥
1.42.m: They declare that sound is born of space, along with these qualities of air. / With these unhindered, one perceives; its uneven course is ninefold.

1.42.s:
āpyāyante ca te nityaṃ dhātavastaistu dhātubhiḥ /
āpo 'gnirmāruścaiva nityaṃ jāgrati dehiṣu //
1.42.d:
आप्यायन्ते च ते नित्यं धातवस्तैस्तु धातुभिः ।
आपो ऽग्निर्मारुश्चैव नित्यं जाग्रति देहिषु ॥
1.42.m: And those bodily elements are constantly nourished by those very elements. / Water, fire, and wind remain perpetually awake within embodied beings.

1.42.s:
mūlamete śarīrasya vyāpya prāṇāniha sthitāḥ /
pārthivaṃ dhātumāsādya yathā ceṣṭayate balī //
1.42.d:
मूलमेते शरीरस्य व्याप्य प्राणानिह स्थिताः ।
पार्थिवं धातुमासाद्य यथा चेष्टयते बली ॥
1.42.m: These, the roots of the body, abide here pervading the vital breaths. / Having reached the earthy element, just as the powerful one moves about,

1.42.s:
śrito mūrddhānamagnistu śarīraṃ paripālayet /
prāṇo mūrddhani vāgnau ca vartamāno viceṣṭate //
1.42.d:
श्रितो मूर्द्धानमग्निस्तु शरीरं परिपालयेत् ।
प्राणो मूर्द्धनि वाग्नौ च वर्तमानो विचेष्टते ॥
1.42.m: so fire, residing in the head, protects the body. / Prāṇa, existing in the head and in the fire, is set in motion.

1.42.s:
sa jantuḥ sarvabhūtātmā puruṣaḥ sa sanātanaḥ /
mano buddhirahṝṅkāro bhūtāni viṣayaśca saḥ //
1.42.d:
स जन्तुः सर्वभूतात्मा पुरुषः स सनातनः ।
मनो बुद्धिरहॄङ्कारो भूतानि विषयश्च सः ॥
1.42.m: That creature is the Self of all beings, the eternal Puruṣa; / it is the mind, intellect, egoity, the elements, and the sense objects.

1.42.s:
evaṃ tviha sa sarvatra prāṇaistu paripālyate /
pṛṣṭatastu samānena svāṃ svāṃ gatimupāśritaḥ //
1.42.d:
एवं त्विह स सर्वत्र प्राणैस्तु परिपाल्यते ।
पृष्टतस्तु समानेन स्वां स्वां गतिमुपाश्रितः ॥
1.42.m: Thus indeed it is protected on all sides here by the vital breaths, / and from behind by samāna, each resorting to its own course.

1.42.s:
vastimūlaṃ gudaṃ caiva pāvakaṃ samupāśritaḥ /
vahanmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vāpyapānaḥ parivartate //
1.42.d:
वस्तिमूलं गुदं चैव पावकं समुपाश्रितः ।
वहन्मूत्रं पुरीषं वाप्यपानः परिवर्तते ॥
1.42.m: Resorting to the bladder-base, the anus, and the digestive fire, / bearing urine or faeces, the apāna revolves.

1.42.s:
prayatne karmaniyame yaca ekastriṣu vartate /
udāna iti taṃ prāhuradhyātmajñānakovidāḥ //
1.42.d:
प्रयत्ने कर्मनियमे यच एकस्त्रिषु वर्तते ।
उदान इति तं प्राहुरध्यात्मज्ञानकोविदाः ॥
1.42.m: That single one which operates across the three in effort and the restraint of action / is called udāna by those skilled in the knowledge of the supreme Self.

1.42.s:
saṃdhiṣvapi ca sarveṣu saṃniviṣṭastathānilaḥ /
śarīreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāna ityupadiśyate //
1.42.d:
संधिष्वपि च सर्वेषु संनिविष्टस्तथानिलः ।
शरीरेषु मनुष्याणां व्यान इत्युपदिश्यते ॥
1.42.m: The wind stationed within all the joints / in the bodies of human beings is taught to be vyāna.

1.42.s:
bāhuṣvagnistu vitataḥ samānena samīritaḥ /
rasānvāru doṣāṃśca vartayannati ceṣṭate //
1.42.d:
बाहुष्वग्निस्तु विततः समानेन समीरितः ।
रसान्वारु दोषांश्च वर्तयन्नति चेष्टते ॥
1.42.m: The fire extended in the arms, impelled by the samāna, / acts vigorously, circulating the bodily humours and the fluids of digested food.

1.42.s:
apānaprāṇayormadhye prāṇāpānasamīhitaḥ /
samanvitastvadhiṣṭānaṃ samyak pacati pāvakaḥ //
1.42.d:
अपानप्राणयोर्मध्ये प्राणापानसमीहितः ।
समन्वितस्त्वधिष्टानं सम्यक् पचति पावकः ॥
1.42.m: Between the apāna and prāṇa, impelled by prāṇa and apāna, / the fire, conjoined with its seat, digests [food] properly.

1.42.s:
āspaṃhi pāyuparyantamante syādgudasaṃjñite /
retastasmātprajāyante sarvasrotāṃsi dehinām //
1.42.d:
आस्पंहि पायुपर्यन्तमन्ते स्याद्गुदसंज्ञिते ।
रेतस्तस्मात्प्रजायन्ते सर्वस्रोतांसि देहिनाम् ॥
1.42.m: From the mouth up to the anus, which terminates in what is called the rectum, / from that, semen and all the bodily channels of embodied beings are produced.

1.42.s:
prāṇānāṃ sannipātāśca sannipātaḥ prajāyate /
ūṣmā cāgirīti jñeyo yo 'nnaṃ pacati dehinām //
1.42.d:
प्राणानां सन्निपाताश्च सन्निपातः प्रजायते ।
ऊष्मा चागिरीति ज्ञेयो यो ऽन्नं पचति देहिनाम् ॥
1.42.m: From the conjunction of the vital breaths, a union is produced; / and the heat is to be known as the fire that digests the food of embodied beings.

1.42.s:
agnivegavahaḥ prāṇo gudānte pratihanyate /
sa ūrdhvamāgamya punaḥ samutkṣipati pāvakam //
1.42.d:
अग्निवेगवहः प्राणो गुदान्ते प्रतिहन्यते ।
स ऊर्ध्वमागम्य पुनः समुत्क्षिपति पावकम् ॥
1.42.m: The prāṇa, bearing the force of the fire, is checked at the end of the rectum; / going upward again, it propels the fire.

1.42.s:
pakvāśayastvadho nābhyā ūrdhvamāmāśayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
nābhimūle śarīrasya sarve prāṇāśca saṃsthitāḥ //
1.42.d:
पक्वाशयस्त्वधो नाभ्या ऊर्ध्वमामाशयः स्मृतः ।
नाभिमूले शरीरस्य सर्वे प्राणाश्च संस्थिताः ॥
1.42.m: The seat of digested food is below the navel, and the stomach is recorded as above. / All the vital breaths are situated at the navel-root of the body.

1.42.s:
prasthitā hṛdayātsarve tiryagūrdhdamadhastathā /
vahṝntyannarasānnāḍyo daśaprāṇapracoditāḥ //
