1.42.d:
प्रस्थिता हृदयात्सर्वे तिर्यगूर्ध्दमधस्तथा ।
वहॄन्त्यन्नरसान्नाड्यो दशप्राणप्रचोदिताः ॥
1.42.m: Setting out from the heart transversely, upward, and downward, / the channels, impelled by the ten vital breaths, carry the essence of food.

1.42.s:
eṣa mārgo 'pi yogānāṃ yena gacchanti tatpadam /
jitaklamāḥ samā dhīrā mūrddhanyātmānamādadhan //
1.42.d:
एष मार्गो ऽपि योगानां येन गच्छन्ति तत्पदम् ।
जितक्लमाः समा धीरा मूर्द्धन्यात्मानमादधन् ॥
1.42.m: This is also the path of yogins by which they go to that abode; / their fatigue overcome, composed and steadfast, they place the self in the crown of the head.

1.42.s:
evaṃ sarveṣu vihitaprāṇāpāneṣu dehinām /
tasminsamidhyate nityamagniḥ sthālyāmivāhitaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bhṛgubharadvājasaṃvāde jagadutpattivarṇanaṃ nāma dvicatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.42.d:
एवं सर्वेषु विहितप्राणापानेषु देहिनाम् ।
तस्मिन्समिध्यते नित्यमग्निः स्थाल्यामिवाहितः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे भृगुभरद्वाजसंवादे जगदुत्पत्तिवर्णनं नाम द्विचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.42.m:
In this way, when all the prāṇa and apāna breaths are regulated in embodied beings, / the fire within is constantly kindled, like one placed in a pot.

Thus ends the forty-second chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Universe', in the dialogue between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja, in the second quarter of the first part in the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadi prāṇapatirvāyurvāyureva viceṣcate /
śvasityābhāṣate caiva tato jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यदि प्राणपतिर्वायुर्वायुरेव विचेष्चते ।
श्वसित्याभाषते चैव ततो जीवो निरर्थकः ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / If wind is the master of the breath, and wind alone moves, / breathes, and speaks, then the soul is useless.

1.43.s:
ya ūṣmabhāva āgneyo vahninaivopalabhyate /
agnirjarayate caitattadā jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
1.43.d:
य ऊष्मभाव आग्नेयो वह्निनैवोपलभ्यते ।
अग्निर्जरयते चैतत्तदा जीवो निरर्थकः ॥
1.43.m: If the condition of heat belongs to fire and is perceived by fire alone, / and fire digests this [food], then the soul is useless.

1.43.s:
jantoḥ pramniyamāṇasya jīvo naivopalabhyate /
vāyureva jahātyenamūṣmabhāvaśca naśyati //
1.43.d:
जन्तोः प्रम्नियमाणस्य जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते ।
वायुरेव जहात्येनमूष्मभावश्च नश्यति ॥
1.43.m: When a living creature is dying, the soul is not perceived at all; / it is wind alone that leaves it, and the state of heat perishes.

1.43.s:
yadi vāthumayo jīvaḥ saṃśleṣo yadi vāyunā /
vāyumañjalavatpaśyedgacchetsaha marudguṇaiḥ //
1.43.d:
यदि वाथुमयो जीवः संश्लेषो यदि वायुना ।
वायुमञ्जलवत्पश्येद्गच्छेत्सह मरुद्गुणैः ॥
1.43.m: If the soul consists of wind, or if it is joined with wind, / one would see the wind like water in the hollow of the hands, and it would depart along with the host of winds.

1.43.s:
saṃśleṣo yadi vā tena yadi tasmātpraṇaśyati /
mahārṇavavimuktatvādanyatsalilabhājanam //
1.43.d:
संश्लेषो यदि वा तेन यदि तस्मात्प्रणश्यति ।
महार्णवविमुक्तत्वादन्यत्सलिलभाजनम् ॥
1.43.m: Or if there is a union with it, and if it perishes from that, / [it would be] like another vessel of water released into the great ocean.

1.43.s:
kṛpe vā salilaṃ dadyātpradīpaṃ vā hutāśane /
kṣipraṃ praviśya naśyeta yathā naśyatyasau tathā //
1.43.d:
कृपे वा सलिलं दद्यात्प्रदीपं वा हुताशने ।
क्षिप्रं प्रविश्य नश्येत यथा नश्यत्यसौ तथा ॥
1.43.m: Or if one should pour water into a well, or [place] a lamp into fire, / having entered it quickly vanishes, just as that one would vanish.

1.43.s:
pañcadhāraṇake hyasmiñcharīre jīvitaṃ kṛtam /
yeṣāmanyatarābhāvāñcaturṇāṃ nāsti saṃśayaḥ //
1.43.d:
पञ्चधारणके ह्यस्मिञ्छरीरे जीवितं कृतम् ।
येषामन्यतराभावाञ्चतुर्णां नास्ति संशयः ॥
1.43.m: Life is established in this body which holds the five [elements]; / without doubt, in the absence of any one of them, the [other] four cannot remain.

1.43.s:
naśyantyāpo hyanāhārādvāyurucchvāsanigrahāt /
naśyate koṣṭabhedārthamagrirnaśyatyabhojanāt //
1.43.d:
नश्यन्त्यापो ह्यनाहाराद्वायुरुच्छ्वासनिग्रहात् ।
नश्यते कोष्टभेदार्थमग्रिर्नश्यत्यभोजनात् ॥
1.43.m: For water perishes from lack of food, and wind from the restraint of breathing; / from the rupturing of the internal cavity fire is destroyed, and it perishes from lack of eating.

1.43.s:
vyādhitraṇaparikleśairmedinī caiva śīryate /
pīḍite 'nyatare hyeṣāṃ saṃghāto yāti pañcatām //
1.43.d:
व्याधित्रणपरिक्लेशैर्मेदिनी चैव शीर्यते ।
पीडिते ऽन्यतरे ह्येषां संघातो याति पञ्चताम् ॥
1.43.m: And the earth decays through the distress of diseases and wounds. / Indeed, when any one of these is afflicted, the aggregate meets dissolution into the five elements.

1.43.s:
tasminpañcatvamāpanne jīvaḥ kimanudhāvati /
kiṃ khedayati vā jīvaḥ kiṃ śṛṇoti bravīti ca //
1.43.d:
तस्मिन्पञ्चत्वमापन्ने जीवः किमनुधावति ।
किं खेदयति वा जीवः किं शृणोति ब्रवीति च ॥
1.43.m: When that [body] has attained dissolution into the five elements, what does the living soul pursue? / Or what causes sorrow to the soul, what does it hear, and what does it speak?

1.43.s:
eṣā gauḥ paralokasthaṃ tārayiṣyatimāmiti /
yo dattvā mriyate jantuḥ sā gauḥ kaṃ tārayiṣyati //
1.43.d:
एषा गौः परलोकस्थं तारयिष्यतिमामिति ।
यो दत्त्वा म्रियते जन्तुः सा गौः कं तारयिष्यति ॥
1.43.m: "This cow will carry me across when I am in the other world"— / when a creature dies after giving [such a gift], whom will that cow carry across?

1.43.s:
gauścapratigrahītā ca dātā caiva samaṃ yadā /
ihaiva vilayaṃ yānti kutasteṣāṃ samāgamaḥ //
1.43.d:
गौश्चप्रतिग्रहीता च दाता चैव समं यदा ।
इहैव विलयं यान्ति कुतस्तेषां समागमः ॥
1.43.m: When the cow, the recipient, and the giver together / dissolve right here in this world, whence comes their reunion?

1.43.s:
vihagairupabhuktasya śailāgrātpatitasya ca /
agninā copayuktasya kutaḥ saṃjīvanaṃ punaḥ //
1.43.d:
विहगैरुपभुक्तस्य शैलाग्रात्पतितस्य च ।
अग्निना चोपयुक्तस्य कुतः संजीवनं पुनः ॥
1.43.m: For one eaten by birds, or fallen from a mountain peak, / or consumed by fire, whence can there be life again?

1.43.s:
chinnasya yadi vṛkṣasya na mūlaṃ pratirohati /
jīvanyasya pravartante mṛtaḥ kva punareṣyati //
1.43.d:
छिन्नस्य यदि वृक्षस्य न मूलं प्रतिरोहति ।
जीवन्यस्य प्रवर्तन्ते मृतः क्व पुनरेष्यति ॥
1.43.m: If a felled tree does not sprout again from its root, / [and only] others living proceed, where will the dead one go again?

1.43.s:
jīvamātraṃ purā sṛṣṭaṃ yadetatparivartate /
mṛtāḥ praṇaśyanti bījādbījaṃ praṇaśyati //
1.43.d:
जीवमात्रं पुरा सृष्टं यदेतत्परिवर्तते ।
मृताः प्रणश्यन्ति बीजाद्बीजं प्रणश्यति ॥
1.43.m: Only the living soul was created formerly, which revolves here; / the dead perish, and seed perishes from seed.

1.43.s:
iti me saṃśayo brahmanhṛdaye paridhāvati /
ta nivartaya sarvajña yatastvāmāśrito hyaham //
1.43.d:
इति मे संशयो ब्रह्मन्हृदये परिधावति ।
त निवर्तय सर्वज्ञ यतस्त्वामाश्रितो ह्यहम् ॥
1.43.m: Thus this doubt rushes through my heart, O sage; / dispel it, O omniscient one, for indeed I have taken refuge in you.

1.43.s:
sanandana uvāca
evaṃ pṛṣṭastadānena sa bhṛgarbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ /
punarāhu muniśreṣṭha tatsaṃdehanivṛttaye //
1.43.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
एवं पृष्टस्तदानेन स भृगर्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ।
पुनराहु मुनिश्रेष्ठ तत्संदेहनिवृत्तये ॥
1.43.m: Sanandana said: / Being thus questioned at that time by him, that Bhṛgu, son of Brahmā, / spoke again, O best of sages, for the dispelling of his doubt.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
na prāṇāḥ santi jīvasya dattasya ca kṛtasya ca /
yāti dehāntaraṃ prāṇī śarīraṃ tu viśīryate //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
न प्राणाः सन्ति जीवस्य दत्तस्य च कृतस्य च ।
याति देहान्तरं प्राणी शरीरं तु विशीर्यते ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / There are no vital breaths of the living soul, nor of what is given or done; / the living being goes to another body, but the physical body falls away.

1.43.s:
na śarīrāśrito jīvastasminnaṣṭe praṇaśyati /
samidhāmagnidagdhānāṃ yathāgrirddaśyate tathā //
1.43.d:
न शरीराश्रितो जीवस्तस्मिन्नष्टे प्रणश्यति ।
समिधामग्निदग्धानां यथाग्रिर्द्दश्यते तथा ॥
1.43.m: The living soul residing in the body does not perish when that is destroyed, / just as fire is seen when firewood is consumed by fire.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
agneryathā tasya nāśāttadvināśo na vidyate /
indhanasyopayogānte sa vāgnirnopalabhyate //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
अग्नेर्यथा तस्य नाशात्तद्विनाशो न विद्यते ।
इन्धनस्योपयोगान्ते स वाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / As with fire, there is no destruction of it through its destruction; / [yet] at the end of the consumption of fuel, that fire is not perceived.

1.43.s:
naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam /
gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate //
1.43.d:
नश्यतीत्येव जानामि शान्तमग्निमनिन्धनम् ।
गतिर्यस्य प्रमाणं वा संस्थानं वा न विद्यते ॥
1.43.m: I know only that fire, extinguished and devoid of fuel, perishes, / [a fire] whose movement, measure, or place of resting is not found.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
samidhāmupayogānte sa cāgnirnopalabhyate /
naśyatītyeva jānāmi śāntamagnimanindhanam //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
समिधामुपयोगान्ते स चाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते ।
नश्यतीत्येव जानामि शान्तमग्निमनिन्धनम् ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / At the end of the consumption of firewood, that fire is not perceived; / I know that the extinguished fire, devoid of fuel, [merely seems to] perish.

1.43.s:
gatiryasya pramāṇaṃ vā saṃsthānaṃ vā na vidyate /
samidhāmupayogānte yathāgnirnopalabhyate //
1.43.d:
गतिर्यस्य प्रमाणं वा संस्थानं वा न विद्यते ।
समिधामुपयोगान्ते यथाग्निर्नोपलभ्यते ॥
1.43.m: Its movement, measure, or place of resting is not found; / as fire is not perceived at the end of the consumption of firewood,

1.43.s:
ākāśānugatatvāddhi durgrāhyo hi nirāśrayaḥ /
tathā śarīrasaṃtyāge jīvo hyākāśavatsthitaḥ //
1.43.d:
आकाशानुगतत्वाद्धि दुर्ग्राह्यो हि निराश्रयः ।
तथा शरीरसंत्यागे जीवो ह्याकाशवत्स्थितः ॥
1.43.m: because it has merged into space, it is indeed difficult to grasp, being without support; / likewise, upon abandonment of the body, the living soul remains like space.

1.43.s:
na naśyate susūkṣmatvādyathā jyotirna saṃśayaḥ /
prāṇāndhārayate hyagniḥ sa jīva upadhāryatām //
1.43.d:
न नश्यते सुसूक्ष्मत्वाद्यथा ज्योतिर्न संशयः ।
प्राणान्धारयते ह्यग्निः स जीव उपधार्यताम् ॥
1.43.m: It does not perish because of its extreme subtlety, just like light; there is no doubt. / Fire indeed sustains the vital breaths; let that be understood as the living soul.

1.43.s:
vāyusaṃdhāraṇo hyagnirnaśyatyucchvāsanigrahāt /
tasminnaṣṭe śarīrāgnau tato dehamacetanam //
1.43.d:
वायुसंधारणो ह्यग्निर्नश्यत्युच्छ्वासनिग्रहात् ।
तस्मिन्नष्टे शरीराग्नौ ततो देहमचेतनम् ॥
1.43.m: Fire is sustained by wind, and perishes through the cessation of breath; / when that bodily fire is destroyed, then the body is unconscious.

1.43.s:
patitaṃ yāti bhūmitvamayanaṃ tasya hi kṣitiḥ /
jagamānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca //
1.43.d:
पतितं याति भूमित्वमयनं तस्य हि क्षितिः ।
जगमानां हि सर्वेषां स्थावराणां तथैव च ॥
1.43.m: Fallen, it turns into earth, for the earth is its destination; / indeed of all moving and likewise of unmoving beings.

1.43.s:
ākāśaṃ pavano 'nveti jyotistamanugacchati /
teṣāṃ trayāṇāmekatvādvayaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭitam //
1.43.d:
आकाशं पवनो ऽन्वेति ज्योतिस्तमनुगच्छति ।
तेषां त्रयाणामेकत्वाद्वयं भूमौ प्रतिष्टितम् ॥
1.43.m: Wind follows space, and light follows it; / because of the oneness of those three, the body is established on earth.

1.43.s:
yatra khaṃ tatra pavanastatrāgniryatra mārutaḥ /
amūrtayaste vijñeyā mūrtimantaḥ śarīriṇaḥ //
1.43.d:
यत्र खं तत्र पवनस्तत्राग्निर्यत्र मारुतः ।
अमूर्तयस्ते विज्ञेया मूर्तिमन्तः शरीरिणः ॥
1.43.m: Where there is space, there is wind; where there is wind, there is fire; / they are to be known as formless, while embodied beings have form.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadyagnimārutau bhūmiḥ khamāpaśca śarīriṣu /
jīvaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇastatretyetadācakṣva me 'nagha //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यद्यग्निमारुतौ भूमिः खमापश्च शरीरिषु ।
जीवः किंलक्षणस्तत्रेत्येतदाचक्ष्व मे ऽनघ ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / If fire and wind, earth, space, and water are in embodied beings, / then what is the characteristic of the living soul there? Tell me this, O sinless one!

1.43.s:
pañcātmake pañcaratau pañcavijñānasaṃjñake /
śarīre prāṇināṃ jīvaṃ vettubhicchāmi yādṛśam //
1.43.d:
पञ्चात्मके पञ्चरतौ पञ्चविज्ञानसंज्ञके ।
शरीरे प्राणिनां जीवं वेत्तुभिच्छामि यादृशम् ॥
1.43.m: Consisting of the five [elements], delighting in the five, named for fivefold perception: / in such a body of living beings, I wish to know of what sort the living soul is.

1.43.s:
māṃsaśoṇitasaṃghāte medaḥsnāyvasthisaṃcaye /
bhidyamāne śarīre tu jīvo naivopalabhyate //
1.43.d:
मांसशोणितसंघाते मेदःस्नाय्वस्थिसंचये ।
भिद्यमाने शरीरे तु जीवो नैवोपलभ्यते ॥
1.43.m: In an aggregate of flesh and blood, a heap of fat, sinews, and bones, / when the body is dissected, the living soul is not found at all.

1.43.s:
yadyajīvaśarīraṃ tu pañcabhūtasamanvitam /
śarīre mānase duḥkha kastāṃ vedayate rujam //
1.43.d:
यद्यजीवशरीरं तु पञ्चभूतसमन्वितम् ।
शरीरे मानसे दुःख कस्तां वेदयते रुजम् ॥
1.43.m: If the body endowed with the five elements were without a living soul, / then in bodily and mental pain, who experiences that ache?

1.43.s:
śṛṇoti kathitaṃ jīvaḥ karṇābhyāṃna śṛṇoti tat /
maharṣe manasi vyagre tasmājjīvo nirarthakaḥ //
1.43.d:
शृणोति कथितं जीवः कर्णाभ्यांन शृणोति तत् ।
महर्षे मनसि व्यग्रे तस्माज्जीवो निरर्थकः ॥
1.43.m: The living soul hears what is spoken; it does not hear it through the ears / when the mind is agitated, O great sage; therefore, is the living soul useless?

1.43.s:
sarve paśyanti yadṛśyaṃ manoyuktena cakṣuṣā /
manasi vyākule cakṣuḥ paśyannapi na paśyati //
1.43.d:
सर्वे पश्यन्ति यदृश्यं मनोयुक्तेन चक्षुषा ।
मनसि व्याकुले चक्षुः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति ॥
1.43.m: All see an object of sight with the eye joined with the mind; / when the mind is distracted, the eye, even though looking, does not see.

1.43.s:
na paśyati na cāghrāti na śṛṇoti na bhāṣate /
na ca smarśamasau vetti nidrāvaśagataḥ punaḥ //
1.43.d:
न पश्यति न चाघ्राति न शृणोति न भाषते ।
न च स्मर्शमसौ वेत्ति निद्रावशगतः पुनः ॥
1.43.m: It does not see, nor does it smell, nor does it hear, nor does it speak; / and fallen under the sway of sleep, it does not perceive touch again.

1.43.s:
hṛṣyati kruddhyate ko 'tra śocatyudvijate ca kaḥ /
icchati dhyāyati dveṣṭi vākyaṃ vācayate ca kaḥ //
1.43.d:
हृष्यति क्रुद्ध्यते को ऽत्र शोचत्युद्विजते च कः ।
इच्छति ध्यायति द्वेष्टि वाक्यं वाचयते च कः ॥
1.43.m: Who rejoices here, who grows angry, who grieves, and who becomes agitated? / Who desires, meditates, hates, and utters speech?

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
taṃ pañcasādhāraṇamatra kiñciccharīrameko vahateṃ'tarātmā /
sa vetti gandhāṃśca rasāñchutīśca sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca guṇāṃśca ye 'lye //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
तं पञ्चसाधारणमत्र किञ्चिच्छरीरमेको वहतेंऽतरात्मा ।
स वेत्ति गन्धांश्च रसाञ्छुतीश्च स्पर्शं च रूपं च गुणांश्च ये ऽल्ये ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / A single inner Self bears that body here, which is the common property of the five [elements]; / it perceives smells, tastes, sounds, touch, form, and whatever other qualities there are.

1.43.s:
pañcātmake pañcaguṇapradarśī sa sarvagātrānugatoṃ'tarātmā /
saveti duḥkhāni sukhāni cātra tadviprayogāttu na vetti deham //
1.43.d:
पञ्चात्मके पञ्चगुणप्रदर्शी स सर्वगात्रानुगतोंऽतरात्मा ।
सवेति दुःखानि सुखानि चात्र तद्विप्रयोगात्तु न वेत्ति देहम् ॥
1.43.m: Discerning the five qualities in that which consists of the five [elements], that inner Self permeates all the limbs; / it experiences pleasures and pains here, but upon separation from it, [the person] does not know the body.

1.43.s:
yadā na rūpaṃ na sparśo noṣyabhavaśca pāvake /
tadā śānte śarīrāgnau dehatyāgena naśyati //
1.43.d:
यदा न रूपं न स्पर्शो नोष्यभवश्च पावके ।
तदा शान्ते शरीराग्नौ देहत्यागेन नश्यति ॥
1.43.m: When there is no form, no touch, and no presence of heat in fire, / then, when the bodily fire is extinguished, it departs through abandonment of the body.

1.43.s:
āpomayamidaṃ sarvamāpomūrtiḥ śarīriṇām /
tatrātmā mānaso brahmā sarvabhūteṣu lokakṛt //
1.43.d:
आपोमयमिदं सर्वमापोमूर्तिः शरीरिणाम् ।
तत्रात्मा मानसो ब्रह्मा सर्वभूतेषु लोककृत् ॥
1.43.m: All this is composed of water; water is the form of embodied beings; / there the mental Self, Brahmā, is the world-maker in all beings.

1.43.s:
ātmānaṃ taṃ vijānīhi sarvalokahitātmakam /
tasminyaḥ saṃśrito dehe hyabbinduriva puṣkare //
1.43.d:
आत्मानं तं विजानीहि सर्वलोकहितात्मकम् ।
तस्मिन्यः संश्रितो देहे ह्यब्बिन्दुरिव पुष्करे ॥
1.43.m: Know that Self, whose nature is the welfare of all the worlds; / that which resides in that body is like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.

1.43.s:
kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ lokahitātmakam /
tamorajaśca sattvaṃ ca viddhi jīvaguṇānimām //
1.43.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञं तं विजानीहि नित्यं लोकहितात्मकम् ।
तमोरजश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि जीवगुणानिमाम् ॥
1.43.m: Know it to be the knower of the field, eternally having the welfare of the world as its nature; / know darkness, passion, and goodness to be these qualities of the living soul.

1.43.s:
acetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam /
ataḥ paraṃ kṣetravido vadanti prāvartayadyo bhuvanāni sapta //
1.43.d:
अचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति स चेष्टते चेष्टयते च सर्वम् ।
अतः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति प्रावर्तयद्यो भुवनानि सप्त ॥
1.43.m: They call the quality of the living soul insentient; it moves and sets everything in motion; / higher than this, the knowers of the field speak of that which set the seven worlds in motion.

1.43.s:
na jīvanāśo 'sti hi dehabhede mithyaitadāhurmuna ityabuddhāḥ /
jīvastu dehāntaritaḥ prayāti daśārddhatastasya śarīrabhedaḥ //
1.43.d:
न जीवनाशो ऽस्ति हि देहभेदे मिथ्यैतदाहुर्मुन इत्यबुद्धाः ।
जीवस्तु देहान्तरितः प्रयाति दशार्द्धतस्तस्य शरीरभेदः ॥
1.43.m: There is no destruction of the living soul upon the dissolution of the body; fools who are not wise say this falsely; / but the living soul departs, separated from the body; the dissolution of its body is from the five [elements].

1.43.s:
evaṃ bhūteṣu sarveṣu gūḍhaścarati sarvadā /
dṛśyate tvagryā budhyāsūkṣmayā tattvadarśibhiḥ //
1.43.d:
एवं भूतेषु सर्वेषु गूढश्चरति सर्वदा ।
दृश्यते त्वग्र्या बुध्यासूक्ष्मया तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
1.43.m: Thus it moves, hidden in all beings at all times; / but it is seen by the seers of truth with a subtle, supreme intellect.

1.43.s:
taṃ pūrvāpararātreṣu yuñjānaḥ satataṃ budhaḥ /
labdhāhāro viśuddhātmā paśyatyātmānamātmani //
1.43.d:
तं पूर्वापररात्रेषु युञ्जानः सततं बुधः ।
लब्धाहारो विशुद्धात्मा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि ॥
1.43.m: The wise one who constantly yokes it in the earlier and later parts of the night, / having taken food, with a purified self, sees the Self in the self.

1.43.s:
cittasya hi prasādena hitvā karma śubhāśubham /
prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukhamānantyamaśnute //
1.43.d:
चित्तस्य हि प्रसादेन हित्वा कर्म शुभाशुभम् ।
प्रसन्नात्मात्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
1.43.m: Through the serenity of the mind, having abandoned auspicious and inauspicious action, / with a serene self, abiding in the Self, he attains endless bliss.

1.43.s:
mānaso 'gniḥ śarīreṣu jīva ityabhidhīyate /
sṛṣṭiḥ prajāpatereṣā bhūtādhyātmaviniścaye //
1.43.d:
मानसो ऽग्निः शरीरेषु जीव इत्यभिधीयते ।
सृष्टिः प्रजापतेरेषा भूताध्यात्मविनिश्चये ॥
1.43.m: The fire belonging to the mind in bodies is called the living soul; / this is the creation of Prajāpati in the ascertainment of the elements and the Self.

1.43.s:
asṛjadbrāhmaṇāneva pūrvaṃ brahmā prajāpatiḥ /
ātmatejo 'bhinir vṛttānbhāskarāgnisamaprabhān //
1.43.d:
असृजद्ब्राह्मणानेव पूर्वं ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः ।
आत्मतेजो ऽभिनिर् वृत्तान्भास्कराग्निसमप्रभान् ॥
1.43.m: First Prajāpati Brahmā created only Brāhmaṇas, / brought forth from his own splendor, equal in radiance to the sun and fire.

1.43.s:
tataḥ satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca tathā brahma ca śāśvatam /
ācāraṃ caiva śaucaṃ ca svargāya vidadhe prabhuḥ //
1.43.d:
ततः सत्यं च धर्मं च तथा ब्रह्म च शाश्वतम् ।
आचारं चैव शौचं च स्वर्गाय विदधे प्रभुः ॥
1.43.m: Then the Lord ordained truth, righteousness, eternal sacred wisdom, / good conduct, and purity for the sake of heaven.

1.43.s:
devadāna vagandharvā daityāsuramahoragāḥ /
yakṣarākṣasanāgāśca piśācā manujāstathā //
1.43.d:
देवदान वगन्धर्वा दैत्यासुरमहोरगाः ।
यक्षराक्षसनागाश्च पिशाचा मनुजास्तथा ॥
1.43.m: Gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Daityas, Asuras, great serpents, / Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Nāgas, Piśācas, and humans—

1.43.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāṇāmasitastathā /
bharadvāja uvāca
cāturvarṇyasya varṇena yadi varṇo vibhidyate //
1.43.d:
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्राणामसितस्तथा ।
भरद्वाज उवाच
चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य वर्णेन यदि वर्णो विभिद्यते ॥
1.43.m: Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and likewise the dark [class] of Śūdras. / Bharadvāja said: / If caste is distinguished by the color of the four castes,

1.43.s:
svedamūtrapurīṣāṇi śleṣmā pitta saśoṇitam /
tvantaḥ kṣarati sarveṣāṃ kasmādvarṇo vibhajyate //
1.43.d:
स्वेदमूत्रपुरीषाणि श्लेष्मा पित्त सशोणितम् ।
त्वन्तः क्षरति सर्वेषां कस्माद्वर्णो विभज्यते ॥
1.43.m: sweat, urine, feces, phlegm, bile, along with blood, / flow within all of them, why then is caste divided?

1.43.s:
jaṅgamānāmasaṃkhyeyāḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jātayaḥ /
teṣāṃ vividhavarṇānāṃ kuto varṇaviniścayaḥ //
1.43.d:
जङ्गमानामसंख्येयाः स्थावराणां च जातयः ।
तेषां विविधवर्णानां कुतो वर्णविनिश्चयः ॥
1.43.m: Countless are the species of moving and unmoving beings; / of those possessing various colors, whence is the determination of caste?

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
na viśeṣo 'sti varṇānāṃ sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ jagat /
brahmaṇā pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ hi karmaṇā varṇatāṃ gatam //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
न विशेषो ऽस्ति वर्णानां सर्वं ब्रह्ममयं जगत् ।
ब्रह्मणा पूर्वसृष्टं हि कर्मणा वर्णतां गतम् ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / There is no distinction among the castes; the entire world consists of Brahman; / for, originally created by Brahmā, it attained the status of caste through action.

1.43.s:
kāmabhogāḥ priyāstīkṣṇāḥ krodhatāpriyasāhasāḥ /
tyaktasvakarmaraktāṅgāste dvijāḥ kṣatratāṃ gatāḥ //
1.43.d:
कामभोगाः प्रियास्तीक्ष्णाः क्रोधताप्रियसाहसाः ।
त्यक्तस्वकर्मरक्ताङ्गास्ते द्विजाः क्षत्रतां गताः ॥
1.43.m: Those twice-born who loved desires and sensual pleasures, who were fierce, fond of anger and daring deeds, / and who abandoned their own duties, red-limbed, attained the status of Kṣatriyas.

1.43.s:
gobhyo vṛttiṃ samāsthāya pītāḥ kṛṣyupajīvinaḥ /
svadharṃmannānutiṣṭanti te dvijā vaiśyatāṃ gatāḥ //
1.43.d:
गोभ्यो वृत्तिं समास्थाय पीताः कृष्युपजीविनः ।
स्वधर्ंमन्नानुतिष्टन्ति ते द्विजा वैश्यतां गताः ॥
1.43.m: Those twice-born who, adopting their livelihood from cows, becoming yellow [in complexion], subsist on agriculture / and do not adhere to their own duty, have attained the status of Vaiśyas.

1.43.s:
rhisānṛtaparā lubdhāḥ sarvakarmopajīvinaḥ /
kṛṣṇāḥ śaucapāribhrāṣṭāste dvijāḥ śūdratāṃ gatāḥ //
1.43.d:
र्हिसानृतपरा लुब्धाः सर्वकर्मोपजीविनः ।
कृष्णाः शौचपारिभ्राष्टास्ते द्विजाः शूद्रतां गताः ॥
1.43.m: Those twice-born who are devoted to violence and falsehood, greedy, subsisting on all kinds of occupations, / black [in complexion], and fallen from ritual purity, have attained the status of Śūdras.

1.43.s:
ityetaiḥ karmabhirvyāptā dvijā varṇāntaraṃ gatāḥ /
brāhmaṇā dharmatantrasthāstapasteṣāṃ na naśyati //
1.43.d:
इत्येतैः कर्मभिर्व्याप्ता द्विजा वर्णान्तरं गताः ।
ब्राह्मणा धर्मतन्त्रस्थास्तपस्तेषां न नश्यति ॥
1.43.m: Occupied with these actions, twice-born men have entered different classes. / For Brahmins established in the system of dharma, their ascetic power does not perish.

1.43.s:
brahma dhārayatāṃ nityaṃ vratāni niyabhāṃstathā /
brahma caiva purā sṛṣṭaṃ yena jānanti tadvidaḥ //
1.43.d:
ब्रह्म धारयतां नित्यं व्रतानि नियभांस्तथा ।
ब्रह्म चैव पुरा सृष्टं येन जानन्ति तद्विदः ॥
1.43.m: For those who constantly uphold Brahman, vows, and observances, / Brahman was created of old, by which those who know it perceive [the truth].

1.43.s:
teṣāṃ bahuvidhāstvanyāstatra tatra dvijātayaḥ /
piśācajā rākṣasāḥ pretā vividhā mlecchajātayaḥ /
sā sṛṣṭirmānasī nāma dharmatantraparāyaṇā //
1.43.d:
तेषां बहुविधास्त्वन्यास्तत्र तत्र द्विजातयः ।
पिशाचजा राक्षसाः प्रेता विविधा म्लेच्छजातयः ।
सा सृष्टिर्मानसी नाम धर्मतन्त्रपरायणा ॥
1.43.m: Various other twice-born groups appeared here and there among them— / Piśācas, Rākṣasas, Pretas, and diverse kinds of Mlecchas. / That was called the mind-born creation, devoted to the order of dharma.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
brāhmaṇaḥ kena bhavati kṣatriyo vā dvijottama /
vaiśyaḥ śūdraśca viprarṣe tadbrūhi vadatāṃ vara //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
ब्राह्मणः केन भवति क्षत्रियो वा द्विजोत्तम ।
वैश्यः शूद्रश्च विप्रर्षे तद्ब्रूहि वदतां वर ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / By what does one become a Brahmin or a Kṣatriya, O best of the twice-born? / And how a Vaiśya and a Śūdra, O Brahmin sage? Tell that, O best among speakers.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
jātakarmādibhiryastu saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ śuciḥ /
vedādhyayanasaṃpanno brahmakarmasvavasthitaḥ //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
जातकर्मादिभिर्यस्तु संस्कारैः संस्कृतः शुचिः ।
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नो ब्रह्मकर्मस्ववस्थितः ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / But he who is purified by the rites of passage beginning with the birth-ceremony, who is clean, / endowed with the study of the Vedas, and established in the duties of Brahman;

1.43.s:
śaucācārasthitaḥ samyagvidyābhyāsī gurupriyaḥ /
nityavratī satyaparaḥ sa vai brāhmaṇa ucyate //
1.43.d:
शौचाचारस्थितः सम्यग्विद्याभ्यासी गुरुप्रियः ।
नित्यव्रती सत्यपरः स वै ब्राह्मण उच्यते ॥
1.43.m: Established properly in ritual purity and conduct, engaged in learning, dear to his teacher, / constant in vows, and devoted to truth—he indeed is called a Brahmin.

1.43.s:
satyaṃ dānamatho 'droha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṛpā ghṛṇā /
tapasyāṃ dṛśyate yatra sa brāhmaṇa iti smṛtaḥ //
1.43.d:
सत्यं दानमथो ऽद्रोह आनृशंस्यं कृपा घृणा ।
तपस्यां दृश्यते यत्र स ब्राह्मण इति स्मृतः ॥
1.43.m: Truth, charity, freedom from malice, harmlessness, compassion, tenderness, / and asceticism—in whom these are seen, he is recorded as a Brahmin.

1.43.s:
kṣatrajaṃ sevate karma vedādhyayanasaṃgataḥ /
dānādānaratiryastu sa vai kṣatriya ucyate //
1.43.d:
क्षत्रजं सेवते कर्म वेदाध्ययनसंगतः ।
दानादानरतिर्यस्तु स वै क्षत्रिय उच्यते ॥
1.43.m: He who pursues the occupation arising from the martial order, engaged in the study of the Vedas, / and delights in giving and receiving—he indeed is called a Kṣatriya.

1.43.s:
viśatyāśu paśubhyaśca kṛṣyādānaratiḥ śuciḥ /
vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sa vaiśya iti saṃjñitaḥ //
1.43.d:
विशत्याशु पशुभ्यश्च कृष्यादानरतिः शुचिः ।
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नः स वैश्य इति संज्ञितः ॥
1.43.m: He who quickly turns to cattle, delights in agriculture and commerce, is pure, / and is endowed with Vedic study—he is termed a Vaiśya.

1.43.s:
sarvaghabhakṣaratirnityaṃ sarvakarmakaro 'śuciḥ /
tyaktavedastvanācāraḥ sa vai śūdra iti smṛtaḥ //
1.43.d:
सर्वघभक्षरतिर्नित्यं सर्वकर्मकरो ऽशुचिः ।
त्यक्तवेदस्त्वनाचारः स वै शूद्र इति स्मृतः ॥
1.43.m: He who habitually delights in eating all foods, performs all types of work, is impure, / has abandoned the Vedas, and is without right conduct—he indeed is recorded as a Śūdra.

1.43.s:
śūdre caitadbhavellakṣma dvije tacca na vidyate /
na vai śūdro bhavecchūdro brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇo na ca //
1.43.d:
शूद्रे चैतद्भवेल्लक्ष्म द्विजे तच्च न विद्यते ।
न वै शूद्रो भवेच्छूद्रो ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणो न च ॥
1.43.m: If this characteristic exists in a Śūdra and is absent in a twice-born man, / then a Śūdra would not be a Śūdra, nor would a Brahmin be a Brahmin.

1.43.s:
sarvopāyaistu lobhasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ /
etatpavitraṃ jñānānāṃ tathā caivātmasaṃyamaḥ //
1.43.d:
सर्वोपायैस्तु लोभस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः ।
एतत्पवित्रं ज्ञानानां तथा चैवात्मसंयमः ॥
1.43.m: The restraint of greed and anger by all means, / and self-control—this is the purifier of all kinds of knowledge.

1.43.s:
varjyau sarvātmanā tau hi śreyoghātārthamudyatau /
nityakrodhācchriyaṃ rakṣettapo rakṣettu matsarāt //
1.43.d:
वर्ज्यौ सर्वात्मना तौ हि श्रेयोघातार्थमुद्यतौ ।
नित्यक्रोधाच्छ्रियं रक्षेत्तपो रक्षेत्तु मत्सरात् ॥
1.43.m: For those two must be shunned with one's whole self, as they are intent upon destroying the highest good. / One should protect prosperity from constant anger, and asceticism from envy;

1.43.s: vidyāṃ mānāpamānābhaghyāmātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ //
1.43.d: विद्यां मानापमानाभघ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः ॥
1.43.m: Knowledge from honour and dishonour, and the self from heedlessness.

1.43.s:
yasya sarve samāraṃbhaghā nirāśīrbandhanā dvija /
tyāge yasya hutaṃ sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān //
1.43.d:
यस्य सर्वे समारंभघा निराशीर्बन्धना द्विज ।
त्यागे यस्य हुतं सर्वं स त्यागी स च बुद्धिमान् ॥
1.43.m: He whose undertakings are all free from the bond of desire, O twice-born, / and to whom everything is offered up in renunciation—he is a renouncer, and he is wise.

1.43.s:
ahiṃstraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ maitrāyaṇa gataścaret /
parigrahātparityajya bhavedbaddhyā jitendriyaḥ //
1.43.d:
अहिंस्त्रः सर्वभूतानां मैत्रायण गतश्चरेत् ।
परिग्रहात्परित्यज्य भवेद्बद्ध्या जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.43.m: Harmless to all beings, he should wander about, benevolent to all; / abandoning possessions, he should become one who has mastered his senses by means of intellect.

1.43.s:
aśokasthānamāti vediha cāmutra cābhayam /
taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmamanā //
1.43.d:
अशोकस्थानमाति वेदिह चामुत्र चाभयम् ।
तपोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्ममना ॥
1.43.m: The sorrowless state brings fearlessness both here and in the hereafter / for the sage who is constant in austerity, subdued, and self-controlled.

1.43.s:
ajitaṃ jetukāmena vyāsaṃgeṣu hyasaṃginā /
indriyairgṛhyate yadyattattavdyaktamiti sthitiḥ //
1.43.d:
अजितं जेतुकामेन व्यासंगेषु ह्यसंगिना ।
इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद्यत्तत्तव्द्यक्तमिति स्थितिः ॥
1.43.m: For one desiring to conquer the unconquered, unattached in the midst of attachments— / whatever is perceived by the senses, that is the manifest: such is the principle.

1.43.s:
avyaktamiti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyamatīndriyam /
aviśraṃbheṇa mantavyaṃ viśraṃbhe dhārayenmanaḥ //
1.43.d:
अव्यक्तमिति विज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ।
अविश्रंभेण मन्तव्यं विश्रंभे धारयेन्मनः ॥
1.43.m: Beyond the senses and graspable by inference, it should be known as the unmanifest. / One should reflect with vigilance; one should fix the mind in steadfast trust.

1.43.s:
manaḥ prāṇena gṛhṇīyātprāṇaṃ brahmaṇi dhārayet /
nivedādeva nirvāṇaṃ na ca kiñcidviccitayet //
1.43.d:
मनः प्राणेन गृह्णीयात्प्राणं ब्रह्मणि धारयेत् ।
निवेदादेव निर्वाणं न च किञ्चिद्विच्चितयेत् ॥
1.43.m: One should hold the mind with the breath, and fix the breath in Brahman; / liberation comes solely from detachment, and one should think of nothing else.

1.43.s:
sukhaṃ vai brahmaṇo brahmannirvedenādhigacchati /
śauce tu satataṃ yuktaḥ sadācārasamanvitaḥ //
1.43.d:
सुखं वै ब्रह्मणो ब्रह्मन्निर्वेदेनाधिगच्छति ।
शौचे तु सततं युक्तः सदाचारसमन्वितः ॥
1.43.m: Through detachment, O Brahmin, one attains the bliss of Brahman. / Constantly engaged in purity and endowed with right conduct,

1.43.s:
svanukrośaśca bhūteṣu taddvijātiṣu lakṣaṇam /
satyaṃvrataṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ satyaṃ visṛjate prajā //
1.43.d:
स्वनुक्रोशश्च भूतेषु तद्द्विजातिषु लक्षणम् ।
सत्यंव्रतं तपः शौचं सत्यं विसृजते प्रजा ॥
1.43.m: Compassionate toward beings—this is the characteristic among the twice-born. / Truth, vows, austerity, and purity—truth brings forth creatures.

1.43.s:
satyena dhāryate lokaḥ svaḥ satyenaiva gacchati /
anṛtaṃ tamaso rūpaṃ tamasā nīyate hyadhaḥ //
1.43.d:
सत्येन धार्यते लोकः स्वः सत्येनैव गच्छति ।
अनृतं तमसो रूपं तमसा नीयते ह्यधः ॥
1.43.m: By truth the world is sustained; by truth alone one goes to heaven. / Falsehood is the form of darkness; by darkness one is led downwards.

1.43.s:
tamograstāna paśyanti prakāśantamasāvṛtāḥ /
suduṣprakāśa ityāhurnarakaṃ tama eva ca //
1.43.d:
तमोग्रस्तान पश्यन्ति प्रकाशन्तमसावृताः ।
सुदुष्प्रकाश इत्याहुर्नरकं तम एव च ॥
1.43.m: Seized by darkness, enveloped in darkness, they do not see the light. / They say that hell is darkness and extremely difficult to illuminate.

1.43.s:
satyānṛtaṃ tadubhaghayaṃ prāpyate jagatīcaraiḥ /
tatrāpyevaṃvidhā loke vṛttiḥ satyānṛte bhavet //
1.43.d:
सत्यानृतं तदुभघयं प्राप्यते जगतीचरैः ।
तत्राप्येवंविधा लोके वृत्तिः सत्यानृते भवेत् ॥
1.43.m: Both truth and falsehood are encountered by those who walk the earth; / even there, such conduct in truth and falsehood exists in the world.

1.43.s:
dharmādharmauṃ prakāśaśca tamo duḥkhasukhaṃ tathā /
śārīrairmānasairduḥkhaiḥ sukhaiścāpyasukhodayaiḥ //
1.43.d:
धर्माधर्मौं प्रकाशश्च तमो दुःखसुखं तथा ।
शारीरैर्मानसैर्दुःखैः सुखैश्चाप्यसुखोदयैः ॥
1.43.m: Righteousness and unrighteousness, light and darkness, as well as pleasure and pain; / by bodily and mental pains, and by pleasures that lead to unhappiness,

1.43.s:
lokasṛṣṭaṃ prapaśyanto na muhyanti vicakṣaṇāḥ /
tatra duḥkhavimokṣārthaṃ prayateta vicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.43.d:
लोकसृष्टं प्रपश्यन्तो न मुह्यन्ति विचक्षणाः ।
तत्र दुःखविमोक्षार्थं प्रयतेत विचक्षणः ॥
1.43.m: Discerning people, observing what has been produced in the world, are not bewildered. / Therefore, the discerning person should strive for release from suffering.

1.43.s:
sukhaṃ hyanityaṃ bhūtānāmiha loke paratra ca /
rāhugrastasya somasya yathā jyotsnā na bhāsate //
1.43.d:
सुखं ह्यनित्यं भूतानामिह लोके परत्र च ।
राहुग्रस्तस्य सोमस्य यथा ज्योत्स्ना न भासते ॥
1.43.m: Pleasure is indeed impermanent for living beings in this world and in the next. / Just as the moonlight of the moon seized by Rāhu does not shine,

1.43.s: tathā tamobhibhūtānāṃ bhūtānāṃ naśyate sukham //
1.43.d: तथा तमोभिभूतानां भूतानां नश्यते सुखम् ॥
1.43.m: So the happiness of beings overcome by darkness is destroyed.

1.43.s:
tatkhalu dvividhaṃ sukhamucyacate śarīraṃ mānasaṃ ca /
iha khalvamuṣmiṃśca loke vastupravṛttayaḥ sukhārthamabhidhīyante nahītaḥ paratrāparvagaphalādviśiṣṭataramasti /
sa eva kāmyo guṇaviśeṣo dharmārthaguṇāraṃbhagastaddheturasyotpattiḥ sukhaprayojanārthamāraṃbhāḥ /
bharadvāja uvāca
vadaitadbhavatābhihitaṃ sukhānāṃ paramā sthitiriti //
1.43.d:
तत्खलु द्विविधं सुखमुच्यचते शरीरं मानसं च ।
इह खल्वमुष्मिंश्च लोके वस्तुप्रवृत्तयः सुखार्थमभिधीयन्ते नहीतः परत्रापर्वगफलाद्विशिष्टतरमस्ति ।
स एव काम्यो गुणविशेषो धर्मार्थगुणारंभगस्तद्धेतुरस्योत्पत्तिः सुखप्रयोजनार्थमारंभाः ।
भरद्वाज उवाच
वदैतद्भवताभिहितं सुखानां परमा स्थितिरिति ॥
1.43.m: Indeed, pleasure is said to be of two kinds: bodily and mental. / In this world and in the other world, the pursuits of objects are designated for the sake of happiness; for there is nothing higher than the fruit of final liberation beyond this. / That desirable, distinguished quality itself is the beginning of the qualities of dharma and artha, the cause of which is its production; undertakings are for the sake of happiness. / Bharadvāja said: / Speak of this which was stated by you, that this is the highest state among pleasures.

1.43.s: na tadupagṛhṇīmo na hyeṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ mahati sthitānām //
1.43.d: न तदुपगृह्णीमो न ह्येषामृषीणां महति स्थितानाम् ॥
1.43.m: We do not accept that, for it does not belong to these sages established in greatness.

1.43.s:
aprāpya eṣa kāmya guṇaviśeṣo na cainamabhiśīlayanti /
tapasi śrūyate trilokakṛdbrahmā prabhurekākī tiṣṭati brahmacārī na kāmasukhoṣvātmānamavadadhāti //
1.43.d:
अप्राप्य एष काम्य गुणविशेषो न चैनमभिशीलयन्ति ।
तपसि श्रूयते त्रिलोककृद्ब्रह्मा प्रभुरेकाकी तिष्टति ब्रह्मचारी न कामसुखोष्वात्मानमवदधाति ॥
1.43.m: This desirable, distinguished quality is unobtainable, and they do not cultivate it. / In austerity, it is heard that the creator of the three worlds, Lord Brahmā, stands alone, chaste, and does not fix his self on the pleasures of desire.

1.43.s: api ca bhagavānviśveśvara umāpatiḥ kāmamabhivartamānamanaṅgatvena samamanayat //
1.43.d: अपि च भगवान्विश्वेश्वर उमापतिः काममभिवर्तमानमनङ्गत्वेन सममनयत् ॥
1.43.m: Moreover, the venerable Lord of the Universe, the husband of Umā, reduced desire, as it was approaching, to bodilessness.

1.43.s: tasmādbhūmau na tu mahātmabhirañjayati gṛhīto na tveṣa tāvadviśiṣṭo guṇaviśeṣa iti //
1.43.d: तस्माद्भूमौ न तु महात्मभिरञ्जयति गृहीतो न त्वेष तावद्विशिष्टो गुणविशेष इति ॥
1.43.m: Therefore on earth, it is not joyfully accepted by great-souled persons; nor is this distinguished quality superior.

1.43.s: naitadbhagavataḥ pratyemi bhavatā tūktaṃ sukhānāṃ paramāḥ striya iti lokapravādo hi dvividhaḥ phalodayaḥ sukṛtātsukhamavāpyate 'nyathā duḥkhamiti //
1.43.d: नैतद्भगवतः प्रत्येमि भवता तूक्तं सुखानां परमाः स्त्रिय इति लोकप्रवादो हि द्विविधः फलोदयः सुकृतात्सुखमवाप्यते ऽन्यथा दुःखमिति ॥
1.43.m: I do not believe this of the lord; yet it was said by you that women are the supreme among pleasures. For popular saying holds that the fruition of actions is twofold: happiness is attained from good deeds, and suffering otherwise.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
atrocyate anṛtātkhalu tamaḥ prādurbhūtaṃ tatastamograstā adharmamevānuvartante na dharmaṃ krodhalobhamohahiṃsānṛtādibhikhacchannāḥ khalvasmiṃlloke nāmutra sukhamāpnuvanti vividhavyādhirujopatāpairavakīryante vadhabandhanaparikleśādibhiśca kṣutpipāsāśramakṛtairupatāpairupatapyante varṣavātātyuṣṇātiśītakṛtaiśca pratibhayaiḥ śārīrairduḥkhairupatapyante bandhudhanavināśaviprayogakṛtaiśca mānasaiḥ śaukairabhibhūyante jarāmṛtyukṛtaiścānyairiti yastvetaiḥ //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
अत्रोच्यते अनृतात्खलु तमः प्रादुर्भूतं ततस्तमोग्रस्ता अधर्ममेवानुवर्तन्ते न धर्मं क्रोधलोभमोहहिंसानृतादिभिखच्छन्नाः खल्वस्मिंल्लोके नामुत्र सुखमाप्नुवन्ति विविधव्याधिरुजोपतापैरवकीर्यन्ते वधबन्धनपरिक्लेशादिभिश्च क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमकृतैरुपतापैरुपतप्यन्ते वर्षवातात्युष्णातिशीतकृतैश्च प्रतिभयैः शारीरैर्दुःखैरुपतप्यन्ते बन्धुधनविनाशविप्रयोगकृतैश्च मानसैः शौकैरभिभूयन्ते जरामृत्युकृतैश्चान्यैरिति यस्त्वेतैः ॥
1.43.m:
Bhṛgu said:
Here it is said: From falsehood indeed darkness arose; then, seized by darkness, they pursue only adharma, not dharma. Veiled by anger, greed, delusion, violence, falsehood, and the like, they indeed obtain no happiness in this world nor in the next. They are strewn with diverse sicknesses, aches, and afflictions; they are tormented by afflictions caused by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, and by slaughters, bondages, distress, and the like; they are tormented by bodily sorrows born of fear, caused by rain, wind, extreme heat, and extreme cold; they are overwhelmed by mental griefs caused by the destruction and separation from kin and wealth, and by others caused by old age and death. But he who, by these—

1.43.s:
śārīraṃ mānasaṃ nāsti na jarā na ca pātakam /
nityameva sukhaṃ svarge sukhaṃ duḥkhamihobhayam //
1.43.d:
शारीरं मानसं नास्ति न जरा न च पातकम् ।
नित्यमेव सुखं स्वर्गे सुखं दुःखमिहोभयम् ॥
1.43.m: There is no bodily or mental [affliction], nor old age, nor sin; / there is only constant happiness in heaven; here [in this world] there are both happiness and sorrow.

1.43.s:
narake duḥkhamevāhuḥ sukhaṃ tatparamaṃ padam /
pṛthivī sarvabhūtānāṃ janitrī tadvidhāḥ striyaḥ //
1.43.d:
नरके दुःखमेवाहुः सुखं तत्परमं पदम् ।
पृथिवी सर्वभूतानां जनित्री तद्विधाः स्त्रियः ॥
1.43.m: In hell, they say, there is only sorrow; that supreme abode is bliss. / The earth is the mother of all beings, and women are of the same nature.

1.43.s:
pumānprajāpatistatraśukraṃ tejomayaṃ viduḥ /
ityetallokanirmātā dharmasya caritasya ca //
1.43.d:
पुमान्प्रजापतिस्तत्रशुक्रं तेजोमयं विदुः ।
इत्येतल्लोकनिर्माता धर्मस्य चरितस्य च ॥
1.43.m: The male is Prajāpati in that regard; they know his semen to be full of fiery energy. / Thus he is the creator of the world, of righteousness, and of good conduct,

1.43.s:
tapasaśca sutaptasya svādhyāyasya hutasya ca /
hutena śāmyate pāpaṃ svādhyāye śāntiruttamā //
1.43.d:
तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य स्वाध्यायस्य हुतस्य च ।
हुतेन शाम्यते पापं स्वाध्याये शान्तिरुत्तमा ॥
1.43.m: and of well-performed austerity, of personal Vedic study, and of oblations. / By oblations sin is pacified; in personal study lies the highest tranquility.

1.43.s:
dānena bhogānityāhusta pasā svargamāpnuyāt /
dānaṃ tu dvividhaṃ prāhuḥ paratrārthamihaiva ca //
1.43.d:
दानेन भोगानित्याहुस्त पसा स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् ।
दानं तु द्विविधं प्राहुः परत्रार्थमिहैव च ॥
1.43.m: They say that through giving one obtains enjoyments; through austerity one may attain heaven. / But giving they declare to be twofold: for the next world, and for this world alone.

1.43.s:
sadbhyo yaddīyate kiñcittatparatropatiṣṭate /
asadbhyo dīyate yattu taddānamiha bhujyate /
yādṛśaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tādṛśaṃ phalamaśnute //
1.43.d:
सद्भ्यो यद्दीयते किञ्चित्तत्परत्रोपतिष्टते ।
असद्भ्यो दीयते यत्तु तद्दानमिह भुज्यते ।
यादृशं दीयते दानं तादृशं फलमश्नुते ॥
1.43.m: Whatever is given to the virtuous waits [for the giver] in the next world; / but what is given to the unvirtuous is enjoyed [as a gift] here in this world. / Just as the gift that is given, so is the fruit that one experiences.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
kiṃ kasya dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃ vā dharmasya lakṣaṇam /
dharmaḥ katividho vāpi tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
किं कस्य धर्मचरणं किं वा धर्मस्य लक्षणम् ।
धर्मः कतिविधो वापि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / What is the practice of righteousness for whom, and what is the mark of righteousness? / Or of how many kinds is righteousness? You ought to explain that.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
svadharmācaraṇe yuktā ye bhavanti manīṣiṇaḥ /
teṣāṃ svargapalāvāptiryo 'nyathā sa vimuhyate //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
स्वधर्माचरणे युक्ता ये भवन्ति मनीषिणः ।
तेषां स्वर्गपलावाप्तिर्यो ऽन्यथा स विमुह्यते ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / Those wise men who are engaged in practicing their own duty, / attain the fruit of heaven; he who acts otherwise becomes deluded.

1.43.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
yadetañcāturāśramyaṃ brahmarṣivihitaṃ purā /
teṣāṃ sve sve samācārāstanme vaktumihārhasi //
1.43.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यदेतञ्चातुराश्रम्यं ब्रह्मर्षिविहितं पुरा ।
तेषां स्वे स्वे समाचारास्तन्मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
1.43.m: Bharadvāja said: / This system of four stages of life which was ordained of old by the Brahmin seers— / you ought to tell me here the respective practices proper to them.

1.43.s:
bhṛguruvāca
pūrvameva bhagavatā brahmaṇā lokahitamanutiṣṭatā dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthamāśramāścatvāro 'bhinirddiṣṭāḥ //
1.43.d:
भृगुरुवाच
पूर्वमेव भगवता ब्रह्मणा लोकहितमनुतिष्टता धर्मसंरक्षणार्थमाश्रमाश्चत्वारो ऽभिनिर्द्दिष्टाः ॥
1.43.m: Bhṛgu said: / In the very beginning, the four stages of life were prescribed by the blessed Lord Brahmā, who was acting for the welfare of the world, for the purpose of preserving righteousness.

1.43.s: tatra gurukulavāsameva prathamamāśramamāharanti samyagatra śaucasaskāraniyamavrataviniyatātmā ubhe saṃdhye bhāskarāgnidaivatānyupasthāya vihāya taddhyālasyaṃ gurorabhivādanavedābyāsaśravaṇapavitraghīkṛtāntarātmā triṣavaṇamupaspṛśya brahmacaryāgniparicaraṇaguruśuśrūṣā nityabhikṣābhaikṣyādisarvaniveditāntarātmā guruvacananideśānuṣṭānāpratikūlo guruprasādalabdhasvādhyāyatatparaḥ syāt //
1.43.d: तत्र गुरुकुलवासमेव प्रथममाश्रममाहरन्ति सम्यगत्र शौचसस्कारनियमव्रतविनियतात्मा उभे संध्ये भास्कराग्निदैवतान्युपस्थाय विहाय तद्ध्यालस्यं गुरोरभिवादनवेदाब्यासश्रवणपवित्रघीकृतान्तरात्मा त्रिषवणमुपस्पृश्य ब्रह्मचर्याग्निपरिचरणगुरुशुश्रूषा नित्यभिक्षाभैक्ष्यादिसर्वनिवेदितान्तरात्मा गुरुवचननिदेशानुष्टानाप्रतिकूलो गुरुप्रसादलब्धस्वाध्यायतत्परः स्यात् ॥
1.43.m: There, they declare living in the teacher's family to be the first stage of life. In this stage, having his self completely restrained by purity, sacraments, observances, and vows; having worshipped the sun, fire, and deities at both twilights; having cast aside sleep and laziness; having his inner self purified by saluting the teacher, Vedic study, and listening [to instruction]; having bathed at the three junctions of the day; devoted to chastity, attending to the sacred fire, service to the teacher, daily begging for alms, and offering his entire inner self [and food received] from alms and the like; never opposed to following the words and directions of the teacher; he should be intent on personal Vedic study obtained through the teacher's favor.

1.43.s:
bhavati cātra ślokaḥ
guruṃ yastu samārādhya dvijo vedamāvānpuyāt /
tasya svargaphalāvāptiḥ siddhyate cāsya mānasam /
iti gārhasthyaṃ khalu dvitīyamāśramaṃ vadanti //
1.43.d:
भवति चात्र श्लोकः
गुरुं यस्तु समाराध्य द्विजो वेदमावान्पुयात् ।
तस्य स्वर्गफलावाप्तिः सिद्ध्यते चास्य मानसम् ।
इति गार्हस्थ्यं खलु द्वितीयमाश्रमं वदन्ति ॥
1.43.m: And there is a verse on this: / But that twice-born man who, having worshipped his teacher, obtains the Veda, / attains the fruit of heaven, and his mental desire is accomplished. / Thus they indeed declare householdership to be the second stage of life.

1.43.s:
tasya sadā cāralakṣaṇaṃ sarvamanuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
samāvṛtānāṃ sadācārāṇāṃ sahadharmacaryaphalārthināṃ gṛhāśramo vidhīyate //
1.43.d:
तस्य सदा चारलक्षणं सर्वमनुव्याख्यास्यामः ।
समावृतानां सदाचाराणां सहधर्मचर्यफलार्थिनां गृहाश्रमो विधीयते ॥
1.43.m: We shall expound all the characteristics of its good conduct. / The householder stage is prescribed for those who have returned home [from studenthood], who possess good conduct, and who desire the fruits of joint performance of duty.

1.43.s: dharmārthakāmāvāptirhya.tra trivargasādhanamapekṣyāgarhitakarmaṇā dhanānyādāya svādhyāyopalabdhaprakarṣeṇa vā brahmarṣinirmitena vā adbhiḥ sāgaragatena vā dravyaniyamābhyāsadaivataprasādopalabdhena vā dhanena gṛhastho gārhasthyaṃ vartayet //
1.43.d: धर्मार्थकामावाप्तिर्ह्य।त्र त्रिवर्गसाधनमपेक्ष्यागर्हितकर्मणा धनान्यादाय स्वाध्यायोपलब्धप्रकर्षेण वा ब्रह्मर्षिनिर्मितेन वा अद्भिः सागरगतेन वा द्रव्यनियमाभ्यासदैवतप्रसादोपलब्धेन वा धनेन गृहस्थो गार्हस्थ्यं वर्तयेत् ॥
1.43.m: For herein lies the attainment of duty, wealth, and pleasure, with a view to the cultivation of the three aims of life. Having acquired wealth through blameless occupations, or by excellence obtained through personal Vedic study, or that established by Brahmin seers, or by crossing the ocean on waters, or by wealth obtained through disciplined pursuit of possessions or the grace of the deities, the householder should maintain householdership.

1.43.s: taddhi sarvāśramaṇāṃ mūlamudāharanti gurukulanivāsinaḥ parivrājakā ye 'nye saṃkalpitavrataniyamadharmānuṣṭāninasteṣāmapyantarā ca bhikṣābalisaṃvibhāgāḥ pravartante //
1.43.d: तद्धि सर्वाश्रमणां मूलमुदाहरन्ति गुरुकुलनिवासिनः परिव्राजका ये ऽन्ये संकल्पितव्रतनियमधर्मानुष्टानिनस्तेषामप्यन्तरा च भिक्षाबलिसंविभागाः प्रवर्तन्ते ॥
1.43.m: For they declare that to be the foundation of all stages of life. For those dwelling in the teacher's household, for wandering mendicants, and for others who practice vows, observances, and duties they have undertaken—even in between these, the distributions of alms and offerings proceed [from him].

1.43.s: vānaprasthānāṃ ca dravyopaskāra iti prāyaśaḥ khalvete sādhavaḥ sādhupathyodanāḥ svādhyāyaprasaṃginastīrthābhigamanadeśadarśanārthaṃ pṛthivīṃ paryaṭanti //
1.43.d: वानप्रस्थानां च द्रव्योपस्कार इति प्रायशः खल्वेते साधवः साधुपथ्योदनाः स्वाध्यायप्रसंगिनस्तीर्थाभिगमनदेशदर्शनार्थं पृथिवीं पर्यटन्ति ॥
1.43.m: And there is the provision of materials for forest hermits. For mostly these virtuous men, having wholesome food suitable for the virtuous, engaged in personal study of the Veda, wander the earth for the purpose of visiting sacred fords and seeing various countries.

1.43.s: teṣāṃ pratyutthānābhigamanamanasūyāvākyadānasukhasatkārāsanasukhaśayanābhyavahārasatkriyā ceti //
1.43.d: तेषां प्रत्युत्थानाभिगमनमनसूयावाक्यदानसुखसत्कारासनसुखशयनाभ्यवहारसत्क्रिया चेति ॥
1.43.m: For them, there is rising to welcome them, going out to greet them, speaking words free from envy, providing comfortable hospitality, seats, comfortable beds, and food.

1.43.s:
bhavati cātra ślokaḥ
atithiryasya bhagnāśo gṛhātpratinivartate /
sa dattvā duṣkṛtaṃ tasmai puṇyamādāya gacchati //
1.43.d:
भवति चात्र श्लोकः
अतिथिर्यस्य भग्नाशो गृहात्प्रतिनिवर्तते ।
स दत्त्वा दुष्कृतं तस्मै पुण्यमादाय गच्छति ॥
1.43.m: And there is a verse on this: / A guest who turns away from a house disappointed in his hopes, / having given his bad deeds to that [householder], goes away taking the [householder's] merit.

1.43.s: api cātra yajñakriyābhirdevatāḥ prīyante nivāpena pitaro vidyābhyāsaśravaṇadhāraṇena ṛṣayaḥ apatyotpādanena prajāpatiriti //
1.43.d: अपि चात्र यज्ञक्रियाभिर्देवताः प्रीयन्ते निवापेन पितरो विद्याभ्यासश्रवणधारणेन ऋषयः अपत्योत्पादनेन प्रजापतिरिति ॥
1.43.m: Moreover, in this stage deities are pleased through sacrificial rites, the ancestors through the libation of water, the seers through the study, hearing, and retention of sacred knowledge, and Prajāpati through the procreation of offspring.

1.43.s:
lokau cātra bhavataḥ
vātsalyāḥ sarvabhūtebhyo vāyoḥ śrotrastathā girā /
paritāpodapaghātaśca pāruṣyaṃ cātra garhitam //
1.43.d:
लोकौ चात्र भवतः
वात्सल्याः सर्वभूतेभ्यो वायोः श्रोत्रस्तथा गिरा ।
परितापोदपघातश्च पारुष्यं चात्र गर्हितम् ॥
1.43.m: And there are two verses on this: / Affection toward all beings, in hearing the wind, and in speech; / and causing torment, injury, and harshness are condemned here.

1.43.s:
avajñānamahṝṅkāro daṃbhaścaiva vigarhitaḥ /
ahiṃsā satyamakrodaṃ sarvāśramagataṃ tapaḥ //
1.43.d:
अवज्ञानमहॄङ्कारो दंभश्चैव विगर्हितः ।
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोदं सर्वाश्रमगतं तपः ॥
1.43.m: Disrespect, egotism, and hypocrisy are also thoroughly condemned; / non-injury, truth, and freedom from anger are the austerity common to all stages of life.

1.43.s: api cātra mālyābharaṇavastrābhyaṅganityopabhoganṛtyagītavāditraśrutisukhanayanasneharāmādarśanānāṃ prāptirbhakṣyabhojyalehyapeyacoṣyāṇāmabhyavahāryyāṇāṃ vividhānāmupabhogaḥ //
1.43.d: अपि चात्र माल्याभरणवस्त्राभ्यङ्गनित्योपभोगनृत्यगीतवादित्रश्रुतिसुखनयनस्नेहरामादर्शनानां प्राप्तिर्भक्ष्यभोज्यलेह्यपेयचोष्याणामभ्यवहार्य्याणां विविधानामुपभोगः ॥
1.43.m: Moreover, in this stage there is the continuous enjoyment of garlands, ornaments, clothes, and anointing, along with the pleasure of hearing dance, song, and musical instruments, the viewing of charming women that gladdens the eyes, and the consumption of various kinds of edibles: chewables, foodstuffs, licked dishes, beverages, and foods to be sucked.

1.43.s:
svavihārasaṃtoṣaḥ kāmasukhāvāptiriti /
trivargaguṇanirvṛttiryasya nityaṃ gṛhāśrame /
sa sukhānyanubhūyeha śiṣṭānāṃ gatimāpnuyāt //
1.43.d:
स्वविहारसंतोषः कामसुखावाप्तिरिति ।
त्रिवर्गगुणनिर्वृत्तिर्यस्य नित्यं गृहाश्रमे ।
स सुखान्यनुभूयेह शिष्टानां गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.43.m: There is satisfaction in one's own pleasures and attainment of the joy of desires. / He in whose household stage the qualities of the three aims of life are constantly fulfilled, / having experienced pleasures here, will attain the destination of the virtuous.

1.43.s:
uñchavṛttirvṛhastho yaḥ svadhama caraṇe rataḥ /
tyaktakāmasukhāraṃbhaḥ svargastasya na durlabhaḥ //
1.43.d:
उञ्छवृत्तिर्वृहस्थो यः स्वधम चरणे रतः ।
त्यक्तकामसुखारंभः स्वर्गस्तस्य न दुर्लभः ॥
1.43.m: The householder who lives by gleaning ears of grain, devoted to practicing his own duty, / who has abandoned the pursuit of sensual pleasure, finds heaven not difficult to attain.

1.43.s: vānaprasthāḥ khalvapi dharmamanusarantaḥ puṇyāni tīrthāni nadīprastravaṇāni svabhakteṣvaraṇyeṣu mṛgavarāhamahiṣa śārdūlavanagajākīrṇeṣu tapasyante anusaṃcaranti //
1.43.d: वानप्रस्थाः खल्वपि धर्ममनुसरन्तः पुण्यानि तीर्थानि नदीप्रस्त्रवणानि स्वभक्तेष्वरण्येषु मृगवराहमहिष शार्दूलवनगजाकीर्णेषु तपस्यन्ते अनुसंचरन्ति ॥
1.43.m: Moreover, the forest hermits, following duty, practice austerities and wander about sacred fords, rivers, waterfalls, and forests dear to them that are teeming with deer, boars, buffaloes, tigers, and wild elephants.

1.43.s:
tyaktagrāmyavastrābhyavahāropabhogā vanyauṣadhiphalamūlaparṇaparimitavicitraniyatāhārāḥ sthānāsaninobhūpāṣāṇasikatāśarkarāvālukābhasmaśāyinaḥ kāśukuśacarmavalkalasaṃvṛtāṅgāḥ keśaśyaśrunakharomadhāriṇo niyatakālopasparśanāḥśuṣkabalihomakālānuṣṭāyinaḥ /
samitkuśakusumāpahārasaṃmārjanalabdhaviśrāmāḥ śītoṣṇapavanaviṣṭaṃ bhavibhinnasarvatvaco vividhaniyamayogacaryānuṣṭānavihitapariśuṣkamāṃsaśoṇitatvagasthibhūtā dhṛtiparāḥ sattvayogāccharīrāṇyudvahṝnte //
1.43.d:
त्यक्तग्राम्यवस्त्राभ्यवहारोपभोगा वन्यौषधिफलमूलपर्णपरिमितविचित्रनियताहाराः स्थानासनिनोभूपाषाणसिकताशर्करावालुकाभस्मशायिनः काशुकुशचर्मवल्कलसंवृताङ्गाः केशश्यश्रुनखरोमधारिणो नियतकालोपस्पर्शनाःशुष्कबलिहोमकालानुष्टायिनः ।
समित्कुशकुसुमापहारसंमार्जनलब्धविश्रामाः शीतोष्णपवनविष्टं भविभिन्नसर्वत्वचो विविधनियमयोगचर्यानुष्टानविहितपरिशुष्कमांसशोणितत्वगस्थिभूता धृतिपराः सत्त्वयोगाच्छरीराण्युद्वहॄन्ते ॥
1.43.m: They have abandoned village clothing, food, and enjoyments; their food is measured, varied, and strictly regulated, consisting of wild herbs, fruits, roots, and leaves; standing and sitting, they sleep on the earth, stones, gravel, grit, sand, and ashes; their limbs are covered with kāśa grass, kuśa grass, hides, and bark-cloth; they bear hair, beards, nails, and body-hair; bathing at fixed times, observing the times for dry offerings and fire oblations; / finding rest in collecting kindling, kuśa grass, and flowers, and in sweeping; having their entire skin cracked by exposure to cold, heat, and wind; reduced to skin and bones with their flesh and blood dried up by the performance of various rules and practices of yoga; devoted to steadfastness, they bear their bodies through the power of purity.

1.43.s:
yastvetāṃ niyatacaryāṃ brahmarṣivihitāṃ caret /
sa dahedagnivaddoṣāñjayellokāṃśca durjāyān //
1.43.d:
यस्त्वेतां नियतचर्यां ब्रह्मर्षिविहितां चरेत् ।
स दहेदग्निवद्दोषाञ्जयेल्लोकांश्च दुर्जायान् ॥
1.43.m: He who practices this regulated conduct prescribed by the Brahmin seers / will burn away blemishes like fire and conquer worlds that are hard to win.

1.43.s:
parivrājakānāṃ punarācāraḥ tadyathā /
vimucyāgniṃ dhanakalatraparibarhasaṃgeṣvātmānaṃ snehapāśānavadhūya parivrajanti /
samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanāstrivargapravṛtteṣvasaktabuddhayaḥ //
1.43.d:
परिव्राजकानां पुनराचारः तद्यथा ।
विमुच्याग्निं धनकलत्रपरिबर्हसंगेष्वात्मानं स्नेहपाशानवधूय परिव्रजन्ति ।
समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनास्त्रिवर्गप्रवृत्तेष्वसक्तबुद्धयः ॥
1.43.m: Now, the conduct of wandering mendicants is as follows: / Having relinquished the sacred fire, having cast off the ties of affection in regard to wealth, wife, and attachments to possessions, they wander forth, / viewing a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal, their minds detached from pursuits concerning the three aims of life.

1.43.s: arimitrodāsīnāṃ tulyadarśanāḥ sthāvarajarāyujāṇḍajasvedajānāṃ bhūtānāṃ vāṅmanṛḥkarmabhiranabhiranabhidrohiṇo 'niketāḥ parvatapulinavṛkṣamūladevāyatanānyanusaṃcaranto vā sārthamupeyurnagaraṃ grāmaṃ vā na krodhadarpalobhamohakārpaṇyadaṃbhaparivādābhimānanirvṛttahiṃsā iti //
1.43.d: अरिमित्रोदासीनां तुल्यदर्शनाः स्थावरजरायुजाण्डजस्वेदजानां भूतानां वाङ्मनृःकर्मभिरनभिरनभिद्रोहिणो ऽनिकेताः पर्वतपुलिनवृक्षमूलदेवायतनान्यनुसंचरन्तो वा सार्थमुपेयुर्नगरं ग्रामं वा न क्रोधदर्पलोभमोहकार्पण्यदंभपरिवादाभिमाननिर्वृत्तहिंसा इति ॥
1.43.m: Regarding enemies, friends, and indifferent persons with an equal eye; harmless in speech, mind, and action towards living beings that are stationary, womb-born, egg-born, or sweat-born; homeless, wandering through mountains, sandbanks, the roots of trees, and temples; or they may enter a caravan, city, or village; their violence has ceased through the elimination of anger, pride, greed, delusion, miserliness, deceit, slander, and egotism.

1.43.s:
bhavanti cātra ślokāḥ
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dattvā yaścarate muniḥ /
na tasya sarvabhūtebhyo bhayamutpadyate kvacit //
1.43.d:
भवन्ति चात्र श्लोकाः
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यश्चरते मुनिः ।
न तस्य सर्वभूतेभ्यो भयमुत्पद्यते क्वचित् ॥
1.43.m: And there are verses on this: / The sage who wanders having granted safety to all beings— / from no beings does fear arise for him anywhere.

1.43.s:
kṛtvāgnihotraṃ svaśarīrasaṃsthaṃ śarīramagniṃ svamukhe juhoti /
viprastu bhaikṣopagatairhavirbhiścitā gninā saṃvrajate hi sokān //
1.43.d:
कृत्वाग्निहोत्रं स्वशरीरसंस्थं शरीरमग्निं स्वमुखे जुहोति ।
विप्रस्तु भैक्षोपगतैर्हविर्भिश्चिता ग्निना संव्रजते हि सोकान् ॥
1.43.m: Having established the agnihotra within his own body, he offers his body-fire into his own mouth; / a Brahmin who offers with oblations obtained from alms goes with his accumulated fire to the worlds of light.

1.43.s:
mokṣāśramaṃ yaścarate yathoktaṃ śuciḥ svasaṃkalpitayuktabuddhiḥ /
anindhanaṃ jyotiriva praśāntaṃ sa brahmalokaṃ śrayate dvijātiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge dvitīyapāde bhṛgubharadvājasaṃvāde brāhmaṇācāranirūpaṇaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.43.d:
मोक्षाश्रमं यश्चरते यथोक्तं शुचिः स्वसंकल्पितयुक्तबुद्धिः ।
अनिन्धनं ज्योतिरिव प्रशान्तं स ब्रह्मलोकं श्रयते द्विजातिः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे द्वितीयपादे भृगुभरद्वाजसंवादे ब्राह्मणाचारनिरूपणं नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.43.m:
The twice-born who practices the stage of life leading to liberation as taught, pure, with an intellect concentrated on his own intention, / attains the world of Brahmā, tranquil like a fire without fuel.

Thus ends the forty-third chapter, entitled "Exposition of the Conduct of Brāhmaṇas", in the dialogue between Bhṛgu and Bharadvāja in the second quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.44.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
asmāllokātparo lokaḥ śrūyate nopalabhyate /
tamahaṃ jñātumicchāmi tadbhavānvaktumarhati //
1.44.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
अस्माल्लोकात्परो लोकः श्रूयते नोपलभ्यते ।
तमहं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
1.44.m:
Bharadvāja said:
A world beyond this world is heard of, but not perceived. / I wish to know about it; you ought to tell me that.

1.44.s:
mṛguruvāca
uttare himavatpārśve puṇye sarvaguṇānvite /
puṇyaḥ kṣemyaśca kāmyaśca sa paro loka ucyate //
1.44.d:
मृगुरुवाच
उत्तरे हिमवत्पार्श्वे पुण्ये सर्वगुणान्विते ।
पुण्यः क्षेम्यश्च काम्यश्च स परो लोक उच्यते ॥
1.44.m:
Bhṛgu said:
On the northern side of the Himavat, sacred and endowed with all virtues, / holy, secure, and desirable, that is called the world beyond.

1.44.s:
tatra hyapāpakarmāṇaḥ śucayo 'tyantanirmalāḥ /
lobhamohaparityaktā mānavā nirupadravāḥ //
1.44.d:
तत्र ह्यपापकर्माणः शुचयो ऽत्यन्तनिर्मलाः ।
लोभमोहपरित्यक्ता मानवा निरुपद्रवाः ॥
1.44.m: For there men are of sinless deeds, pure, exceedingly spotless, / free from greed and delusion, and without affliction.

1.44.s:
sa svargasadṛśo deśaḥ tatra hyuktāḥ śubhā guṇāḥ /
kāle mṛtyuḥ prabavati spṛśanti vyādhayo na ca //
1.44.d:
स स्वर्गसदृशो देशः तत्र ह्युक्ताः शुभा गुणाः ।
काले मृत्युः प्रबवति स्पृशन्ति व्याधयो न च ॥
1.44.m: That region is like heaven, for auspicious qualities are declared there. / Death occurs [only] at the appointed time, and diseases do not touch [them].

1.44.s:
na lobaḥ paradāreṣu svadāranirato janaḥ /
nānyo hi vadhyate tatra dravyeṣu ca na vismayaḥ //
1.44.d:
न लोबः परदारेषु स्वदारनिरतो जनः ।
नान्यो हि वध्यते तत्र द्रव्येषु च न विस्मयः ॥
1.44.m: There is no desire for another's wife; people are devoted to their own wives. / Indeed, no other person is slain there, nor is there greed for possessions.

1.44.s:
paro hyadharmo naivāsti saṃdeho nāpi jāyate /
kṛtasya tu phalaṃ tatra pratyakṣamupalabhyate //
1.44.d:
परो ह्यधर्मो नैवास्ति संदेहो नापि जायते ।
कृतस्य तु फलं तत्र प्रत्यक्षमुपलभ्यते ॥
1.44.m: For supreme adharma does not exist at all, nor does doubt arise; / and the fruit of what is done is directly perceived there.

1.44.s:
yānāsanāśanopetā prasādabhavanāśrayāḥ /
sarvakāmairvṛtāḥ keciddhemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ //
1.44.d:
यानासनाशनोपेता प्रसादभवनाश्रयाः ।
सर्वकामैर्वृताः केचिद्धेमाभरणभूषिताः ॥
1.44.m: Endowed with vehicles, seats, and food, dwelling in palaces, / some are surrounded by all desirable things and adorned with golden ornaments.

1.44.s:
prāṇadhāraṇamātraṃ tu keṣāñcidupapadyate /
śrameṇa mahatā kecitkurvanti prāṇadhāraṇam //
1.44.d:
प्राणधारणमात्रं तु केषाञ्चिदुपपद्यते ।
श्रमेण महता केचित्कुर्वन्ति प्राणधारणम् ॥
1.44.m: For some, however, only mere sustenance of life is obtained; / some maintain their life only with great toil.

1.44.s:
iha dharmaparāḥ kecitkecinnaiṣkṛtikā narāḥ /
sukhitā duḥkhitāḥ kecinnirdhanā dhanino pare //
1.44.d:
इह धर्मपराः केचित्केचिन्नैष्कृतिका नराः ।
सुखिता दुःखिताः केचिन्निर्धना धनिनो परे ॥
1.44.m: Here [on earth] some men are devoted to dharma, while some are deceitful; / some are happy, some are sorrowful; some are penniless, others wealthy.

1.44.s:
iha śramo bhayaṃ mohaḥ kṣudhā tīvrā ca jāyate /
lobhaścārthakṛto tṝṇāṃ yena muhyantyapaṇḍitāḥ //
1.44.d:
इह श्रमो भयं मोहः क्षुधा तीव्रा च जायते ।
लोभश्चार्थकृतो तॄणां येन मुह्यन्त्यपण्डिताः ॥
1.44.m: Here fatigue, fear, delusion, and intense hunger arise, / as well as greed caused by wealth among men, by which fools are deluded.

1.44.s:
yastadvedo bhayaṃ prājñaḥ pāpmanā na sa lipyate /
sopadhe nikṛtiḥ steyaṃ parivādo 'bhyasūyatā //
1.44.d:
यस्तद्वेदो भयं प्राज्ञः पाप्मना न स लिप्यते ।
सोपधे निकृतिः स्तेयं परिवादो ऽभ्यसूयता ॥
1.44.m: The wise man who knows that danger is not tainted by evil. / Fraud with deception, theft, slander, malice,

1.44.s:
paropaghāto hiṃsā ca paiśunmanṛtaṃ tathā /
etānsaṃsevate yastu tapastasya prahīyate //
1.44.d:
परोपघातो हिंसा च पैशुन्मनृतं तथा ।
एतान्संसेवते यस्तु तपस्तस्य प्रहीयते ॥
1.44.m: injury to others, violence, calumny, and falsehood— / whoever practices these, his austerity diminishes.

1.44.s:
yastvetānācaredvidvānna tapastasya varddhate /
iha cintā bahuvidhā dharmādharmasya karmaṇaḥ //
1.44.d:
यस्त्वेतानाचरेद्विद्वान्न तपस्तस्य वर्द्धते ।
इह चिन्ता बहुविधा धर्माधर्मस्य कर्मणः ॥
1.44.m: And if an educated man practices these, his austerity does not grow. / Here there are many kinds of anxiety concerning actions of dharma and adharma.

1.44.s:
karmabhūmiriyaṃ loke iha kṛtvā śubhāśubham /
śubhaiḥ śubhamavāpnoti tathāśubhamathānyathā //
1.44.d:
कर्मभूमिरियं लोके इह कृत्वा शुभाशुभम् ।
शुभैः शुभमवाप्नोति तथाशुभमथान्यथा ॥
1.44.m: This world is the land of action; having done auspicious and inauspicious deeds here, / one attains good by good [deeds], and likewise bad through the opposite.

1.44.s:
iha prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāstathā /
iṣṭeṣṭatapasaḥ pūtā brahmalokamupāśritāḥ //
1.44.d:
इह प्रजापतिः पूर्वं देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा ।
इष्टेष्टतपसः पूता ब्रह्मलोकमुपाश्रिताः ॥
1.44.m: Here formerly Prajāpati, the gods, and hosts of sages, / having offered sacrifices and performed desired austerities, became purified and resorted to the world of Brahmā.

1.44.s:
uttaraḥ pṛthivībhāgaḥ sarvapuṇyatamaḥ śubhaḥ /
ihasthāstatra jāyante ye vai puṇyakṛto janāḥ //
1.44.d:
उत्तरः पृथिवीभागः सर्वपुण्यतमः शुभः ।
इहस्थास्तत्र जायन्ते ये वै पुण्यकृतो जनाः ॥
1.44.m: The northern part of the earth is the most sacred of all and auspicious; / those people living here who perform holy deeds are born there.

1.44.s:
yadi satkāramicchanti tiryagyoniṣu cāpare /
kṣīṇāyuṣastathā cānye naśyanti pṛthivītale //
1.44.d:
यदि सत्कारमिच्छन्ति तिर्यग्योनिषु चापरे ।
क्षीणायुषस्तथा चान्ये नश्यन्ति पृथिवीतले ॥
1.44.m: If they desire honour [they may go there], while others [fall] into animal wombs; / and others, their lifespans exhausted, perish on the surface of the earth.

1.44.s:
anyonyabhakṣaṇāsaktā lobhamohasamanvitāḥ /
ihaiva parivarttante na ca yāntyuttarāṃ diśam //
1.44.d:
अन्योन्यभक्षणासक्ता लोभमोहसमन्विताः ।
इहैव परिवर्त्तन्ते न च यान्त्युत्तरां दिशम् ॥
1.44.m: Addicted to devouring one another, filled with greed and delusion, / they revolve right here and do not go to the northern direction.

1.44.s:
gurūnupāsate ye tu niyatā brahmacāriṇaḥ /
panthānaṃ sarvālokānāṃ vijānanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
1.44.d:
गुरूनुपासते ये तु नियता ब्रह्मचारिणः ।
पन्थानं सर्वालोकानां विजानन्ति मनीषिणः ॥
1.44.m: Those who serve their teachers, disciplined and celibate, / those wise men know the path of all the worlds.

1.44.s:
ityukto 'yaṃ mayā dharmaḥ saṃkṣipto brahmanirmitaḥ /
dharmādharmauṃ hi lokasya yo vai vetti sa buddhimān //
1.44.d:
इत्युक्तो ऽयं मया धर्मः संक्षिप्तो ब्रह्मनिर्मितः ।
धर्माधर्मौं हि लोकस्य यो वै वेत्ति स बुद्धिमान् ॥
1.44.m: Thus this concise dharma created by Brahmā has been spoken by me; / for whoever knows the dharma and adharma of the world is wise.

1.44.s:
bharadvāja uvāca /.
adhyātmaṃ nāma yadidaṃ puruṣasyeha cintyate /
yadadhyātmaṃ yathā caitattanme brūhi tapodhana //
1.44.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच ॥
अध्यात्मं नाम यदिदं पुरुषस्येह चिन्त्यते ।
यदध्यात्मं यथा चैतत्तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन ॥
1.44.m:
Bharadvāja said:
What is this that is considered here as the 'self' of man? / Tell me, O ascetic, what this inner self is and how it exists.

1.44.s:
bhṛguruvāca
adhyātmamiti viprarṣe yadetadanupṛcchasi /
tadvyākhyāṃsyāmi te tāta śreyaskaratamaṃ sukham //
1.44.d:
भृगुरुवाच
अध्यात्ममिति विप्रर्षे यदेतदनुपृच्छसि ।
तद्व्याख्यांस्यामि ते तात श्रेयस्करतमं सुखम् ॥
1.44.m:
Bhṛgu said:
Since you ask this, O brahmin sage, concerning the inner self, / I will explain that to you, my dear child, which is most beneficial and brings happiness,

1.44.s:
sṛṣṭipralayasaṃyuktamācāryaiḥ paridarśitam /
yajjñātvā puruṣo loke prītiṃ saukhyaṃ ca vindati //
1.44.d:
सृष्टिप्रलयसंयुक्तमाचार्यैः परिदर्शितम् ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा पुरुषो लोके प्रीतिं सौख्यं च विन्दति ॥
1.44.m: associated with creation and dissolution, shown by the teachers, / knowing which a man finds joy and happiness in the world.

1.44.s:
phalalābhaśca tasya syātsarvabhūtahitaṃ ca tat /
pṛthivī vāyurākāśamāpo jyotiśca pañcamam //
1.44.d:
फललाभश्च तस्य स्यात्सर्वभूतहितं च तत् ।
पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम् ॥
1.44.m: And there will be gain of fruit for him, and that is beneficial to all beings. / Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth—

1.44.s:
mahābhūtāni bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prabhavāpyayau /
yataḥ sṛṣṭāni tatraiva tāni yānti layaṃ punaḥ //
1.44.d:
महाभूतानि भूतानां सर्वेषां प्रभवाप्ययौ ।
यतः सृष्टानि तत्रैव तानि यान्ति लयं पुनः ॥
1.44.m: these great elements are the origin and dissolution of all beings; / from where they are created, into that very source they dissolve again.

1.44.s:
mahābhūtāni bhūtebhyaḥ sāgarasyormayo yathā /
prasārya ca yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ //
1.44.d:
महाभूतानि भूतेभ्यः सागरस्योर्मयो यथा ।
प्रसार्य च यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः ॥
1.44.m: The great elements [arise] from beings like the waves of the ocean; / and just as a tortoise extends its limbs and withdraws them again,

1.44.s:
tadvad bhūtāni bhūtātmā sṛṣṭāni harate punaḥ /
mahābhūtāni pañcaiva sarvabhūteṣu bhūtakṛt //
1.44.d:
तद्वद् भूतानि भूतात्मा सृष्टानि हरते पुनः ।
महाभूतानि पञ्चैव सर्वभूतेषु भूतकृत् ॥
1.44.m: in the same way the Self of beings withdraws the created beings again. / The Creator of beings made the five great elements in all beings

1.44.s:
akarotteṣu vai samyak taṃ tu jīvo na paśyati /
śabdaḥ śrotraṃ tathā khāni trayamākāśayonijam //
1.44.d:
अकरोत्तेषु वै सम्यक् तं तु जीवो न पश्यति ।
शब्दः श्रोत्रं तथा खानि त्रयमाकाशयोनिजम् ॥
1.44.m: properly within them, but the living soul does not see Him. / Sound, the ear, and the bodily cavities: this triad is born from the womb of space.

1.44.s:
vāyoḥ sparsastathā ceṣṭā tvakcaiva tritayaṃ smṛtam /
rūpaṃ cakṣustathā pākastrividhaṃ teja ucyate //
1.44.d:
वायोः स्पर्सस्तथा चेष्टा त्वक्चैव त्रितयं स्मृतम् ।
रूपं चक्षुस्तथा पाकस्त्रिविधं तेज उच्यते ॥
1.44.m: Touch, movement, and the skin are known as the triad of wind. / Form, the eye, and digestion are declared as the threefold nature of fire.

1.44.s:
rasāḥ kledaśca jihvā ca trayo jalaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ /
ghreyaṃ ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca ete bhūmiguṇāstrayaḥ //
1.44.d:
रसाः क्लेदश्च जिह्वा च त्रयो जलगुणाः स्मृताः ।
घ्रेयं घ्राणं शरीरं च एते भूमिगुणास्त्रयः ॥
1.44.m: Tastes, moisture, and the tongue are remembered as the three qualities of water. / The smellable, the organ of smell, and the body: these are the three qualities of earth.

1.44.s:
mahābhūtāni pacaiva ṣaṣṭaṃ ca mana ucyate /
indriyāṇi manaścaiva vijñātānyasya bhārata //
1.44.d:
महाभूतानि पचैव षष्टं च मन उच्यते ।
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव विज्ञातान्यस्य भारत ॥
1.44.m: The great elements are five, and the mind is called the sixth; / the senses and the mind are known for this [embodied soul], O descendant of Bharata.

1.44.s:
saptamī buddhirityāhuḥ kṣetrajñaḥ punaraṣṭamaḥ /
śrotraṃ vai śravaṇārthāya sparśanāya ca tvak smṛtā //
1.44.d:
सप्तमी बुद्धिरित्याहुः क्षेत्रज्ञः पुनरष्टमः ।
श्रोत्रं वै श्रवणार्थाय स्पर्शनाय च त्वक् स्मृता ॥
1.44.m: They say the intellect is the seventh, and the knower of the field is the eighth. / The ear is for hearing, and the skin is known to be for touching;

1.44.s:
rasādānāya rasanā gandhādānāya nāsikā /
cakṣurālokanāyaiva saṃśayaṃ kurute manaḥ //
1.44.d:
रसादानाय रसना गन्धादानाय नासिका ।
चक्षुरालोकनायैव संशयं कुरुते मनः ॥
1.44.m: the tongue is for perceiving taste, and the nose is for perceiving smell; / the eye is for seeing, and the mind produces doubt;

1.44.s:
buddhiradhyavasānāya kṣetrajñaḥ sākṣivatsthitaḥ /
urddhaṃ pādatalābhyāṃ yadavākcodakca paśyati //
1.44.d:
बुद्धिरध्यवसानाय क्षेत्रज्ञः साक्षिवत्स्थितः ।
उर्द्धं पादतलाभ्यां यदवाक्चोदक्च पश्यति ॥
1.44.m: the intellect is for determination, and the knower of the field stands like a witness. / What looks upward from the soles of the feet, and downward and horizontally—

1.44.s:
etena sarvamevedaṃ vibhunā cyāptamantaram /
puruṣairindriyāṇīha veditavyāni kṛtstraśaḥ //
1.44.d:
एतेन सर्वमेवेदं विभुना च्याप्तमन्तरम् ।
पुरुषैरिन्द्रियाणीह वेदितव्यानि कृत्स्त्रशः ॥
1.44.m: all this inside is pervaded by this all-pervading [knower of the field]. / The senses here ought to be known completely by men.

1.44.s:
tamo rajaśca sattvaṃ ca te 'pi bhāvāstadāśritāḥ /
etāṃ buddhiṃ naro buddhā bhūtānāgatiṃ gatim //
1.44.d:
तमो रजश्च सत्त्वं च ते ऽपि भावास्तदाश्रिताः ।
एतां बुद्धिं नरो बुद्धा भूतानागतिं गतिम् ॥
1.44.m: Tamas, rajas, and sattva—these states also depend on that. / A man, having understood this intellect and the origin and passing of beings,

1.44.s:
samavekṣya śanaiścaivaṃ labhate śamamuttamam /
guṇairvinaśyate buddirbuddherevendriyāṇyapi //
1.44.d:
समवेक्ष्य शनैश्चैवं लभते शममुत्तमम् ।
गुणैर्विनश्यते बुद्दिर्बुद्धेरेवेन्द्रियाण्यपि ॥
1.44.m: and reflecting thus gradually, attains supreme peace. / The intellect is destroyed by the qualities (guṇas), and the senses by the intellect.

1.44.s:
manaḥṣaṣṭāni bhūtāni buddhyabāve kuto guṇāḥ /
iti tanmayamevaitatsarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.44.d:
मनःषष्टानि भूतानि बुद्ध्यबावे कुतो गुणाः ।
इति तन्मयमेवैतत्सर्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.44.m: The elements have the mind as their sixth; in the absence of intellect, whence could the qualities arise? / Thus this entire universe of moving and unmoving beings is made of that.

1.44.s:
pralīyate codbhavati tasmānnirddiśyate tathā /
yena paśyati tañcakṣuḥ śṛṇoti śrotramucyate //
1.44.d:
प्रलीयते चोद्भवति तस्मान्निर्द्दिश्यते तथा ।
येन पश्यति तञ्चक्षुः शृणोति श्रोत्रमुच्यते ॥
1.44.m: It dissolves and emerges; therefore it is designated accordingly. / That by which one sees is the eye; that which hears is called the ear.

1.44.s:
jighrati ghrāṇamityāhuḥ rasaṃ jānāti jihvayā /
tvacā sparśayati sparśaṃ buddhirvikriyate sakṛt //
1.44.d:
जिघ्रति घ्राणमित्याहुः रसं जानाति जिह्वया ।
त्वचा स्पर्शयति स्पर्शं बुद्धिर्विक्रियते सकृत् ॥
1.44.m: They say that by which one smells is the olfactory organ; by the tongue one knows taste; / through the skin one perceives touch; the intellect undergoes modification each time.

1.44.s:
yena prārthayate kiñcittadā bhavati tanmanaḥ /
adhiṣṭānāttu buddherhi pṛthagarthāni pañcadhā //
1.44.d:
येन प्रार्थयते किञ्चित्तदा भवति तन्मनः ।
अधिष्टानात्तु बुद्धेर्हि पृथगर्थानि पञ्चधा ॥
1.44.m: That by which one desires anything is then the mind. / From the location of the intellect, indeed, the fivefold objects are distinct.

1.44.s:
indriyāṇīti tānyāhustānyadṛśyo 'dhitiṣṭati /
puruṣe tiṣṭatī buddhistriṣu bhāveṣu vartate //
1.44.d:
इन्द्रियाणीति तान्याहुस्तान्यदृश्यो ऽधितिष्टति ।
पुरुषे तिष्टती बुद्धिस्त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते ॥
1.44.m: These are called the senses; the unseen [Self] resides within them. / Residing in the person, the intellect operates in three states.

1.44.s:
kadācillabhate prītiṃ kadācidupaśocati /
na sukhena na duḥkhena kadācidapi vartate //
1.44.d:
कदाचिल्लभते प्रीतिं कदाचिदुपशोचति ।
न सुखेन न दुःखेन कदाचिदपि वर्तते ॥
1.44.m: Sometimes it experiences joy, sometimes it grieves; / and sometimes it abides in neither pleasure nor pain.

1.44.s:
evaṃ narāṇāṃ manasi triṣu bhāveṣu vartate /
seyaṃ bhāvātmikā bhāvāṃstrīnetānativartate //
1.44.d:
एवं नराणां मनसि त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते ।
सेयं भावात्मिका भावांस्त्रीनेतानतिवर्तते ॥
1.44.m: Thus in the mind of human beings it functions in three states; / this [intellect], which consists of these states, transcends these three states.

1.44.s:
saritāṃ sāgaro bhartā velānāmiva vāridhiḥ /
atibhāvagatā buddhirbhāvairmanasi vartate //
1.44.d:
सरितां सागरो भर्ता वेलानामिव वारिधिः ।
अतिभावगता बुद्धिर्भावैर्मनसि वर्तते ॥
1.44.m: Just as the ocean, the lord of rivers, [surpasses] its shorelines, / the intellect, having transcended states, operates in the mind through these states.

1.44.s:
vartamāno munistvevaṃ svabāvamanuvartate /
indriyāṇi hi sarvāṇi pravartayati sā sadā //
1.44.d:
वर्तमानो मुनिस्त्वेवं स्वबावमनुवर्तते ।
इन्द्रियाणि हि सर्वाणि प्रवर्तयति सा सदा ॥
1.44.m: Functioning thus, the sage conforms to his true nature; / for it always activates all the senses.

1.44.s:
prītiḥ sattvaṃ rajaḥ śokastamaḥ krodhastu te trayaḥ /
ye ye ca bhāvā loke 'sminsarve pyeteṣu vai triṣu //
1.44.d:
प्रीतिः सत्त्वं रजः शोकस्तमः क्रोधस्तु ते त्रयः ।
ये ये च भावा लोके ऽस्मिन्सर्वे प्येतेषु वै त्रिषु ॥
1.44.m: Joy is sattva, sorrow is rajas, and anger is tamas: these are the three; / and whatever states exist in this world, they all are indeed within these three.

1.44.s:
iti buddhigatāḥ sarvā vyākhyātāstava bhāvanāḥ /
indriyāṇi ca sarvāṇi vijetavyāni dhīmatā //
1.44.d:
इति बुद्धिगताः सर्वा व्याख्यातास्तव भावनाः ।
इन्द्रियाणि च सर्वाणि विजेतव्यानि धीमता ॥
1.44.m: Thus all the mental states belonging to the intellect have been explained to you; / and all the senses must be conquered by the wise person.

1.44.s:
sattvaṃ rajastamaścaiva prāṇināṃ saṃśritāḥ sadā /
triviśvāvedanāścaiva sarvasattveṣu dṛśyate //
1.44.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव प्राणिनां संश्रिताः सदा ।
त्रिविश्वावेदनाश्चैव सर्वसत्त्वेषु दृश्यते ॥
1.44.m: Sattva, rajas, and tamas are always situated in living beings; / and a threefold perception is seen in all creatures.

1.44.s:
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti mānada /
sukhasparśaḥ sattvaguṇo duḥkhasparśo rajoguṇaḥ //
1.44.d:
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति मानद ।
सुखस्पर्शः सत्त्वगुणो दुःखस्पर्शो रजोगुणः ॥
1.44.m: It is sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa, O giver of honor. / The quality of sattva is contact with pleasure; the quality of rajas is contact with pain.

1.44.s:
tamoguṇena saṃyuktau bhavato vyāvahārikau /
tava yatprītisaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet //
1.44.d:
तमोगुणेन संयुक्तौ भवतो व्यावहारिकौ ।
तव यत्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत् ॥
1.44.m: Coupled with the quality of tamas, both become worldly. / Whatever in you is accompanied by joy in the body or mind,

1.44.s:
vartate sāttviko bhāva ityācakṣīta tattathā /
atha yadduḥkhasaṃyuktamaprītikaramātmanaḥ //
1.44.d:
वर्तते सात्त्विको भाव इत्याचक्षीत तत्तथा ।
अथ यद्दुःखसंयुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः ॥
1.44.m: one should know to be functioning as a sāttvika state. / Now, whatever is accompanied by sorrow and causes displeasure to oneself,

1.44.s:
pravṛttaṃ raja ityeva jānīhi munisattama /
athayanmohasaṃyuktamavyakta viṣamaṃ bhavet //
1.44.d:
प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येव जानीहि मुनिसत्तम ।
अथयन्मोहसंयुक्तमव्यक्त विषमं भवेत् ॥
1.44.m: know that to have arisen from rajas, O best of sages. / And that which is accompanied by delusion, indistinct and unsteady,

1.44.s:
apratarkyamavijñeyaṃ tamastadupadhārayet /
praharṣaḥ prītirānandaḥ sukhaṃ vā śāntacittatā //
1.44.d:
अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत् ।
प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः सुखं वा शान्तचित्तता ॥
1.44.m: incomprehensible and unknowable, one should understand as tamas. / Exhilaration, delight, bliss, joy, or tranquillity of mind—

1.44.s:
kathañcidabhivartanta ityete sāttvikā guṇāḥ /
atuṣṭiḥ paritāpaśca śoko lobhastathā kṣamā //
1.44.d:
कथञ्चिदभिवर्तन्त इत्येते सात्त्विका गुणाः ।
अतुष्टिः परितापश्च शोको लोभस्तथा क्षमा ॥
1.44.m: if these arise in any way, these are the qualities of sattva. / Dissatisfaction, distress, sorrow, greed, and impatience—

1.44.s:
liṅgāni rajasastāni dṛśyante dehahetubhiḥ /
apamānastathā mohaḥ pramādaḥ svapnatandrite //
1.44.d:
लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि दृश्यन्ते देहहेतुभिः ।
अपमानस्तथा मोहः प्रमादः स्वप्नतन्द्रिते ॥
1.44.m: these marks of rajas are seen caused by bodily concerns. / Disrespect, delusion, negligence, sleep, and sluggishness—

1.44.s:
kathañcidabhivartante vividhāstāmasā guṇāḥ /
dūṣaṇaṃ bahudhāgāmi prārthanāsaṃśayātmakam //
1.44.d:
कथञ्चिदभिवर्तन्ते विविधास्तामसा गुणाः ।
दूषणं बहुधागामि प्रार्थनासंशयात्मकम् ॥
1.44.m: these diverse qualities of tamas manifest somehow. / The mind, which tends to run in many directions and consists of desire and doubt,

1.44.s:
manaḥ svaniyataṃ yasya sa sukhī pretyaceha ca /
sattvakṣetrajñayoretadantaraṃ yasya sūkṣmayoḥ //
1.44.d:
मनः स्वनियतं यस्य स सुखी प्रेत्यचेह च ।
सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेतदन्तरं यस्य सूक्ष्मयोः ॥
1.44.m: when restrained by oneself, brings happiness in this world and the next. / This is the distinction between the subtle sattva and the knower of the field:

1.44.s:
sṛjatehi guṇāneka eko na sṛjate guṇān /
maśakoduṃbarau vāpi saṃprayuktau yathā sadā //
1.44.d:
सृजतेहि गुणानेक एको न सृजते गुणान् ।
मशकोदुंबरौ वापि संप्रयुक्तौ यथा सदा ॥
1.44.m: the one creates the qualities; the other does not create qualities. / Just as a gnat and a fig are always conjoined,

1.44.s:
anyonyametau syātāṃ ca sapraṃyogastathobhayoḥ /
pṛthagbhūtau prakṛtyā tau sapraṃyuktau ca sarvadā //
1.44.d:
अन्योन्यमेतौ स्यातां च सप्रंयोगस्तथोभयोः ।
पृथग्भूतौ प्रकृत्या तौ सप्रंयुक्तौ च सर्वदा ॥
1.44.m: they may be mutual, and there is conjunction between both; / they are distinct by nature, and yet always conjoined.

1.44.s:
yathā matsyo jalaṃ caiva saṃprayukto tathaiva tau /
na guṇā vidurātmānaṃ sa guṇānvetti sarvaśaḥ //
1.44.d:
यथा मत्स्यो जलं चैव संप्रयुक्तो तथैव तौ ।
न गुणा विदुरात्मानं स गुणान्वेत्ति सर्वशः ॥
1.44.m: Just as a fish and water are conjoined, so indeed are the two. / The qualities do not know the Self; the Self knows the qualities entirely.

1.44.s:
paridraṣṭā guṇānāṃ tu saṃstraṣṭā manyate tathā /
indriyastu pradīpārthaṃ kurute buddhisattamaiḥ //
1.44.d:
परिद्रष्टा गुणानां तु संस्त्रष्टा मन्यते तथा ।
इन्द्रियस्तु प्रदीपार्थं कुरुते बुद्धिसत्तमैः ॥
1.44.m: It is the spectator of the qualities, yet is regarded as the creator. / The sense organ acts like a lamp through the best functions of the intellect.

1.44.s:
nirviceṣṭairajānadbhiḥ paramātmā pradīpavān /
sṛjate hi guṇānsattvaṃ kṣetrajñaḥ paripaśyati //
1.44.d:
निर्विचेष्टैरजानद्भिः परमात्मा प्रदीपवान् ।
सृजते हि गुणान्सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञः परिपश्यति ॥
1.44.m: For them who are motionless and unknowing, the Supreme Self serves as a lamp. / For sattva produces the qualities, and the knower of the field beholds them.

1.44.s:
saṃprayogastayoreṣa sattvakṣetrajñayordhruvam /
āśrayo nāsti sattvasya kṣetrajñasya ca kaścana //
1.44.d:
संप्रयोगस्तयोरेष सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ध्रुवम् ।
आश्रयो नास्ति सत्त्वस्य क्षेत्रज्ञस्य च कश्चन ॥
1.44.m: This connection between the two, sattva and the knower of the field, is constant. / There is no other support for sattva, nor for the knower of the field.

1.44.s:
sattvaṃ manaḥ saṃsṛjate na guṇānvai kadācana /
raśmīṃsteṣāṃ sa manasā yadā samyaṅniyacchati //
1.44.d:
सत्त्वं मनः संसृजते न गुणान्वै कदाचन ।
रश्मींस्तेषां स मनसा यदा सम्यङ्नियच्छति ॥
1.44.m: Sattva produces the mind, never the qualities. / When one properly restrains their reins with the mind,

1.44.s:
tadā prakāśate 'syātmā ghaṭe dīpo jvalanniva /
tyaktvā yaḥ prākṛtaṃ karma nityamātmaratirmuniḥ //
1.44.d:
तदा प्रकाशते ऽस्यात्मा घटे दीपो ज्वलन्निव ।
त्यक्त्वा यः प्राकृतं कर्म नित्यमात्मरतिर्मुनिः ॥
1.44.m: then one's Self shines like a lamp burning in a pot. / The sage who has renounced material action, who constantly delights in the Self,

1.44.s:
sarvabhūtātmabhūstasmātsa gaccheduttamāṃ gatim /
yathā vāricaraḥ pakṣī salilena na lipyate //
1.44.d:
सर्वभूतात्मभूस्तस्मात्स गच्छेदुत्तमां गतिम् ।
यथा वारिचरः पक्षी सलिलेन न लिप्यते ॥
1.44.m: and who has become the Self of all beings, will therefore attain the supreme state. / Just as an aquatic bird is not smeared by water,

1.44.s:
evameva kṛtaprajño bhūteṣu parivartate /
evaṃ svabhāvamevaitatsvabuddhyā viharennaraḥ //
1.44.d:
एवमेव कृतप्रज्ञो भूतेषु परिवर्तते ।
एवं स्वभावमेवैतत्स्वबुद्ध्या विहरेन्नरः ॥
1.44.m: in the very same way a person of steady wisdom moves among living beings. / Thus a person should live in accordance with true nature through their own intellect,

1.44.s:
aśocannaprahṛṣyaṃśca samo vigatamatsaraḥ /
bhāvayuktyā prayuktastu sa nityaṃ sṛjate guṇān //
1.44.d:
अशोचन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च समो विगतमत्सरः ।
