भावयुक्त्या प्रयुक्तस्तु स नित्यं सृजते गुणान् ॥
1.44.m: neither grieving nor rejoicing, even-minded and free from malice. / Employed through the conjunction of mental states, it constantly creates qualities.

1.44.s:
ūrṇanābhiryathā sūtraṃ vijñeyāstantuvadguṇāḥ /
pradhvastā na nivartante nivṛttirnopalabhyate //
1.44.d:
ऊर्णनाभिर्यथा सूत्रं विज्ञेयास्तन्तुवद्गुणाः ।
प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते निवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते ॥
1.44.m: Just as a spider produces thread, the qualities should be known like threads; / once destroyed, they do not return, nor is their cessation directly perceived.

1.44.s:
pratyakṣeṇa parokṣaṃ tadanumānena siddhyati /
evameke vyavasyanti nivṛttiriti cāpare //
1.44.d:
प्रत्यक्षेण परोक्षं तदनुमानेन सिद्ध्यति ।
एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे ॥
1.44.m: That which is beyond direct perception is established by inference. / Some conclude in this way, while others hold cessation [as the truth].

1.44.s:
ubhayaṃ saṃpradhāryaitadvyavasyeta yathāmati /
itīmaṃ hṛdayagrathiṃ buddhicintāmayaṃ dṛḍham //
1.44.d:
उभयं संप्रधार्यैतद्व्यवस्येत यथामति ।
इतीमं हृदयग्रथिं बुद्धिचिन्तामयं दृढम् ॥
1.44.m: Having deliberated upon both, one should make a resolution according to one's wisdom. / Having thus untied this firm knot of the heart composed of intellect and anxiety,

1.44.s:
vimucya sukhamāsīta na śocecchinnasaṃśavaḥ /
malināḥ prāṇnuyuḥ śuddhiṃ yathā pūrṇāṃ nadīṃ narāḥ //
1.44.d:
विमुच्य सुखमासीत न शोचेच्छिन्नसंशवः ।
मलिनाः प्राण्नुयुः शुद्धिं यथा पूर्णां नदीं नराः ॥
1.44.m: one should sit happily and not grieve, with doubts severed. / Just as impure people attain purity [by entering] a full river,

1.44.s:
avagāhya suvidvāṃso viddhi jñānabhide tathā /
mahānadyā hi pārajñastapyate na taranyathā //
1.44.d:
अवगाह्य सुविद्वांसो विद्धि ज्ञानभिदे तथा ।
महानद्या हि पारज्ञस्तप्यते न तरन्यथा ॥
1.44.m: having bathed in it, so know the wise to attain purity through the distinction of knowledge. / For one who knows the other shore of a great river is not afflicted while crossing it;

1.44.s:
na tu tapyati tattvajñaḥ kulajñastu taratyuta /
evaṃ ye viduradhyātmaṃ kaivalyaṃ jñānamuttamam //
1.44.d:
न तु तप्यति तत्त्वज्ञः कुलज्ञस्तु तरत्युत ।
एवं ये विदुरध्यात्मं कैवल्यं ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥
1.44.m: nor is the knower of truth afflicted, and one who knows the riverbanks crosses safely. / Thus those who know the inner Self attain solitary liberation, the supreme knowledge.

1.44.s:
evaṃ buddhā naraḥ sarvo bhūtānāmagatiṃ gatim /
avekṣya ca śanairbuddhyā labhate ca śamaṃ tataḥ //
1.44.d:
एवं बुद्धा नरः सर्वो भूतानामगतिं गतिम् ।
अवेक्ष्य च शनैर्बुद्ध्या लभते च शमं ततः ॥
1.44.m: Having thus understood the departure and arrival of living beings, / and having perceived it slowly through intellect, a person thereupon attains peace.

1.44.s:
trivargo yasya viditaḥ prekṣya yaśca vimuñcati /
anviṣya manasā yuktastattvadarśī nirutsukaḥ //
1.44.d:
त्रिवर्गो यस्य विदितः प्रेक्ष्य यश्च विमुञ्चति ।
अन्विष्य मनसा युक्तस्तत्त्वदर्शी निरुत्सुकः ॥
1.44.m: The one by whom the three ends of life are understood, who beholds and abandons [attachment], / seeking with a disciplined mind, sees the truth and is devoid of longing.

1.44.s:
na cātmā śakyate draṣṭumindriyeṣu vibhāgaśaḥ /
tatra tatra visṛṣṭeṣu durvāpeṣvakṛtātmābhiḥ //
1.44.d:
न चात्मा शक्यते द्रष्टुमिन्द्रियेषु विभागशः ।
तत्र तत्र विसृष्टेषु दुर्वापेष्वकृतात्माभिः ॥
1.44.m: The Self cannot be seen separately among the senses, / scattered here and there, difficult to attain by undisciplined minds.

1.44.s:
etad buddhā bhaved buddhaḥ kimanyad buddhalakṣaṇam /
vijñāya taddhi manyante katakṛtyā manīṣiṇaḥ //
1.44.d:
एतद् बुद्धा भवेद् बुद्धः किमन्यद् बुद्धलक्षणम् ।
विज्ञाय तद्धि मन्यन्ते कतकृत्या मनीषिणः ॥
1.44.m: Having understood this, one becomes awakened; what other mark of the awakened is there? / Indeed, having known that, the wise consider their purpose accomplished.

1.44.s:
na bhavati viduṣāṃ tato bhayaṃ yadaviduṣāṃ sumahadbhayaṃ bhavet /
nahi gatiradhikāsti kasyacitsati hi guṇepravadatyatulyatām //
1.44.d:
न भवति विदुषां ततो भयं यदविदुषां सुमहद्भयं भवेत् ।
नहि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचित्सति हि गुणेप्रवदत्यतुल्यताम् ॥
1.44.m: There is no fear for the wise from that which causes immense fear to the ignorant; / for there is no higher path for anyone, since when a quality is present, it reveals inequality.

1.44.s:
yaḥ karotyanabhisaṃdhipūrvakaṃ tacca nirdahati yatpurākṛtam /
nāpriyaṃ tadubhayaṃ kutaḥ priyaṃ tasya tajjanayatīha kurvataḥ //
1.44.d:
यः करोत्यनभिसंधिपूर्वकं तच्च निर्दहति यत्पुराकृतम् ।
नाप्रियं तदुभयं कुतः प्रियं तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वतः ॥
1.44.m: That which one performs without selfish intention burns up what was done in the past; / neither unpleasant nor pleasant is produced here for one who acts thus—whence could it arise?

1.44.s:
lokamāyurabhisūyate janastasya tajjanayatīha kurvantaḥ /
tatra paśya kuśalānna śocate jāyate yadi bhayaṃ padaṃ sadā //
1.44.d:
लोकमायुरभिसूयते जनस्तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वन्तः ।
तत्र पश्य कुशलान्न शोचते जायते यदि भयं पदं सदा ॥
1.44.m: People revile [their allotted] life in this world; it produces that for one who acts in this world. / Behold there: the skilled person does not grieve if the state of fear arises continually.

1.44.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
dhyānayogaṃ samācakṣvamahyaṃ tatpadasiddhaye /
yajjñātvā mucyate brahmannarastrividhatāpataḥ //
1.44.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
ध्यानयोगं समाचक्ष्वमह्यं तत्पदसिद्धये ।
यज्ज्ञात्वा मुच्यते ब्रह्मन्नरस्त्रिविधतापतः ॥
1.44.m: Bharadvāja said: / Explain to me the yoga of meditation for attaining that state, / knowing which, O holy one, a human being is freed from the threefold suffering.

1.44.s:
bhṛguruvāca
hṝnta te saṃpravakṣyāmi jñānayogaṃ caturvidham /
yaṃ jñātvā śāśvatīṃ siddhiṃ gacchantīha maharṣayaḥ //
1.44.d:
भृगुरुवाच
हॄन्त ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञानयोगं चतुर्विधम् ।
यं ज्ञात्वा शाश्वतीं सिद्धिं गच्छन्तीह महर्षयः ॥
1.44.m:
Bhṛgu said:
Listen! I shall explain to you the fourfold yoga of knowledge, / knowing which the great sages attain eternal perfection in this world.

1.44.s:
yathā svanuṣṭitaṃ dhyānaṃ tathā kurvanti yoginaḥ /
maharṣayo jñānatṛptā nirvāṇagatamānasāḥ //
1.44.d:
यथा स्वनुष्टितं ध्यानं तथा कुर्वन्ति योगिनः ।
महर्षयो ज्ञानतृप्ता निर्वाणगतमानसाः ॥
1.44.m: Yogins practice meditation just as it is prescribed, / [and become] great sages satisfied through knowledge, with their minds dissolved in nirvāṇa.

1.44.s:
nāvartante punaścāpi muktāḥ saṃsāradoṣataḥ /
janmadoṣapārīkṣīṇāḥ svabhāve paryavasthitāḥ //
1.44.d:
नावर्तन्ते पुनश्चापि मुक्ताः संसारदोषतः ।
जन्मदोषपारीक्षीणाः स्वभावे पर्यवस्थिताः ॥
1.44.m: They do not return again, freed from the defects of worldly existence; / with the defect of rebirth destroyed, they abide established in their own nature.

1.44.s:
nirdvandvā nityasattvasthā vimuktā niṣparigrahāḥ /
asaṃgānya vidhādīni manaḥ śāntikarāṇi ca //
1.44.d:
निर्द्वन्द्वा नित्यसत्त्वस्था विमुक्ता निष्परिग्रहाः ।
असंगान्य विधादीनि मनः शान्तिकराणि च ॥
1.44.m: Free from dualities, ever established in sattva, liberated, devoid of possessions, / [they cultivate] unattached practices and the like, which pacify the mind.

1.44.s:
tatra dhyānena saṃkliṣṭamekāgraṃ dhārayenmanaḥ /
piṇḍīkṛtyendriyagrāmamāsīnaḥ kāṣṭavanmuniḥ //
1.44.d:
तत्र ध्यानेन संक्लिष्टमेकाग्रं धारयेन्मनः ।
पिण्डीकृत्येन्द्रियग्राममासीनः काष्टवन्मुनिः ॥
1.44.m: Restrained by meditation, the sage, seated like a piece of wood, / drawing together the group of senses, should hold the mind one-pointed.

1.44.s:
śabdaṃ na vindecchrotreṇa tvacā sparśaṃ na vedayet /
rūpaṃ na cakṣuṣā vindyājjihvayā na rasāṃstathā //
1.44.d:
शब्दं न विन्देच्छ्रोत्रेण त्वचा स्पर्शं न वेदयेत् ।
रूपं न चक्षुषा विन्द्याज्जिह्वया न रसांस्तथा ॥
1.44.m: He should not perceive sound with the ear, nor feel touch with the skin; / he should not perceive form with the eye, nor tastes with the tongue.

1.44.s:
ghroyāṇyapi ca sarvāṇi jahyāddhyānena tattvavit /
pañcavargapramāthīni neccheñcaitāni vīryavān //
1.44.d:
घ्रोयाण्यपि च सर्वाणि जह्याद्ध्यानेन तत्त्ववित् ।
पञ्चवर्गप्रमाथीनि नेच्छेञ्चैतानि वीर्यवान् ॥
1.44.m: The knower of truth, through meditation, should also abandon all smells; / powerful, he should not desire these that torment the group of five.

1.44.s:
tato manasi saṃgṛhya pañcavargaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ /
samādadhyānmano bhrāntamindriyaiḥ saha pañcabhiḥ //
1.44.d:
ततो मनसि संगृह्य पञ्चवर्गं विचक्षणः ।
समादध्यान्मनो भ्रान्तमिन्द्रियैः सह पञ्चभिः ॥
1.44.m: Then, gathering the group of five into the mind, the wise man / should concentrate the wandering mind together with the five senses.

1.44.s:
visañcāri nirālambaṃ pañcadvāraṃ balābalam /
pūrvadhyānapathe dhīraḥ samādadhyānmanastvarā //
1.44.d:
विसञ्चारि निरालम्बं पञ्चद्वारं बलाबलम् ।
पूर्वध्यानपथे धीरः समादध्यान्मनस्त्वरा ॥
1.44.m: The steadfast man should promptly concentrate upon the path of primary meditation the mind, / which wanders about, lacks support, has five gates, and fluctuates in strength.

1.44.s:
indriyāṇi manaścaiva yadā piṇḍīkarotyayam /
eṣa dhyānapathaḥ pūrvo bhayā samanuvarṇitaḥ //
1.44.d:
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव यदा पिण्डीकरोत्ययम् ।
एष ध्यानपथः पूर्वो भया समनुवर्णितः ॥
1.44.m: When he draws together the senses and the mind, / this is the primary path of meditation that has been described by me.

1.44.s:
tasya tatpūrvasaṃruddha ātmaṣaṣṭhamanantaram /
sphuriṣyati samudrāntā vidyudambudhare yathā //
1.44.d:
तस्य तत्पूर्वसंरुद्ध आत्मषष्ठमनन्तरम् ।
स्फुरिष्यति समुद्रान्ता विद्युदम्बुधरे यथा ॥
1.44.m: To him, when that [mind] with the self as sixth has subsequently been restrained, / it will flash at the edge of the ocean like lightning in a rain-cloud.

1.44.s:
jalabinduryathā lolaḥ parṇasthaḥ sarvataścalaḥ /
evamevāsya cittaṃ ca bhavati dhyānavartmani //
1.44.d:
जलबिन्दुर्यथा लोलः पर्णस्थः सर्वतश्चलः ।
एवमेवास्य चित्तं च भवति ध्यानवर्त्मनि ॥
1.44.m: Just as a drop of water on a leaf is restless and moving in all directions, / in the very same way does his mind become on the path of meditation.

1.44.s:
samāhitaṃ kṣaṇaṃ kiñjiddhyānavartmani tiṣṭati /
punarvāyupathaṃ bhrāntaṃ mano bhavati vāyuvat //
1.44.d:
समाहितं क्षणं किञ्जिद्ध्यानवर्त्मनि तिष्टति ।
पुनर्वायुपथं भ्रान्तं मनो भवति वायुवत् ॥
1.44.m: For a moment it stays concentrated somewhat on the path of meditation; / then the wandering mind again enters the path of the wind, like the wind itself.

1.44.s:
anirvedo gatakleśo gatatandro hyamatsarī /
samādadhyātpunaśceto dhyānena dhyānayogavit //
1.44.d:
अनिर्वेदो गतक्लेशो गततन्द्रो ह्यमत्सरी ।
समादध्यात्पुनश्चेतो ध्यानेन ध्यानयोगवित् ॥
1.44.m: Free from despondency, with distress gone, with sluggishness gone, free from envy, / the knower of dhyāna-yoga should concentrate the mind again through meditation.

1.44.s:
vicāraśca vitarkaśca vivekaścopajāyate /
muneḥ samādhiyuktasya prathamaṃ dhyānamāditaḥ //
1.44.d:
विचारश्च वितर्कश्च विवेकश्चोपजायते ।
मुनेः समाधियुक्तस्य प्रथमं ध्यानमादितः ॥
1.44.m: Deliberation, reflection, and discernment arise / from the very beginning in the first meditation of the sage engaged in samādhi.

1.44.s:
manasā kliśyamānastu samādhānaṃ ca kārayet /
na nirvedaṃ munirgacchetkuryādevātmano hitam //
1.44.d:
मनसा क्लिश्यमानस्तु समाधानं च कारयेत् ।
न निर्वेदं मुनिर्गच्छेत्कुर्यादेवात्मनो हितम् ॥
1.44.m: Even when afflicted by the mind, he should effect concentration; / the sage should not fall into despondency, but should work for his own welfare.

1.44.s:
pāṃśubhasmakarīṣāṇāṃ yathā vai rāśayaścitāḥ /
sahasā vāriṇā siktā na yānti paribhāvanāḥ //
1.44.d:
पांशुभस्मकरीषाणां यथा वै राशयश्चिताः ।
सहसा वारिणा सिक्ता न यान्ति परिभावनाः ॥
1.44.m: Just as heaps of dust, ashes, and dry cow-dung that have been gathered / do not become thoroughly moistened when suddenly sprinkled with water,

1.44.s:
kiñcit snigdhaṃ yathā ca syācchuṣkaṃ cūrṇamabhāvitam /
krameṇa tu śanairgacchatsarvaṃ tatparibhāvanam //
1.44.d:
किञ्चित् स्निग्धं यथा च स्याच्छुष्कं चूर्णमभावितम् ।
क्रमेण तु शनैर्गच्छत्सर्वं तत्परिभावनम् ॥
1.44.m: and just as dry unsoaked powder remains partially dry, / but by degrees, going slowly, all of it becomes thoroughly permeated,

1.44.s:
evamevendriyagrāmaṃ śanaiḥ śaṃ paribhāvayet /
saṃharetkramaśaścaiva samyak tatpraśamiṣyati //
1.44.d:
एवमेवेन्द्रियग्रामं शनैः शं परिभावयेत् ।
संहरेत्क्रमशश्चैव सम्यक् तत्प्रशमिष्यति ॥
1.44.m: in the very same way one should gradually discipline the group of senses; / and one should withdraw it by degrees; it will become completely pacified.

1.44.s:
svayameva manaścaivaṃ pañcavargaṃ munīśvara /
pūrvaṃ dhyānapathe sthāpya nityayogena śāmyati //
1.44.d:
स्वयमेव मनश्चैवं पञ्चवर्गं मुनीश्वर ।
पूर्वं ध्यानपथे स्थाप्य नित्ययोगेन शाम्यति ॥
1.44.m: O lord of sages, having first established the mind and the group of five / on the path of meditation, it becomes pacified of its own accord through constant practice.

1.44.s:
na tatpuruṣakāreṇa na ca daivena kenacit /
sukhameṣyati tattasya yadevaṃ saṃyatātmanaḥ //
1.44.d:
न तत्पुरुषकारेण न च दैवेन केनचित् ।
सुखमेष्यति तत्तस्य यदेवं संयतात्मनः ॥
1.44.m: Not by human effort nor by any fate / does that bliss come to him, except when he is thus self-controlled.

1.44.s:
sukhena tena saṃyukto raṃsyate dhyānakarmaṇi /
gacchanti yogino hyovaṃ nirvāṇaṃ tu nirāmayam //
1.44.d:
सुखेन तेन संयुक्तो रंस्यते ध्यानकर्मणि ।
गच्छन्ति योगिनो ह्योवं निर्वाणं तु निरामयम् ॥
1.44.m: Endowed with that bliss, he will delight in the practice of meditation; / for yogins thus attain nirvāṇa free from affliction.

1.44.s:
sanandana uvāca
ityukto bhṛguṇā brahmanbharadvājaḥ pratāpavān /
bhṛguṃ paramadharmātmā vismitaḥ pratyapūjayat //
1.44.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
इत्युक्तो भृगुणा ब्रह्मन्भरद्वाजः प्रतापवान् ।
भृगुं परमधर्मात्मा विस्मितः प्रत्यपूजयत् ॥
1.44.m:
Sanandana said:
Addressed in this way by Bhṛgu, O brāhmaṇa, the glorious Bharadvāja, / supreme in righteousness, full of wonder, worshipped Bhṛgu in return.

1.44.s:
eṣa te prasavo vidvan jagataḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ /
nikhilena mahāprājña kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe dvitīyapāde catuścatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.44.d:
एष ते प्रसवो विद्वन् जगतः संप्रकीर्तितः ।
निखिलेन महाप्राज्ञ किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे द्वितीयपादे चतुश्चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.44.m:
This origin of the world has been proclaimed to you in full, O wise one; / O greatly intelligent one, what more do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter in the second part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.45.s:
sūta uvāca
sanandanavacaḥ śrutvā mokṣadharmāśritaṃ dvijāḥ /
punaḥ papraccha tattvajño nārado 'dhyātmasatkathām //
1.45.d:
सूत उवाच
सनन्दनवचः श्रुत्वा मोक्षधर्माश्रितं द्विजाः ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ तत्त्वज्ञो नारदो ऽध्यात्मसत्कथाम् ॥
1.45.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard Sanandana's words concerning the doctrine of liberation, O twice-born ones, / Nārada, the knower of truth, again asked about the sacred discourse on the inner self.

1.45.s:
nārada uvāca
śrutaṃ mayā mahābhāga mokṣaśāstraṃ tvayoditam /
na ca me jāyate tṛptirbhūyobhūyo 'pi śṛṇvataḥ //
1.45.d:
नारद उवाच
श्रुतं मया महाभाग मोक्षशास्त्रं त्वयोदितम् ।
न च मे जायते तृप्तिर्भूयोभूयो ऽपि शृण्वतः ॥
1.45.m:
Nārada said:
I have heard, O fortunate one, the treatise on liberation spoken by you; / yet my satiety does not arise, even as I listen again and again.

1.45.s:
yathā saṃmucyate janturavidyābandhanānmune /
tathā kathaya sarvajña mokṣadharmaṃ sadāśritam //
1.45.d:
यथा संमुच्यते जन्तुरविद्याबन्धनान्मुने ।
तथा कथय सर्वज्ञ मोक्षधर्मं सदाश्रितम् ॥
1.45.m: O sage, tell me how an embodied soul is completely freed from the bondage of ignorance; / O omniscient one, tell me the everlasting doctrine of liberation.

1.45.s:
sanandana uvāca
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
yathā mokṣamanuprāpto janako mithilādhipaḥ //
1.45.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
यथा मोक्षमनुप्राप्तो जनको मिथिलाधिपः ॥
1.45.m:
Sanandana said:
Concerning this, they also cite this ancient narrative / of how Janaka, the ruler of Mithilā, attained liberation.

1.45.s:
janako janadevastu mithilāyā adhīśvaraḥ /
aurdhvadehikadharmāṇāmāsīdyukto vicintane //
1.45.d:
जनको जनदेवस्तु मिथिलाया अधीश्वरः ।
और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणामासीद्युक्तो विचिन्तने ॥
1.45.m: Janaka Janadeva, the ruler of Mithilā, / was intent upon pondering duties concerning the afterlife.

1.45.s:
tasya śmaśāna mācāryā vasati satataṃ gṛhe /
darśayantaḥ pṛthagdharmānnānāpāṣañjavādinaḥ //
1.45.d:
तस्य श्मशान माचार्या वसति सततं गृहे ।
दर्शयन्तः पृथग्धर्मान्नानापाषञ्जवादिनः ॥
1.45.m: In his house there constantly lived a hundred teachers, / teachers of various heterodox doctrines, expounding different paths.

1.45.s:
sa teṣāṃ pretyabhāve ca pretya jātau viniścaye /
ādamasthaḥ sa bhūyiṣṭamātmatattvena tuṣaayati //
1.45.d:
स तेषां प्रेत्यभावे च प्रेत्य जातौ विनिश्चये ।
आदमस्थः स भूयिष्टमात्मतत्त्वेन तुषअयति ॥
1.45.m: Regarding their determination of life after death and rebirth after dying, / he, remaining within his own control, was mostly not satisfied with their doctrine of the self.

1.45.s:
tatra pañcaśikho nāma kāpileyo mahāmuniḥ /
paridhāvanmahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ jagāma mithilāmatha //
1.45.d:
तत्र पञ्चशिखो नाम कापिलेयो महामुनिः ।
परिधावन्महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम मिथिलामथ ॥
1.45.m: Then the great sage named Pañcaśikha, the son of Kapilā, / wandering over the whole earth, arrived at Mithilā.

1.45.s:
sarvasaṃnyāsadharmāṇaḥ tattvajñānaviniścaye /
suparyavasitārthaśca nirdvandvo naṣṭasaṃśayaḥ //
1.45.d:
सर्वसंन्यासधर्माणः तत्त्वज्ञानविनिश्चये ।
सुपर्यवसितार्थश्च निर्द्वन्द्वो नष्टसंशयः ॥
1.45.m: Practicing the duties of total renunciation, in the determination of the knowledge of truth / his purpose was thoroughly achieved; he was free from dualities, his doubts destroyed.

1.45.s:
ṛṣīṇāmāhurekaṃ yaṃ kāmādavasitaṃ nṛṣu /
śāśvataṃ sukhamatyantamanvicchansa sudurlabham //
1.45.d:
ऋषीणामाहुरेकं यं कामादवसितं नृषु ।
शाश्वतं सुखमत्यन्तमन्विच्छन्स सुदुर्लभम् ॥
1.45.m: Among the sages they speak of him as the singular one among men who transcended desire, / seeking eternal, ultimate bliss, which is exceedingly difficult to attain.

1.45.s:
yamāhuḥ kapilaṃ sāṃkhyāḥ paramarṣi prajāpatim /
sa manye tena rūpeṇa vikhyāpayati hi svayam //
1.45.d:
यमाहुः कपिलं सांख्याः परमर्षि प्रजापतिम् ।
स मन्ये तेन रूपेण विख्यापयति हि स्वयम् ॥
1.45.m: He whom the Sāṃkhyas call Kapila, the supreme sage and progenitor— / he himself, I think, makes himself known in that form.

1.45.s:
āsureḥ prathamaṃ śiṣyaṃ yamāhuścirajīvinam /
pañcasrotasi yaḥ satramāste varṣasahasrakam //
1.45.d:
आसुरेः प्रथमं शिष्यं यमाहुश्चिरजीविनम् ।
पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रमास्ते वर्षसहस्रकम् ॥
1.45.m: He whom they call the long-lived first disciple of Āsuri, / who performed a sacrificial session for a thousand years at Pañcasrotas—

1.45.s:
pañcasrotasamāgamya kāpilaṃ maṇḍalaṃ mahat /
puruṣāvasthamavyaṅktaṃ paramārthaṃ nyavedayat //
1.45.d:
पञ्चस्रोतसमागम्य कापिलं मण्डलं महत् ।
पुरुषावस्थमव्यङ्क्तं परमार्थं न्यवेदयत् ॥
1.45.m: having arrived at Pañcasrotas, he imparted the supreme truth, / the great Sāṃkhya circle, the unmanifest condition of Puruṣa.

1.45.s:
iṣṭimantreṇa saṃyukto bhūyaśca tapasāsuriḥ /
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorvyaktiṃ vibudhe dehadarśanaḥ //
1.45.d:
इष्टिमन्त्रेण संयुक्तो भूयश्च तपसासुरिः ।
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्व्यक्तिं विबुधे देहदर्शनः ॥
1.45.m: Endowed with sacrificial mantras and further through austerity, Āsuri, / discerning the body, understood the manifestation of the field and the knower of the field.

1.45.s:
yattadekākṣaraṃ brahma nānārūpaṃ pradṛśyate /
āsurirmaṇḍale tasminpratipede tamavyayam //
1.45.d:
यत्तदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म नानारूपं प्रदृश्यते ।
आसुरिर्मण्डले तस्मिन्प्रतिपेदे तमव्ययम् ॥
1.45.m: That which is the single-syllabled Brahman perceived as multiform— / that imperishable [reality] Āsuri realized in that circle.

1.45.s:
tasya pañcaśikhaḥ śiṣyo mānuṣyā payasā bhṛtaḥ /
brāhmaṇī kapilī nāma kācidāsītkuṭumbinī //
1.45.d:
तस्य पञ्चशिखः शिष्यो मानुष्या पयसा भृतः ।
ब्राह्मणी कपिली नाम काचिदासीत्कुटुम्बिनी ॥
1.45.m: Pañcaśikha was his disciple, nourished with human milk; / there was a certain brāhmaṇa householder woman named Kapilā.

1.45.s:
tasyaḥ putratvamāgatya sriyāḥ sa pibagati stanau /
tataśca kāpileyatvaṃ lebhe buddhiṃ ca naiṣṭikīm //
1.45.d:
तस्यः पुत्रत्वमागत्य स्रियाः स पिबगति स्तनौ ।
ततश्च कापिलेयत्वं लेभे बुद्धिं च नैष्टिकीम् ॥
1.45.m: Becoming her son, he drank from the woman's breasts; / and from that he obtained the status of Kapilā's son and resolute intellect.

1.45.s:
etanme bhagavānāha kāpileyasya saṃbhavam /
tasya tatkāpileyatvaṃ sarvavittvamanuttamam //
1.45.d:
एतन्मे भगवानाह कापिलेयस्य संभवम् ।
तस्य तत्कापिलेयत्वं सर्ववित्त्वमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.45.m: The lord told me this origin of Kapilā's son; / hence his status as son of Kapilā and his unsurpassed omniscience.

1.45.s:
sāmātyo janako jñātvā dharmajño jñāninaṃ mune /
upetya śatamācāryānmohayāmāsa hetubhiḥ //
1.45.d:
सामात्यो जनको ज्ञात्वा धर्मज्ञो ज्ञानिनं मुने ।
उपेत्य शतमाचार्यान्मोहयामास हेतुभिः ॥
1.45.m: Janaka, the knower of righteousness, learning together with his ministers of this wise man, O sage, / approached [him, who] confounded the hundred teachers with arguments.

1.45.s:
janakastvabhisaṃraktaḥ kāpi leyānudarśanam /
utsṛjya śatamācāryāmpṛṣṭato 'nujagāma tam //
1.45.d:
जनकस्त्वभिसंरक्तः कापि लेयानुदर्शनम् ।
उत्सृज्य शतमाचार्याम्पृष्टतो ऽनुजगाम तम् ॥
1.45.m: Janaka, deeply attached to the philosophical system of Kapilā's son, / abandoned the hundred teachers and followed after him.

1.45.s:
tasmai paramakalyāṇaṃ praṇatāya ca dharmataḥ /
abravītparamaṃ mokṣaṃ yattatsāṃkhyaṃ vidhīyate //
1.45.d:
तस्मै परमकल्याणं प्रणताय च धर्मतः ।
अब्रवीत्परमं मोक्षं यत्तत्सांख्यं विधीयते ॥
1.45.m: To him, bowed in accordance with righteousness, he expounded the supreme good, / the ultimate liberation which is known as Sāṃkhya.

1.45.s:
jātinirvedamuktvā sa karmanirvedamabravīt /
karmanirvedamuktvā ca sarvanirvedamabravīt //
1.45.d:
जातिनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा स कर्मनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् ।
कर्मनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा च सर्वनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् ॥
1.45.m: Having spoken of disillusionment with birth, he spoke of disillusionment with action; / and having spoken of disillusionment with action, he spoke of disillusionment with all.

1.45.s:
yadarthaṃ dharmasaṃsargaḥ karmaṇāṃ ca phalo dayaḥ /
tamanāśvāsikaṃ mohaṃ vināśi calamadhruvam //
1.45.d:
यदर्थं धर्मसंसर्गः कर्मणां च फलो दयः ।
तमनाश्वासिकं मोहं विनाशि चलमध्रुवम् ॥
1.45.m: That for the sake of which there is connection with dharma and the rising of the fruits of actions, / that [very object] is devoid of solace, delusion, perishable, unsteady, and transient.

1.45.s:
dṛśyamāne vināśe ca pratyakṣe lokasākṣike /
āgamātparamastīti bruvannapi parājitaḥ //
1.45.d:
दृश्यमाने विनाशे च प्रत्यक्षे लोकसाक्षिके ।
आगमात्परमस्तीति ब्रुवन्नपि पराजितः ॥
1.45.m: And when destruction is seen directly, witnessed by the world, / even one who asserts from scripture, 'The supreme exists,' is defeated.

1.45.s:
anātmā hyātmano mṛtyuḥ kleśo mṛtyurjarāmayaḥ /
ātmānaṃ manyate mohāttadasamyak paraṃ matam //
1.45.d:
अनात्मा ह्यात्मनो मृत्युः क्लेशो मृत्युर्जरामयः ।
आत्मानं मन्यते मोहात्तदसम्यक् परं मतम् ॥
1.45.m: For death is not the Self, affliction is death, as are old age and disease; / out of delusion one considers [the body] to be the Self; that is considered an erroneous view.

1.45.s:
atha cedevamapyasti yalloke nopapadyate /
ajaro 'yamamṛtyuśca rājāsau manyate yathā //
1.45.d:
अथ चेदेवमप्यस्ति यल्लोके नोपपद्यते ।
अजरो ऽयममृत्युश्च राजासौ मन्यते यथा ॥
1.45.m: Now, even if this is so, which does not hold true in the world, / [it is] just as this king considers, 'I am ageless and deathless.'

1.45.s:
asti nāstīti cāpyetattasminnasitalakṣaṇe /
kimadhiṣṭāya tad brūyāllokayātrāviniścayam //
1.45.d:
अस्ति नास्तीति चाप्येतत्तस्मिन्नसितलक्षणे ।
किमधिष्टाय तद् ब्रूयाल्लोकयात्राविनिश्चयम् ॥
1.45.m: Regarding that which is characterized by unclarity as to whether 'it is' or 'it is not,' / relying on what could one declare a settled conclusion regarding the ways of the world?

1.45.s:
pratyakṣaṃ hyetayormūlaṃ kṛtānta hyetayorapi /
pratyakṣo hyāgamo bhinnaḥ kṛtānto vā na kiñcana //
1.45.d:
प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतयोर्मूलं कृतान्त ह्येतयोरपि ।
प्रत्यक्षो ह्यागमो भिन्नः कृतान्तो वा न किञ्चन ॥
1.45.m: Perception indeed is the root of these two, and the settled conclusion also belongs to them; / for perception contradicted by scripture, or a settled doctrine [contrary to perception], is nothing at all.

1.45.s:
yatra tatrānumāne 'sminkṛtaṃ bhāvayate 'pi ca /
anyojīvaḥ śarīrasya nāstikānāṃ mate sthitaḥ //
1.45.d:
यत्र तत्रानुमाने ऽस्मिन्कृतं भावयते ऽपि च ।
अन्योजीवः शरीरस्य नास्तिकानां मते स्थितः ॥
1.45.m: Wherever in this inference one conceives what is done, / the living soul is distinct from the body—such is the position in the doctrine of the materialists.

1.45.s:
retovaṭakaṇīkāyāṃ ghṛtapākādhivāsanam /
jātismṛtirayaskāntaḥ sūryakāntoṃ'bubhakṣaṇam //
1.45.d:
रेतोवटकणीकायां घृतपाकाधिवासनम् ।
जातिस्मृतिरयस्कान्तः सूर्यकान्तोंऽबुभक्षणम् ॥
1.45.m: The infusion of clarified butter when cooking, in a speck of a banyan seed, / the memory of past births, the lodestone, the sunstone, the drinking of water,

1.45.s:
pretabhūtapriyaścaiva devatā hyupayācanam /
mṛtakarmanivattiṃ ca pramāṇamiti niścayaḥ //
1.45.d:
प्रेतभूतप्रियश्चैव देवता ह्युपयाचनम् ।
मृतकर्मनिवत्तिं च प्रमाणमिति निश्चयः ॥
1.45.m: and the fondness for spirits and ghosts, the entreaty made to deities, / and the cessation of work upon death—the certainty is that [these] constitute proof.

1.45.s:
nanvete hetavaḥ saṃti ye kecinmūrtisasthitāḥ /
amūtasya hi mūrtena sāmānyaṃ nopalabhyate //
1.45.d:
नन्वेते हेतवः संति ये केचिन्मूर्तिसस्थिताः ।
अमूतस्य हि मूर्तेन सामान्यं नोपलभ्यते ॥
1.45.m: "Indeed, these reasons exist, whatever are located in material form; / for there is no commonality perceived between the formless and that which has form."

1.45.s:
avidyā karma tṛṣṇā ca kecidāhuḥ punarbhavam /
tasminnaṣṭe ca dagdhe ca citte maraṇadharmiṇi //
1.45.d:
अविद्या कर्म तृष्णा च केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवम् ।
तस्मिन्नष्टे च दग्धे च चित्ते मरणधर्मिणि ॥
1.45.m: "Some say that ignorance, action, and craving are rebirth; / and when that mortal mind is destroyed and burned,

1.45.s:
anyo 'smājjāyate mohastamāhuḥ sattvasaṃkṣayam /
yadā sarūpataścānyo jātitaḥ śrutator'thataḥ //
1.45.d:
अन्यो ऽस्माज्जायते मोहस्तमाहुः सत्त्वसंक्षयम् ।
यदा सरूपतश्चान्यो जातितः श्रुततोर्ऽथतः ॥
1.45.m: another delusion is born from this, which they call the destruction of the living being. / When it is different in form, birth, learning, and meaning,

1.45.s:
kathamasminsa ityeva saṃbandhaḥ syādasaṃhitaḥ /
evaṃ sati ca kā prīhirjñānavidyātapobalaiḥ //
1.45.d:
कथमस्मिन्स इत्येव संबन्धः स्यादसंहितः ।
एवं सति च का प्रीहिर्ज्ञानविद्यातपोबलैः ॥
1.45.m: how could an unconnected relation exist in this [case], such as 'this is he'? / If this be so, what joy is there in the powers of knowledge, learning, and austerities,

1.45.s:
yadasyācaritaṃ karma sāmānyātpratipadyate /
api tvayamihaivānyaiḥ prākṛtairduḥkhito bhavet //
1.45.d:
यदस्याचरितं कर्म सामान्यात्प्रतिपद्यते ।
अपि त्वयमिहैवान्यैः प्राकृतैर्दुःखितो भवेत् ॥
1.45.m: since he incurs the action performed by this [other] on account of commonality? / Rather, he would become distressed right here by other ordinary [factors].

1.45.s:
sukhito duḥkhito vāpi dṛśyādṛśyavinirṇayaḥ /
yathā hi muśalairhanyuḥ śarīraṃ tatpunarbhavet //
1.45.d:
सुखितो दुःखितो वापि दृश्यादृश्यविनिर्णयः ।
यथा हि मुशलैर्हन्युः शरीरं तत्पुनर्भवेत् ॥
1.45.m: Whether happy or distressed, there is the ascertainment of the visible and invisible; / just as if they beat a body with clubs, that would exist again.

1.45.s:
vṛthā jñānaṃ yadanyañca yenaitannopalabhyate /
ṛmasaṃvatsarau tiṣyaḥ śītoṣṇo 'tha priyāpriye //
1.45.d:
वृथा ज्ञानं यदन्यञ्च येनैतन्नोपलभ्यते ।
ऋमसंवत्सरौ तिष्यः शीतोष्णो ऽथ प्रियाप्रिये ॥
1.45.m: Futile is the knowledge that is different, by which this is not perceived: / seasons, years, the constellation Tiṣya, cold and heat, pleasant and unpleasant.

1.45.s:
yathā tātāni paśyati tādṛśaḥ sattvasaṃkṣayaḥ /
jarayābhiparītasya mṛtyunā ca vināśitam //
1.45.d:
यथा तातानि पश्यति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः ।
जरयाभिपरीतस्य मृत्युना च विनाशितम् ॥
1.45.m: As one sees these, such is the destruction of the living being; / destroyed by death when overcome by old age,

1.45.s:
durbalaṃ durbalaṃ pūrvaṃ gṛhasyeva vinaśyati /
indriyāṇi mano vāyuḥ śoṇitaṃ māṃsamasthi ca //
1.45.d:
दुर्बलं दुर्बलं पूर्वं गृहस्येव विनश्यति ।
इन्द्रियाणि मनो वायुः शोणितं मांसमस्थि च ॥
1.45.m: the weak [part] perishes first, like that of a house: / the senses, mind, breath, blood, flesh, and bone

1.45.s:
ānupūrvyā vinaśyanti svaṃ dhātumupayāti ca /
lokayātrāvidhātaśca dānadharmaphalāgame //
1.45.d:
आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति स्वं धातुमुपयाति च ।
लोकयात्राविधातश्च दानधर्मफलागमे ॥
1.45.m: perish in sequence and go to their own element. / And by the ordinance of worldly life, upon the arrival of the fruit of charity and righteousness,

1.45.s:
tadarthaṃ vedaṃśabdāśca vyavahārāśca laukikāḥ /
iti samyaṅ manasyete bahavaḥ saṃti hetavaḥ //
1.45.d:
तदर्थं वेदंशब्दाश्च व्यवहाराश्च लौकिकाः ।
इति सम्यङ् मनस्येते बहवः संति हेतवः ॥
1.45.m: there are the words of the Veda for that purpose, and worldly conventions. / Thus in the mind, there are indeed many reasons for this.

1.45.s:
aita dastīti nāstīti na kaścitpratidṛśyate /
teṣāṃ vimṛśatāmeva tatsamyagabhidhāvatām //
1.45.d:
ऐत दस्तीति नास्तीति न कश्चित्प्रतिदृश्यते ।
तेषां विमृशतामेव तत्सम्यगभिधावताम् ॥
1.45.m: No one is seen to clearly distinguish, 'This exists,' or 'This does not exist.' / While they are thus deliberating, running fully toward it,

1.45.s:
kvacinnivasate buddhistatra jīryati vṛkṣavat /
evantur thairanarthaiśca duḥkhitāḥ sarvajantavaḥ //
1.45.d:
क्वचिन्निवसते बुद्धिस्तत्र जीर्यति वृक्षवत् ।
एवन्तुर् थैरनर्थैश्च दुःखिताः सर्वजन्तवः ॥
1.45.m: the intellect settles somewhere, and there it withers like a tree. / Thus, distressed by purposeful and unpurposed things, all creatures

1.45.s: āgamairapakṛṣyante hastipairhastino yathā //
1.45.d: आगमैरपकृष्यन्ते हस्तिपैर्हस्तिनो यथा ॥
1.45.m: are dragged away by scriptures, as elephants are by elephant-drivers."

1.45.s:
arthāstathā hṝnti sukhāvahāṃśca lihata ete bahavopaśuṣkāḥ /
mahattaraṃ duḥkhamabhiprapannā hitvāmiṣaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ prayānti //
1.45.d:
अर्थास्तथा हॄन्ति सुखावहांश्च लिहत एते बहवोपशुष्काः ।
महत्तरं दुःखमभिप्रपन्ना हित्वामिषं मृत्युवशं प्रयान्ति ॥
1.45.m: "Objects of sense likewise carry off agreeable things; licking these, many wither away; / falling into greater sorrow, abandoning the bait, they pass into the power of death.

1.45.s:
vināśino hyadhruvajīvinaḥ kiṃ kiṃ bandhubhirmatraparigrahaiśca /
vihāya yo gacchati sarvameva kṣaṇena gatvā na nivartate ca //
1.45.d:
विनाशिनो ह्यध्रुवजीविनः किं किं बन्धुभिर्मत्रपरिग्रहैश्च ।
विहाय यो गच्छति सर्वमेव क्षणेन गत्वा न निवर्तते च ॥
1.45.m: What is the use of relatives, mantras, and possessions for those who perish, who live impermanently? / He who leaves everything and departs, having gone in an instant, does not return.

1.45.s:
bhūvyomatoyānalavāyavo 'pi sadā śarīraṃ pratipālayanti /
itīdamālakṣya ratiḥ kuto bhavedvināśināpyasya na śama vidyate //
1.45.d:
भूव्योमतोयानलवायवो ऽपि सदा शरीरं प्रतिपालयन्ति ।
इतीदमालक्ष्य रतिः कुतो भवेद्विनाशिनाप्यस्य न शम विद्यते ॥
1.45.m: Earth, space, water, fire, and wind also constantly sustain the body; / having perceived this, whence could pleasure arise? Even though it perishes, there is no peace for it."

1.45.s:
idamanupadhivākyamacchalaṃ paramanirāmayamātmasākṣikam /
narapatirabhivīkṣya vismitaḥ punaranuyoktumidaṃ pracakrame //
1.45.d:
इदमनुपधिवाक्यमच्छलं परमनिरामयमात्मसाक्षिकम् ।
नरपतिरभिवीक्ष्य विस्मितः पुनरनुयोक्तुमिदं प्रचक्रमे ॥
1.45.m: Seeing this speech—free from deceit, without guile, supremely wholesome, and witnessed by the Self— / the king of men was astonished, and proceeded to question him again:

1.45.s:
janaka uvāca
bhagavanyadi na pretya saṃjñā bhavati kasyacit /
evaṃ sati kimajñānaṃ jñānaṃ vā kiṃ kariṣyati //
1.45.d:
जनक उवाच
भगवन्यदि न प्रेत्य संज्ञा भवति कस्यचित् ।
एवं सति किमज्ञानं ज्ञानं वा किं करिष्यति ॥
1.45.m: Janaka said: / "O venerable one, if there is no consciousness for anyone after death, / this being so, what will ignorance do, or what will knowledge do?

1.45.s:
sarvamucchedaniṣṭasyātpaśya caitaddvijottama /
apramattaḥ pramatto vā kiṃ viśeṣaṃ kariṣyati //
1.45.d:
सर्वमुच्छेदनिष्टस्यात्पश्य चैतद्द्विजोत्तम ।
अप्रमत्तः प्रमत्तो वा किं विशेषं करिष्यति ॥
1.45.m: All would result in annihilation; see this, O best of the twice-born! / What distinction will the vigilant or the negligent make?

1.45.s:
asaṃsargo hi bhūteṣu saṃsargo vā vināśiṣu /
kasmai kriyata kalpeta niścayaḥ ko 'tra tattvataḥ //
1.45.d:
असंसर्गो हि भूतेषु संसर्गो वा विनाशिषु ।
कस्मै क्रियत कल्पेत निश्चयः को ऽत्र तत्त्वतः ॥
1.45.m: Non-contact with beings, or contact with perishable things: / for what purpose would an action be performed? What is the ascertainment in truth here?"

1.45.s:
sanandana uvāca
tamasā hi maticchatraṃ vibhrāntamiva cāturam /
punaḥ praśamayanvākyaiḥ kaviḥ pañcaśikho 'bravīt //
1.45.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
तमसा हि मतिच्छत्रं विभ्रान्तमिव चातुरम् ।
पुनः प्रशमयन्वाक्यैः कविः पञ्चशिखो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
1.45.m: Sanandana said: / As the umbrella of the intellect was bewildered and afflicted, as it were, by darkness, / the wise sage Pañcaśikha, calming him again with words, spoke:

1.45.s:
pañcaśikha uvāca
ucchedaniṣṭā nehāsti bhāvaniṣṭā na vidyate /
ayaṃ hyapi samāhāraḥ śarīredriyacetasām //
1.45.d:
पञ्चशिख उवाच
उच्छेदनिष्टा नेहास्ति भावनिष्टा न विद्यते ।
अयं ह्यपि समाहारः शरीरेद्रियचेतसाम् ॥
1.45.m: Pañcaśikha said: / "There is no annihilationism here, nor does eternalism exist. / For this is an aggregation of the body, the senses, and consciousness.

1.45.s:
vartate pṛthaganyonyamapyupāśritya karmasu /
dhātavaḥ pañcadhā toyaṃ khe vāyurjyotiṣo dharā //
1.45.d:
वर्तते पृथगन्योन्यमप्युपाश्रित्य कर्मसु ।
धातवः पञ्चधा तोयं खे वायुर्ज्योतिषो धरा ॥
1.45.m: It operates distinctly, having recourse also to one another in actions. / The elements are fivefold: water, wind in space, light, and earth.

1.45.s:
teṣu bhāvena tiṣṭanti viyujyante svabhāvataḥ /
ākāśaṃ vāyurūṣmā ca sneho yaścāpi pārthivaḥ //
1.45.d:
तेषु भावेन तिष्टन्ति वियुज्यन्ते स्वभावतः ।
आकाशं वायुरूष्मा च स्नेहो यश्चापि पार्थिवः ॥
1.45.m: They stay together through condition; they disunite by their own nature. / Space, wind, heat, moisture, and that which is earthy—

1.45.s:
eṣa pañcasamāhāraḥ śarīramapi naikadhā /
jñānamūṣmā ca vāyuśca trividhaḥ kāyasaṃgrahaḥ //
1.45.d:
एष पञ्चसमाहारः शरीरमपि नैकधा ।
ज्ञानमूष्मा च वायुश्च त्रिविधः कायसंग्रहः ॥
1.45.m: this fivefold aggregation is the body, manifold as well. / Knowledge, heat, and wind: this is the threefold constitution of the body.

1.45.s:
indriyāṇīndriyārthāśca svabhāvaścetanāmanaḥ /
prāṇāpānau vikāraśca dhātavaścātra niḥsṛtāḥ //
1.45.d:
इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च स्वभावश्चेतनामनः ।
प्राणापानौ विकारश्च धातवश्चात्र निःसृताः ॥
1.45.m: The senses, the objects of the senses, inherent nature, consciousness, mind, / prāṇa and apāna, modification, and the elements—these have issued forth here.

1.45.s:
śravaṇaṃ sparśanaṃ jihvā dṛṣṭirnāsā tathaiva ca /
indriyāṇīti pañcaite cittapūrvaṅgamā guṇāḥ //
1.45.d:
श्रवणं स्पर्शनं जिह्वा दृष्टिर्नासा तथैव च ।
इन्द्रियाणीति पञ्चैते चित्तपूर्वङ्गमा गुणाः ॥
1.45.m: Hearing, touch, tongue, sight, and nose likewise: / these are the five senses, qualities preceded by the mind.

1.45.s:
tatra vijñānasaṃyuktā trividhā cetanā dhruvā /
sukhaduḥkheti yāmāhuranaduḥkhāsukheti ca //
1.45.d:
तत्र विज्ञानसंयुक्ता त्रिविधा चेतना ध्रुवा ।
सुखदुःखेति यामाहुरनदुःखासुखेति च ॥
1.45.m: There, united with consciousness, constant consciousness is threefold, / which they speak of as pleasant, painful, and neither painful nor pleasant.

1.45.s:
śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca mūrtyarthameva te trayaḥ /
ete hyāmaraṇātpañca sadguṇā jñānasiddhaye //
1.45.d:
शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च मूर्त्यर्थमेव ते त्रयः ।
एते ह्यामरणात्पञ्च सद्गुणा ज्ञानसिद्धये ॥
1.45.m: Sound, touch, and form: these three are for the purpose of material form. / These five true qualities exist until death for the attainment of knowledge.

1.45.s:
teṣu karmaṇi siddhiśca sarvatattvārthaniścayaḥ /
tamāhuḥ paramaṃ śuddhiṃ buddhirityavyayaṃ mahat //
1.45.d:
तेषु कर्मणि सिद्धिश्च सर्वतत्त्वार्थनिश्चयः ।
तमाहुः परमं शुद्धिं बुद्धिरित्यव्ययं महत् ॥
1.45.m: In them is the accomplishment in action and the determination of all true principles; / that they call supreme purity, the great imperishable intellect.

1.45.s:
imaṃ guṇasamāhāramātmabhāvena paśyataḥ /
asamyagdarśanairduḥkhamanantaṃ nopaśāmyati //
1.45.d:
इमं गुणसमाहारमात्मभावेन पश्यतः ।
असम्यग्दर्शनैर्दुःखमनन्तं नोपशाम्यति ॥
1.45.m: For one who views this aggregate of qualities as the Self, / through incorrect perceptions endless sorrow is not pacified.

1.45.s:
anātmeti ca yadṛṣṭaṃ tenāhaṃ na mametyapi /
vartate kimadhiṣṭānātprasaktā duḥkhasaṃtatiḥ //
1.45.d:
अनात्मेति च यदृष्टं तेनाहं न ममेत्यपि ।
वर्तते किमधिष्टानात्प्रसक्ता दुःखसंततिः ॥
1.45.m: And because it is seen as not-self, through that there is 'not I, nor mine.' / From what foundation does the continuous succession of sorrow remain attached?

1.45.s:
tatra samyagjano nāma tyāgaśāstramanuttamam /
śṛṇuyāttacca mokṣāya bhāṣyamāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati //
1.45.d:
तत्र सम्यग्जनो नाम त्यागशास्त्रमनुत्तमम् ।
शृणुयात्तच्च मोक्षाय भाष्यमाणं भविष्यति ॥
1.45.m: There, a right-minded person should listen to the unsurpassed teaching on renunciation; / and that, being spoken, will lead to liberation.

1.45.s:
tyāga eva hi sarveṣāmuktānāmapi karmaṇām /
nityaṃ mithyāvinītānāṃ kleśo duḥkhāvaho tamaḥ //
1.45.d:
त्याग एव हि सर्वेषामुक्तानामपि कर्मणाम् ।
नित्यं मिथ्याविनीतानां क्लेशो दुःखावहो तमः ॥
1.45.m: For renunciation is indeed of all actions that have been spoken of; / for those who are falsely trained, affliction always brings sorrow and darkness.

1.45.s:
dravyatyāge tu karmāṇi bhogatyāge vratāni ca /
sukhatyāgā tapo yogaṃ sarvatyāge samāpanā //
1.45.d:
द्रव्यत्यागे तु कर्माणि भोगत्यागे व्रतानि च ।
सुखत्यागा तपो योगं सर्वत्यागे समापना ॥
1.45.m: In the renunciation of possessions lie rituals; in the renunciation of enjoyment, vows; / in the renunciation of pleasure, asceticism and yoga; in the renunciation of all, completion.

1.45.s:
tasya mārgo 'yamadvaidhaḥ sarvatyāgasya darśitaḥ /
viprahāṇāya duḥkhasya durgatirhi tathā bhavet //
1.45.d:
तस्य मार्गो ऽयमद्वैधः सर्वत्यागस्य दर्शितः ।
विप्रहाणाय दुःखस्य दुर्गतिर्हि तथा भवेत् ॥
1.45.m: This non-dual path of the renunciation of all has been shown / for the abandoning of sorrow, for otherwise a bad state would result.

1.45.s:
pañca jñānendriyāṇyuktvā manaḥ ṣaṣṭāni cetasi /
basaṣaṣṭāni vakṣyāmi pañca karmedriyāṇi tu //
1.45.d:
पञ्च ज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्युक्त्वा मनः षष्टानि चेतसि ।
बसषष्टानि वक्ष्यामि पञ्च कर्मेद्रियाणि तु ॥
1.45.m: Having spoken of the five senses of knowledge, with the mind as sixth in the intellect, / I shall speak of the five organs of action, with speech as the sixth.

1.45.s:
hastau karmedriyaṃ jñeyamatha pādau gatīndriyam /
prajanāna dayomeḍhro visargo pāyurindriyam //
1.45.d:
हस्तौ कर्मेद्रियं ज्ञेयमथ पादौ गतीन्द्रियम् ।
प्रजनान दयोमेढ्रो विसर्गो पायुरिन्द्रियम् ॥
1.45.m: The hands are to be known as an organ of action, and the feet as the organ of movement; / the penis is for reproduction and pleasure, and the anus is the organ for evacuation;

1.45.s:
vākca śabdaviśeṣārthamiti pañcānvitaṃ viduḥ /
evamekādaśetāni buddhyā tvavasṛjanmanaḥ //
1.45.d:
वाक्च शब्दविशेषार्थमिति पञ्चान्वितं विदुः ।
एवमेकादशेतानि बुद्ध्या त्ववसृजन्मनः ॥
1.45.m: and speech is for the purpose of distinguishing words—thus they know it as endowed with five. / Having thus given up these eleven along with the mind by means of the intellect,

1.45.s:
karṇo śabdaśca cittaṃ ca trayaḥ śravaṇasaṃgrahe /
tathā sparśe tathā rūpe tathaiva rasagandhayoḥ //
1.45.d:
कर्णो शब्दश्च चित्तं च त्रयः श्रवणसंग्रहे ।
तथा स्पर्शे तथा रूपे तथैव रसगन्धयोः ॥
1.45.m: ear, sound, and mind are the triad in the apprehension of hearing; / likewise in touch, likewise in form, and likewise in taste and smell.

1.45.s:
evaṃ pañca trikā hyete guṇastadupalabdhaye /
yenāyaṃ trividho bhāvaḥ paryāyātsamupasthitaḥ //
1.45.d:
एवं पञ्च त्रिका ह्येते गुणस्तदुपलब्धये ।
येनायं त्रिविधो भावः पर्यायात्समुपस्थितः ॥
1.45.m: Thus these five triads of qualities exist for their perception, / by which this threefold state arises in succession:

1.45.s:
sāttviko rājasaścāpi tāmasaścāpi te trayaḥ /
trividhā vedānā yeṣu prasṛtā sarvasādhinī //
1.45.d:
सात्त्विको राजसश्चापि तामसश्चापि ते त्रयः ।
त्रिविधा वेदाना येषु प्रसृता सर्वसाधिनी ॥
1.45.m: sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa are those three, / in which the threefold feeling, accomplishing everything, has spread forth.

1.45.s:
praharṣaḥ prītirānandaḥ sukhaṃ saṃśāntacittatā /
akutaścitkutaścidvā cittataḥ sāttviko guṇaḥ //
1.45.d:
प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः सुखं संशान्तचित्तता ।
अकुतश्चित्कुतश्चिद्वा चित्ततः सात्त्विको गुणः ॥
1.45.m: Delight, affection, joy, pleasure, and peace of mind, / whether from no cause or from some cause, arising from the mind, is the sāttvika quality.

1.45.s:
atuṣṭiḥ paritāpaśca śoko lobhastathākṣamā /
liṅgāni rajasastāni dṛśyante hetvahetutaḥ //
1.45.d:
अतुष्टिः परितापश्च शोको लोभस्तथाक्षमा ।
लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि दृश्यन्ते हेत्वहेतुतः ॥
1.45.m: Discontent, torment, grief, greed, and intolerance— / those signs of rajas are seen, whether from a cause or without a cause.

1.45.s:
avivekastathā mohaḥ pramādaḥ svapnatandritā /
kathañcidapi vartante vividhāstāmasā guṇāḥ //
1.45.d:
अविवेकस्तथा मोहः प्रमादः स्वप्नतन्द्रिता ।
कथञ्चिदपि वर्तन्ते विविधास्तामसा गुणाः ॥
1.45.m: Lack of discrimination, delusion, carelessness, sleep, and lethargy— / the manifold tāmasa qualities somehow exist."

1.45.s:
imāṃ ca yo veda vimokṣabuddhimātmānamanvicchati cāpramattaḥ /
na lipyate karmapalairaniṣṭaiḥ patraṃ viṣasyeva jalena siktam //
1.45.d:
इमां च यो वेद विमोक्षबुद्धिमात्मानमन्विच्छति चाप्रमत्तः ।
न लिप्यते कर्मपलैरनिष्टैः पत्रं विषस्येव जलेन सिक्तम् ॥
1.45.m: And whoever knows this discernment concerning liberation and seeks the Self with vigilance, / is not stained by undesirable fruits of actions, just as the leaf of a water-lily is not stained by water.

1.45.s:
dṛḍhairhi pāśairvividhairvimuktaḥ prajānimittairapi daivataiśca /
yadā hyasau duḥkhasaukhye jahāti muktastadāgryāṃ gatimetyaliṅgaḥ //
1.45.d:
दृढैर्हि पाशैर्विविधैर्विमुक्तः प्रजानिमित्तैरपि दैवतैश्च ।
यदा ह्यसौ दुःखसौख्ये जहाति मुक्तस्तदाग्र्यां गतिमेत्यलिङ्गः ॥
1.45.m: Being released indeed from various firm bonds caused by progeny as well as by deities, / when he truly abandons pleasure and pain, then, liberated and markless, he attains the highest goal.

1.45.s:
śrutipramāṇagamamaṅgalaiśca śeti jarāmṛtyubhayādatītaḥ /
kṣīṇe ca puṇye vigate ca pāpe tanornimitte ca phale vinaṣṭe //
1.45.d:
श्रुतिप्रमाणगममङ्गलैश्च शेति जरामृत्युभयादतीतः ।
क्षीणे च पुण्ये विगते च पापे तनोर्निमित्ते च फले विनष्टे ॥
1.45.m: And through the auspicious truths derived from the means of knowledge of the Vedas, he rests, gone beyond the fear of old age and death, / when merit is exhausted, evil has departed, and the fruit that caused the body has perished.

1.45.s:
alepamākāśamaliṅgamevamāsthāya paśyanti mahatyaśaktā /
yathorṇanābhiḥ parivartamānastantukṣaye tiṣṭati yātyamānaḥ //
1.45.d:
अलेपमाकाशमलिङ्गमेवमास्थाय पश्यन्ति महत्यशक्ता ।
यथोर्णनाभिः परिवर्तमानस्तन्तुक्षये तिष्टति यात्यमानः ॥
1.45.m: Resorting thus to the unstained, unconditioned space, those unable [to act] look upon the great [reality], / just as a spider, turning around when its thread is exhausted, remains, being led forth.

1.45.s:
tathā vimuktaḥ prajahāti duḥkhaṃ vidhaavaṃsate loṣṭamivādimṛcchan /
yathā ruruḥ śṛṅgamatho purāṇaṃ hitvā tvacaṃ vāpyurago yathā ca //
1.45.d:
तथा विमुक्तः प्रजहाति दुःखं विधअवंसते लोष्टमिवादिमृच्छन् ।
यथा रुरुः शृङ्गमथो पुराणं हित्वा त्वचं वाप्युरगो यथा च ॥
1.45.m: In that manner, the liberated one abandons sorrow; he falls away, as if reaching a clod of earth at the beginning; / just as a deer casts off its old horn, or just as a snake casts off its slough,

1.45.s:
vihāya gacchannanavekṣaghamāṇastathā vimukto vijahāti duḥkham /
matsyaṃ yathā vāpyudake patantamutsṛjya pakṣī nipatatsaśaktaḥ //
1.45.d:
विहाय गच्छन्ननवेक्षघमाणस्तथा विमुक्तो विजहाति दुःखम् ।
मत्स्यं यथा वाप्युदके पतन्तमुत्सृज्य पक्षी निपतत्सशक्तः ॥
1.45.m: departing without looking back, so the liberated one completely casts off sorrow; / or just as a bird capable of diving, releasing a fish that falls back into the water,

1.45.s: tathā hyasau duḥkhasaukhye vihāya muktaḥ parārddhyā gatimetyaliṅgaḥ //
1.45.d: तथा ह्यसौ दुःखसौख्ये विहाय मुक्तः परार्द्ध्या गतिमेत्यलिङ्गः ॥
1.45.m: even so, having abandoned pleasure and pain, the liberated one, markless, attains the highest goal.

1.45.s:
idamamṛtapadaṃ niśamya rājā svayamihapañcaśikhena bhāṣyamāṇam /
nikhilamabhisamīkṣya niścitārthaḥ paramasukhī vijahāra vītaśokaḥ //
1.45.d:
इदममृतपदं निशम्य राजा स्वयमिहपञ्चशिखेन भाष्यमाणम् ।
निखिलमभिसमीक्ष्य निश्चितार्थः परमसुखी विजहार वीतशोकः ॥
1.45.m: Having heard this immortal word spoken here personally by Pañcaśikha, / examining all of it and having ascertained its meaning, the king, free from grief, wandered about in supreme happiness.

1.45.s:
api ca bhavati maithilena gītaṃ nagaramupāhitamagninābhivīkṣya /
na khalu mama hi dahyate 'tra kiñcitsvayamidamāha kila sma bhūmipālaḥ //
1.45.d:
अपि च भवति मैथिलेन गीतं नगरमुपाहितमग्निनाभिवीक्ष्य ।
न खलु मम हि दह्यते ऽत्र किञ्चित्स्वयमिदमाह किल स्म भूमिपालः ॥
1.45.m: And indeed, it was sung by the ruler of Mithilā upon beholding the city engulfed by fire: / 'Truly nothing of mine burns here!'—so said the king himself.

1.45.s:
imaṃ hi yaḥ paṭhati vimokṣaniścayaṃ mahāmune satatamavekṣate tathā /
upadravānanubhaghavate hyaduḥ khitaḥ pramucyate kapilamivaitya maithilaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde pañcacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.45.d:
इमं हि यः पठति विमोक्षनिश्चयं महामुने सततमवेक्षते तथा ।
उपद्रवाननुभघवते ह्यदुः खितः प्रमुच्यते कपिलमिवैत्य मैथिलः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे पञ्चचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.45.m:
Whoever recites this ascertained doctrine of liberation, O great sage, and constantly contemplates it thus, / experiences calamities without being grieved, and is liberated just like the ruler of Mithilā after approaching Kapila.

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter in the second quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the glorious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.46.s:
sūta uvāca
tacchṛtvā nārado viprā maithilādhyātmamuttamam /
punaḥ papraccha taṃ prītyā sanandanamudāradhīḥ //
1.46.d:
सूत उवाच
तच्छृत्वा नारदो विप्रा मैथिलाध्यात्ममुत्तमम् ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ तं प्रीत्या सनन्दनमुदारधीः ॥
1.46.m: Sūta said: / Having heard that supreme spirituality of the ruler of Mithilā, O Brahmins, / Nārada of noble intellect asked Sanandana again with affection.

1.46.s:
nārada uvāca
ādhyātmikādatrividhaṃ tāpaṃ nānubhavedyathā /
prabrūhi tanmune mahyaṃ prapannāya dayānidhe //
1.46.d:
नारद उवाच
आध्यात्मिकादत्रिविधं तापं नानुभवेद्यथा ।
प्रब्रूहि तन्मुने मह्यं प्रपन्नाय दयानिधे ॥
1.46.m: Nārada said: / Tell me, O sage, treasure of compassion, to me who have surrendered [to you], / how one may not experience the threefold torment beginning with the internal.

1.46.s:
sanandana uvāca
tadasya trividhaṃ duḥkhamiha jātasya paṇḍita /
garbe janmajarādyeṣusthāneṣu prabhaviṣyataḥ //
1.46.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
तदस्य त्रिविधं दुःखमिह जातस्य पण्डित ।
गर्बे जन्मजराद्येषुस्थानेषु प्रभविष्यतः ॥
1.46.m: Sanandana said: / That threefold suffering belongs to one born here, O wise one, / who is about to arise in places such as the womb, birth, and old age.

1.46.s:
nirastātiśayāhlādasukhabhāvaikalakṣaṇā /
bheṣajaṃ bhagavatprāptiraikā cātyantikī matā //
1.46.d:
निरस्तातिशयाह्लादसुखभावैकलक्षणा ।
भेषजं भगवत्प्राप्तिरैका चात्यन्तिकी मता ॥
1.46.m: Attainment of the Blessed Lord, whose sole characteristic is the state of bliss and joy surpassing all others, / is considered the single and ultimate remedy.

1.46.s:
tasmāttatprāptaye yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ paṇḍitairnaraiḥ /
tatprāptihetujñānaṃ ca karma coktaṃ mahāmune //
1.46.d:
तस्मात्तत्प्राप्तये यत्नः कर्तव्यः पण्डितैर्नरैः ।
तत्प्राप्तिहेतुज्ञानं च कर्म चोक्तं महामुने ॥
1.46.m: Therefore, effort for attaining Him should be made by wise men; / and both knowledge and action have been declared the means of attaining Him, O great sage.

1.46.s:
āgamotthaṃ vivekāñca dvidhā jñānaṃ tathocyate /
śabdabrahmāgamamayaṃ paraṃ brahmavivekajam //
1.46.d:
आगमोत्थं विवेकाञ्च द्विधा ज्ञानं तथोच्यते ।
शब्दब्रह्मागममयं परं ब्रह्मविवेकजम् ॥
1.46.m: Knowledge is likewise said to be of two kinds: that arising from scripture and that from discrimination; / the sonic Brahman consists of scripture, while the supreme Brahman arises from discrimination.

1.46.s:
manurapyāha vedārthaṃ smṛtvāyaṃ munisattamamaḥ /
tadetacchrūyatāmatra subodhaṃ gadato mama //
1.46.d:
मनुरप्याह वेदार्थं स्मृत्वायं मुनिसत्तममः ।
तदेतच्छ्रूयतामत्र सुबोधं गदतो मम ॥
1.46.m: Remembering the meaning of the Veda, Manu also, the best of sages, spoke this; / let that be heard here as I speak it, easy to understand:

1.46.s:
dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat /
śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati //
1.46.d:
द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये शब्दब्रह्म परं च यत् ।
शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
1.46.m: 'Two Brahmans are to be known: the sonic Brahman and that which is supreme; / one who is well-versed in the sonic Brahman attains the supreme Brahman.'

1.46.s:
dve vidye veditavye cetyāha cātharvaṇī śrutiḥ /
paramā tvakṣaraprāptirṛgvedādimayā parā //
1.46.d:
द्वे विद्ये वेदितव्ये चेत्याह चाथर्वणी श्रुतिः ।
परमा त्वक्षरप्राप्तिरृग्वेदादिमया परा ॥
1.46.m: And the Atharvaṇa Vedic text declares: 'Two kinds of knowledge are to be known'; / the supreme is the attainment of the imperishable, while the other consists of the Ṛgveda and the rest.

1.46.s:
yattadavyaktamajaramanīhamajamavyayam /
anirdeśyamarūpaṃ ca pāṇipādādisaṃyutam //
1.46.d:
यत्तदव्यक्तमजरमनीहमजमव्ययम् ।
अनिर्देश्यमरूपं च पाणिपादादिसंयुतम् ॥
1.46.m: That which is unmanifest, ageless, devoid of exertion, unborn, imperishable, / undefinable, formless, yet possessed of hands, feet, and other limbs,

1.46.s:
vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ nityaṃ bhūtayo nimakāraṇam /
vyāpyaṃ vyāptaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ taṃ vai paśyanti sūrayaḥ //
1.46.d:
विभुं सर्वगतं नित्यं भूतयो निमकारणम् ।
व्याप्यं व्याप्तं यतः सर्वं तं वै पश्यन्ति सूरयः ॥
1.46.m: all-pervading, omnipresent, eternal, the cause of the source of beings, / by whom everything pervaded is pervaded—that indeed the wise behold.

1.46.s:
tadbūhya tatparaṃ dhāma taddhyeyaṃ mo7kāṅkṣibhiḥ /
śrutivākyoditaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.46.d:
तद्बूह्य तत्परं धाम तद्ध्येयं मो7काङ्क्षिभिः ।
श्रुतिवाक्योदितं सूक्ष्मं तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.46.m: That is to be conceived, that is the supreme abode, that is to be meditated upon by seekers of liberation; / proclaimed by Vedic declarations, subtle—that is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.46.s:
tadeva bhagavadvācyaṃ svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ /
vācako bhagavacchabdastasyoddiṣṭo 'kṣayātmanaḥ //
1.46.d:
तदेव भगवद्वाच्यं स्वरूपं परमात्मनः ।
वाचको भगवच्छब्दस्तस्योद्दिष्टो ऽक्षयात्मनः ॥
1.46.m: That alone is the essential nature of the Supreme Self signified by 'bhagavat'; / the word 'bhagavat' is designated as the designator of that imperishable Self.

1.46.s:
evaṃ nigaditārthasya yattatvaṃ tasya tattvataḥ /
jñāyate yena tajjñānaṃ paramanyatrayīmayam //
1.46.d:
एवं निगदितार्थस्य यत्तत्वं तस्य तत्त्वतः ।
ज्ञायते येन तज्ज्ञानं परमन्यत्रयीमयम् ॥
1.46.m: The reality of that which has been thus explained, by which it is known in truth— / that is supreme knowledge; the other consists of the three Vedas.

1.46.s:
aśabdagocarasyāpi tasya vai brahmaṇo dvijā /
pūjāyāṃ bhagavacchabdaḥ kriyate hyaupacārikaḥ //
1.46.d:
अशब्दगोचरस्यापि तस्य वै ब्रह्मणो द्विजा ।
पूजायां भगवच्छब्दः क्रियते ह्यौपचारिकः ॥
1.46.m: Even of that Brahman which is beyond the range of words, O twice-born, / the word 'bhagavat' is used figuratively in worship.

1.46.s:
śuddhe mahāvibhūtyākhye pare brahmaṇi varttate /
bhagavanbhagavacchabdaḥ sarvakāraṇakāraṇe //
jñeyaṃ jñāteti tathā bhakāror'thadvayātmakaḥ /
tenāgamapitā sraṣṭā gakāro 'yaṃ tathā mune //
1.46.d:
शुद्धे महाविभूत्याख्ये परे ब्रह्मणि वर्त्तते ।
भगवन्भगवच्छब्दः सर्वकारणकारणे ॥
ज्ञेयं ज्ञातेति तथा भकारोर्ऽथद्वयात्मकः ।
तेनागमपिता स्रष्टा गकारो ऽयं तथा मुने ॥
1.46.m: The word 'bhagavat', O venerable one, applies to the pure, supreme Brahman called 'of great majesty', / the cause of all causes. / The syllable 'bha' has two meanings: the object of knowledge and the knower; / likewise, O sage, the syllable 'ga' is the leader, father, and creator.

1.46.s:
aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ /
jñānavairāgyayoścaiva ṣaṇṇāṃ bhaga itīraṇā //
1.46.d:
ऐश्वर्यस्य समग्रस्य वीर्यस्य यशसः श्रियः ।
ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्चैव षण्णां भग इतीरणा ॥
1.46.m: Total sovereignty, virility, fame, splendour, / and knowledge and dispassion—these six are called 'bhaga'.

1.46.s:
vasaṃti tatra bhūtāni bhūtātmanyakhilātmani /
sarvabhūteṣvaśeṣeṣu vakārārthastato 'vyayaḥ //
1.46.d:
वसंति तत्र भूतानि भूतात्मन्यखिलात्मनि ।
सर्वभूतेष्वशेषेषु वकारार्थस्ततो ऽव्ययः ॥
1.46.m: All beings dwell in Him, the Self of beings, the universal Self, / and He [dwells] in all beings without remainder; hence the meaning of the syllable 'va' is the imperishable.

1.46.s:
evameva mahāśabdo bhagavāniti sattama /
paramabrahmabhūtasya vāsudevasya nānyagaḥ //
1.46.d:
एवमेव महाशब्दो भगवानिति सत्तम ।
परमब्रह्मभूतस्य वासुदेवस्य नान्यगः ॥
1.46.m: Thus this great word 'bhagavān', O best of beings, / belongs only to Vāsudeva, who is the Supreme Brahman, and to no other.

1.46.s:
tatra pūjyapadārthoktiḥ paribhāṣāsamanvitaḥ /
śabdo 'yaṃ nopacāreṇa cānyatra hyupacārataḥ //
1.46.d:
तत्र पूज्यपदार्थोक्तिः परिभाषासमन्वितः ।
शब्दो ऽयं नोपचारेण चान्यत्र ह्युपचारतः ॥
1.46.m: There, it expresses an object of worship accompanied by technical definition; / this word is not applied figuratively to Him, whereas elsewhere it is applied figuratively.

1.46.s:
utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānāmāgatiṃ gatim /
vetti vidyāmavidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavāniti //
1.46.d:
उत्पत्तिं प्रलयं चैव भूतानामागतिं गतिम् ।
वेत्ति विद्यामविद्यां च स वाच्यो भगवानिति ॥
1.46.m: He who knows the origin and dissolution, the arrival and departure of beings, / and knowledge and ignorance—he is to be called 'bhagavān'.

1.46.s:
jñānaśaktibalaiśvaryavīryatejāṃsyaśeṣataḥ /
bhagavacchabdavācyāni vinā heyairguṇādibhiḥ //
1.46.d:
ज्ञानशक्तिबलैश्वर्यवीर्यतेजांस्यशेषतः ।
भगवच्छब्दवाच्यानि विना हेयैर्गुणादिभिः ॥
1.46.m: Knowledge, power, strength, sovereignty, virility, and splendour without remainder, / are denoted by the word 'bhagavat', devoid of all undesirable qualities and the like.

1.46.s:
sarvāṇi tatra bhūtāni vasaṃti paramātmani /
bhūteṣu vasanādeva vāsudevastataḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.46.d:
सर्वाणि तत्र भूतानि वसंति परमात्मनि ।
भूतेषु वसनादेव वासुदेवस्ततः स्मृतः ॥
1.46.m: All beings dwell in Him, the Supreme Self, / and because of His dwelling in beings, He is traditionally called Vāsudeva.

1.46.s:
khāṇḍikyaṃ janakaṃ prāha pṛṣṭaḥ keśidhvajaḥ purā /
nāmavyākhyāmanantasya vāsudevasya tattvataḥ //
1.46.d:
खाण्डिक्यं जनकं प्राह पृष्टः केशिध्वजः पुरा ।
नामव्याख्यामनन्तस्य वासुदेवस्य तत्त्वतः ॥
1.46.m: Formerly, Keśidhvaja, when asked, explained in truth to Khāṇḍikya Janaka / the meaning of the name of the infinite Vāsudeva:

1.46.s:
bhūteṣu vasate soṃ'tarvasaṃtyatra ca tāni yat /
dhātā vidhātā jagatāṃ vāsudevastataḥ prabhuḥ //
1.46.d:
भूतेषु वसते सोंऽतर्वसंत्यत्र च तानि यत् ।
धाता विधाता जगतां वासुदेवस्ततः प्रभुः ॥
1.46.m: "Because he dwells within all beings, and because they dwell in him, / he is the creator and ordainer of worlds, therefore the Lord is Vāsudeva.

1.46.s:
sa sarvabhūtaprakṛtiṃ vikāraṃ guṇādidoṣāṃśca mune vyatītaḥ /
atītasarvāvaraṇo 'khilātmā tenāstṛtaṃ yadbhuvanāntarālam //
1.46.d:
स सर्वभूतप्रकृतिं विकारं गुणादिदोषांश्च मुने व्यतीतः ।
अतीतसर्वावरणो ऽखिलात्मा तेनास्तृतं यद्भुवनान्तरालम् ॥
1.46.m: O sage, he transcends the material nature of all beings, its modification, and the defects such as the guṇas; / he has transcended all coverings, the Self of all, by whom the intermediate space of the worlds is pervaded.

1.46.s:
samastakalyāṇaguṇaṃ guṇātmako hitvātiduḥkhāvṛtabhūtasargaḥ /
icchāgṛhītābhimatorudehaḥ saṃsādhitāśeṣajagaddhito 'sau //
1.46.d:
समस्तकल्याणगुणं गुणात्मको हित्वातिदुःखावृतभूतसर्गः ।
इच्छागृहीताभिमतोरुदेहः संसाधिताशेषजगद्धितो ऽसौ ॥
1.46.m: Free from the creation of beings enveloped in extreme suffering, he possesses all auspicious qualities, being of the nature of virtues; / by his own will he assumes his vast beloved body, having accomplished the welfare of all worlds.

1.46.s:
tejobalaiśvaryamahāvabodhaṃ svavīryaśaktyāduguṇaikarāśiḥ /
paraḥ parāṇāṃ sakalā na yatra kleśādayaḥ saṃti parāvareśe //
1.46.d:
तेजोबलैश्वर्यमहावबोधं स्ववीर्यशक्त्यादुगुणैकराशिः ।
परः पराणां सकला न यत्र क्लेशादयः संति परावरेशे ॥
1.46.m: He is a sole mass of virtues such as splendor, strength, sovereignty, supreme awareness, his own valor, and power; / higher than the highest, in whom, the ruler of high and low, no afflictions or similar taints exist.

1.46.s:
sa īśvaro vyaṣṭisamaṣṭirūpo 'vyaktasvarūpaḥ prakaṭasvarūpaḥ /
sarveśvaraḥ sarvanisargavettā samaskaśaktiḥ parameśvarākhyaḥ //
1.46.d:
स ईश्वरो व्यष्टिसमष्टिरूपो ऽव्यक्तस्वरूपः प्रकटस्वरूपः ।
सर्वेश्वरः सर्वनिसर्गवेत्ता समस्कशक्तिः परमेश्वराख्यः ॥
1.46.m: He is the Lord whose form is both individual and aggregate, unmanifest in essence and manifest in form; / the Lord of all, knower of all natures, endowed with all power, designated as the Supreme Lord.

1.46.s:
sa jñāyate yena tadastadoṣaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ nirmalameva rūpam /
saṃdṛśyate cāpyavagamyate ca tajjñānamato 'nyaduktam //
1.46.d:
स ज्ञायते येन तदस्तदोषं शुद्धं परं निर्मलमेव रूपम् ।
संदृश्यते चाप्यवगम्यते च तज्ज्ञानमतो ऽन्यदुक्तम् ॥
1.46.m: That by which his flawless, pure, supreme, and completely stainless form / is known, seen, and comprehended—that is knowledge; other than that is declared [ignorance].

1.46.s:
/.
svādhyāyasaṃyamābagyāṃ sa dṛśyate puruṣottamaḥ /
tatprāptikāraṇaṃ brahma tavetatpratipadyate //
1.46.d:
॥
स्वाध्यायसंयमाबग्यां स दृश्यते पुरुषोत्तमः ।
तत्प्राप्तिकारणं ब्रह्म तवेतत्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
1.46.m: Through Vedic study and restraint, that Highest Person is seen; / Brahman, the cause of attaining him, is comprehended in this way by you.

1.46.s:
svādhyāyādyogamāsīta yogātsvādhyāyamāmanet /
svādhyāyayogasaṃpattyā paramātmā prakāśate //
1.46.d:
स्वाध्यायाद्योगमासीत योगात्स्वाध्यायमामनेत् ।
स्वाध्याययोगसंपत्त्या परमात्मा प्रकाशते ॥
1.46.m: From Vedic study one should sit in yoga; from yoga one should reflect upon Vedic study; / by the perfection of Vedic study and yoga, the Supreme Self shines forth.

1.46.s:
tadīkṣaṇāya svādhyāyaścakṣuryogastathāparam /
na māṃsacakṣuṣā draṣṭuṃ brahmabhūtaḥ sa śakyate //
1.46.d:
तदीक्षणाय स्वाध्यायश्चक्षुर्योगस्तथापरम् ।
न मांसचक्षुषा द्रष्टुं ब्रह्मभूतः स शक्यते ॥
1.46.m: For perceiving him, Vedic study is one eye, and yoga is the other; / one who has become Brahman cannot be seen with the eye of flesh."

1.46.d:
॥ नारद उवाच
भगवंस्तमहं योगं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तं वद ।
ज्ञाते यन्नाखिलाधारं पश्येयं परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.46.m: Nārada said: / "O lord, I desire to know that yoga; tell it to me, / knowing which I may behold the Supreme Lord, the support of all."

1.46.s:
sanandana uvāca
keśidhvajo yathā prāha khāṇḍikyāya mahātmane /
janakāya purā yogaṃ tathāhaṃ kathayāmi te //
1.46.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
केशिध्वजो यथा प्राह खाण्डिक्याय महात्मने ।
जनकाय पुरा योगं तथाहं कथयामि ते ॥
1.46.m: Sanandana said: / "Just as Keśidhvaja formerly spoke yoga to the great-souled Khāṇḍikya Janaka, / so I shall relate it to you."

1.46.s:
nārada uvāca
khāṇḍikyaḥ ko 'bhavadbrahman ko vā keśidhvajo 'bhavat /
kathaṃ tayośca saṃvādo yogasaṃbandhavānabhūt //
1.46.d:
नारद उवाच
खाण्डिक्यः को ऽभवद्ब्रह्मन् को वा केशिध्वजो ऽभवत् ।
कथं तयोश्च संवादो योगसंबन्धवानभूत् ॥
1.46.m: Nārada said: / "Who was Khāṇḍikya, O Brahman, or who was Keśidhvaja? / And how did their conversation concerning yoga take place?"

1.46.s:
sanandana uvāca
dharmadhvajo vai janaka tasya puśe 'mitadhvajaḥ /
kṛtadhvajo 'sya bhrātābhūtsadādhyātmaratirnṛpaḥ //
1.46.d:
सनन्दन उवाच
धर्मध्वजो वै जनक तस्य पुशे ऽमितध्वजः ।
कृतध्वजो ऽस्य भ्राताभूत्सदाध्यात्मरतिर्नृपः ॥
1.46.m: Sanandana said: / "Dharmadhvaja was indeed a Janaka; his son was Amitadhvaja. / Kṛtadhvaja was his brother, a king who always delighted in the supreme self.

1.46.s:
kṛtadhvajasya putro 'bhūddhanyaḥ keśidhvajo dvijaḥ /
putro 'mitavvajasyāpi khāṇḍikyajanakābhidhaḥ //
karmamārge hi khāṇḍikyaḥ svarājyādavaropitaḥ /
purodhasā mantribhiśca samaveto 'lpasādhanaḥ //
1.46.d:
कृतध्वजस्य पुत्रो ऽभूद्धन्यः केशिध्वजो द्विजः ।
पुत्रो ऽमितव्वजस्यापि खाण्डिक्यजनकाभिधः ॥
कर्ममार्गे हि खाण्डिक्यः स्वराज्यादवरोपितः ।
पुरोधसा मन्त्रिभिश्च समवेतो ऽल्पसाधनः ॥
1.46.m: The son of Kṛtadhvaja was the fortunate twice-born Keśidhvaja; / and the son of Amitadhvaja was named Khāṇḍikya Janaka. / For Khāṇḍikya was deposed from his own kingdom along the path of ritual action; / accompanied by his family priest and ministers, he possessed few resources.

1.46.s:
rājyānnirākṛtaḥ so 'tha durgāraṇyacaro 'bhavat /
iyāḍaja so 'pi subahūna yajñāñjñānavyapāśrayaḥ //
1.46.d:
राज्यान्निराकृतः सो ऽथ दुर्गारण्यचरो ऽभवत् ।
इयाडज सो ऽपि सुबहून यज्ञाञ्ज्ञानव्यपाश्रयः ॥
1.46.m: Banished from his kingdom, he then wandered in the impassable forest; / having taken recourse in knowledge, he also performed very many sacrifices,

1.46.s:
brahmavidyāmadhiṣṭāya tartuṃ mṛtyumapi svayam /
ekadā vartamānasya yāge yogavidāṃ vara //
1.46.d:
ब्रह्मविद्यामधिष्टाय तर्तुं मृत्युमपि स्वयम् ।
एकदा वर्तमानस्य यागे योगविदां वर ॥
1.46.m: having taken his stand on the knowledge of Brahman in order to cross beyond death himself. / Once, while he was engaged in a sacrifice, O best of the knowers of yoga,

1.46.s:
tasya dhenuṃ jaghānograḥ śārdūlo vijane vane /
tato rājā hatāṃ jñātvā dhenuṃ vyāghreṇa cartvijaḥ //
1.46.d:
तस्य धेनुं जघानोग्रः शार्दूलो विजने वने ।
ततो राजा हतां ज्ञात्वा धेनुं व्याघ्रेण चर्त्विजः ॥
1.46.m: a fierce tiger killed his cow in a deserted forest. / Then, learning that the cow had been killed by a tiger, the king asked his priests

1.46.s:
prāyaścittaṃ sa papraccha kimatreti vidhīyatām /
te cocurnavayaṃvidmaḥ kaśeruḥ pṛcchyatāmiti //
1.46.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं स पप्रच्छ किमत्रेति विधीयताम् ।
ते चोचुर्नवयंविद्मः कशेरुः पृच्छ्यतामिति ॥
1.46.m: for an expiation: 'What should be performed here?' / And they said, 'We do not know; let Kaśeru be asked.'

1.46.s:
kaśerurapi tenoktastatheti prāha nārada /
śunakaṃ pṛccha rājendra veda sa vetsyati //
1.46.d:
कशेरुरपि तेनोक्तस्तथेति प्राह नारद ।
शुनकं पृच्छ राजेन्द्र वेद स वेत्स्यति ॥
1.46.m: Kaśeru also, addressed by him, said: 'So be it,' O Nārada; / 'Ask Śunaka, O best of kings; he knows, he will understand.'

1.46.s:
sa gatvā tamapṛcchañca so 'pyāha nṛpatiṃ mune /
na kaśerurnacaivāhaṃ na cānyaḥ sāṃprataṃ bhuvi //
1.46.d:
स गत्वा तमपृच्छञ्च सो ऽप्याह नृपतिं मुने ।
न कशेरुर्नचैवाहं न चान्यः सांप्रतं भुवि ॥
1.46.m: Having gone, he questioned him, and he also said to the king, O sage: / 'Neither Kaśeru, nor I, nor anyone else on earth at present

1.46.s:
vettyeka eva tvacchatruḥ khāṇḍikyo yo jitastvayā /
sa cāha taṃ vrajāmyeṣa praṣṭumātmaripuṃ mune //
1.46.d:
वेत्त्येक एव त्वच्छत्रुः खाण्डिक्यो यो जितस्त्वया ।
स चाह तं व्रजाम्येष प्रष्टुमात्मरिपुं मुने ॥
1.46.m: knows, except your enemy Khāṇḍikya alone, who was conquered by you.' / And he said to him: 'I will go to question my own enemy, O sage.

1.46.s:
prāpta eva mayā yajñe yadi māṃ sa haniṣyati /
prāyaścittaṃ sa cetpṛṣṭo vadiṣyati ripurmama //
1.46.d:
प्राप्त एव मया यज्ञे यदि मां स हनिष्यति ।
प्रायश्चित्तं स चेत्पृष्टो वदिष्यति रिपुर्मम ॥
1.46.m: If he kills me, the sacrifice will indeed have been accomplished by me; / if my enemy, being questioned, declares the expiation,

1.46.s:
tataścāvikalo yogo muniśreṣṭha bhaviṣyati /
ityuktvā rathamāruhya kṛṣṇājinadharo nṛpaḥ //
1.46.d:
ततश्चाविकलो योगो मुनिश्रेष्ठ भविष्यति ।
इत्युक्त्वा रथमारुह्य कृष्णाजिनधरो नृपः ॥
1.46.m: then the sacrifice will be complete, O best of sages.' / Having spoken thus, the king mounted his chariot, wearing a black antelope skin,

1.46.s:
vanaṃ jagāma yatrāste khāṇḍikyaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ /
tamāyāntaṃ samālokya khāñjaḍikyo ripumātmanaḥ //
1.46.d:
वनं जगाम यत्रास्ते खाण्डिक्यः स महीपतिः ।
तमायान्तं समालोक्य खाञ्जडिक्यो रिपुमात्मनः ॥
1.46.m: and went to the forest where that ruler of the earth, Khāṇḍikya, resided. / Seeing his enemy arriving,

1.46.s:
provāca krodhatāmrākṣaḥ samāropitakārmukaḥ /
khāṇḍikya uvāca
kṛṣṇājinatvakkavacabhāvenāsmānhaniṣyasi //
1.46.d:
प्रोवाच क्रोधताम्राक्षः समारोपितकार्मुकः ।
खाण्डिक्य उवाच
कृष्णाजिनत्वक्कवचभावेनास्मान्हनिष्यसि ॥
1.46.m: Khāṇḍikya, his eyes red with anger, with strung bow, spoke. / Khāṇḍikya said: / 'Will you slay us under the guise of wearing a black antelope skin as armor?

1.46.s:
kṛṣṇājinadhare vetsi na mayi prahariṣyati /
mṛgānāṃ vada pṛṣṭeṣu mūḍha kṛṣṇājinaṃ na kim //
1.46.d:
कृष्णाजिनधरे वेत्सि न मयि प्रहरिष्यति ।
मृगानां वद पृष्टेषु मूढ कृष्णाजिनं न किम् ॥
1.46.m: Do you think: "He will not strike me while I wear a black antelope skin"? / Tell me, fool, is there not a black antelope skin on the backs of deer,

1.46.s:
yeṣāṃ matvā vṛthā cogrāḥ prahitāḥ śitasāyakāḥ /
sa tvāmahaṃ haniṣyāmi na me jīvanvimokṣyase //
1.46.d:
येषां मत्वा वृथा चोग्राः प्रहिताः शितसायकाः ।
स त्वामहं हनिष्यामि न मे जीवन्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
1.46.m: against whom fierce, sharp arrows are discharged without hesitation? / I shall kill you; you will not escape me alive!

1.46.s:
ātatāyyasi durbuddhe mama rājyaharo ripuḥ /
keśidhvaja uvāca
khāṇḍikya saṃśayaṃ praṣṭuṃ bhavantamahamāgataḥ //
1.46.d:
आतताय्यसि दुर्बुद्धे मम राज्यहरो रिपुः ।
केशिध्वज उवाच
खाण्डिक्य संशयं प्रष्टुं भवन्तमहमागतः ॥
1.46.m: You are a treacherous foe, O evil-minded one, who seized my kingdom!' / Keśidhvaja said: / 'O Khāṇḍikya, I have come to ask you about a doubt,

1.46.s:
na tvāṃ hṝntuṃ vicāryataitkopaṃ bāṇaṃ ca muñca vā /
tataḥ sa mantribhiḥ sārddhamekānte sapurohitaḥ //
1.46.d:
न त्वां हॄन्तुं विचार्यतैत्कोपं बाणं च मुञ्च वा ।
ततः स मन्त्रिभिः सार्द्धमेकान्ते सपुरोहितः ॥
1.46.m: not to kill you; consider this, and release your anger and arrow.' / Then, together with his ministers and family priest in private,

1.46.s:
mantrayāmāsa khāṇḍikyaḥ sarvaireva mahāmatiḥ /
tamūrmantriṇo vadhyo ripureṣa vaśaṅgataḥ //
1.46.d:
मन्त्रयामास खाण्डिक्यः सर्वैरेव महामतिः ।
तमूर्मन्त्रिणो वध्यो रिपुरेष वशङ्गतः ॥
1.46.m: the highly intelligent Khāṇḍikya deliberated with them all. / The ministers said to him: 'This enemy has fallen into your power; he should be killed!

1.46.s:
hate 'tra pṛthivī sarvā tava vaśyā bhaviṣyati /
khāṇḍikyaścāha tānsarvāneva meva na saṃśayaḥ //
1.46.d:
हते ऽत्र पृथिवी सर्वा तव वश्या भविष्यति ।
खाण्डिक्यश्चाह तान्सर्वानेव मेव न संशयः ॥
1.46.m: When he is killed, the entire earth will be under your control.' / Khāṇḍikya said to them all: 'It is so indeed, there is no doubt:

1.46.s:
hate tu pṛthivī sarvā mama vaśyā bhaviṣyati /
paralokajayastasya pṛthivī sakalā mama //
1.46.d:
हते तु पृथिवी सर्वा मम वश्या भविष्यति ।
परलोकजयस्तस्य पृथिवी सकला मम ॥
1.46.m: if he is killed, the entire earth will be under my control. / Conquest of the next world is his, while the whole earth is mine.

1.46.s:
na hanmi cellokajayo mama vayatvaḥsuṃdharā /
paralokajayo 'nantaḥ svalpakālo mahījayaḥ //
1.46.d:
न हन्मि चेल्लोकजयो मम वयत्वःसुंधरा ।
परलोकजयो ऽनन्तः स्वल्पकालो महीजयः ॥
1.46.m: If I do not kill him, the conquest of worlds will be mine, even though the earth belongs to him; / conquest of the other world is eternal, while conquest of the earth lasts but a short time.

1.46.s:
tasmānnainaṃ haniṣye 'haṃ yatpṛcchati vadāmi tat /
tatastamabhyupetyāha khāṇḍikyo janako ripum //
1.46.d:
तस्मान्नैनं हनिष्ये ऽहं यत्पृच्छति वदामि तत् ।
ततस्तमभ्युपेत्याह खाण्डिक्यो जनको रिपुम् ॥
1.46.m: Therefore, I will not kill him; I will answer what he asks.' / Then Khāṇḍikya Janaka, having approached his enemy, said:

1.46.s:
praṣṭavyaṃ yattvayā sarvaṃ tatpṛccha tvaṃ vadāmyaham /
tataḥ prāha yathāvṛttaṃ homadhenuvadhaṃ mune //
1.46.d:
प्रष्टव्यं यत्त्वया सर्वं तत्पृच्छ त्वं वदाम्यहम् ।
ततः प्राह यथावृत्तं होमधेनुवधं मुने ॥
1.46.m: 'Whatever is to be asked by you, ask all that; I will tell you.' / Then he related, O sage, the slaughter of the sacrificial cow just as it had occurred.

1.46.s:
tataśca taṃ sa papraccha prāyaścittaṃ hi tadrūtam /
sa cācaṣṭa yathānyāyaṃ mune keśidhvajāya tat //
1.46.d:
ततश्च तं स पप्रच्छ प्रायश्चित्तं हि तद्रूतम् ।
स चाचष्ट यथान्यायं मुने केशिध्वजाय तत् ॥
1.46.m: And then he quickly asked him for the expiation for it, / and he explained that properly to Keśidhvaja, O sage—

1.46.s:
prāyaścittamaśeṣaṃ hi yadvai tatra vidhīyate /
viditārthaḥ sa tenaivamanujñāto mahātmanā //
1.46.d:
प्रायश्चित्तमशेषं हि यद्वै तत्र विधीयते ।
विदितार्थः स तेनैवमनुज्ञातो महात्मना ॥
1.46.m: the entire expiation, indeed, which is prescribed in that case. / Having understood the matter, and permitted by that great-souled one,

1.46.s:
yāgabhūmimupāgatya cakre sarvāṃ kriyāṃ kramat /
krameṇa vidhivadyāgaṃ nītvā so 'vabhṛthāplutaḥ //
1.46.d:
यागभूमिमुपागत्य चक्रे सर्वां क्रियां क्रमत् ।
क्रमेण विधिवद्यागं नीत्वा सो ऽवभृथाप्लुतः ॥
1.46.m: he went to the sacrificial ground and performed all the rites in sequence. / Having duly brought the sacrifice to completion in order, and having bathed in the concluding bath,

1.46.s:
kṛtakṛtyastato bhūtvā cintayāmāsa pārthivaḥ /
pūjitā ṛtvijaḥ sarve sadasyā mānitā mayā //
1.46.d:
कृतकृत्यस्ततो भूत्वा चिन्तयामास पार्थिवः ।
पूजिता ऋत्विजः सर्वे सदस्या मानिता मया ॥
1.46.m: and having thus achieved his purpose, the king reflected: / 'All the officiating priests have been honored, the assembly members respected by me,

1.46.s:
tathaivārthijano 'pyarthojito 'bhimatairmayā /
yathāhaṃ martyalokasya mayā sarvaṃ vicaṣṭitam //
1.46.d:
तथैवार्थिजनो ऽप्यर्थोजितो ऽभिमतैर्मया ।
यथाहं मर्त्यलोकस्य मया सर्वं विचष्टितम् ॥
1.46.m: and the supplicants have been gratified by me with their desired wealth; / I have done everything properly according to the mortal world.

1.46.s:
aniṣpannakriyaṃ cetastathā na mama kiṃ yathā /
itthaṃ tu cintayanneva saṃmāra sa mahīpatiḥ //
1.46.d:
अनिष्पन्नक्रियं चेतस्तथा न मम किं यथा ।
इत्थं तु चिन्तयन्नेव संमार स महीपतिः ॥
1.46.m: Why, then, does my mind feel as though its duties are incomplete?' / While thus reflecting, the ruler of the earth remembered:

1.46.s:
khāṇḍikyāya na datteti mayā vaigurudakṣiṇā /
sa jagāma tato bhūyo rathamāruhya pārthivaḥ //
1.46.d:
खाण्डिक्याय न दत्तेति मया वैगुरुदक्षिणा ।
स जगाम ततो भूयो रथमारुह्य पार्थिवः ॥
1.46.m: 'The fee for the preceptor has not been given by me to Khāṇḍikya!' / Thereupon, mounting his chariot again, the king went

1.46.s:
svāyaṃbhuvaḥ sthito yatra khāṇḍikyo 'raṇyadurgamam /
khāṇḍikyo 'pi punarddaṣṭvā tamāyāntaṃ dhṛtāyudhaḥ //
1.46.d:
स्वायंभुवः स्थितो यत्र खाण्डिक्यो ऽरण्यदुर्गमम् ।
खाण्डिक्यो ऽपि पुनर्द्दष्ट्वा तमायान्तं धृतायुधः ॥
1.46.m: to the impassable forest where Khāṇḍikya of Svāyambhuva's lineage was residing. / Khāṇḍikya also, seeing him arriving once more, took up his weapon.

1.46.s:
tasthau hṝntuṃ kṛtamatismamāha sa punarnṛpaḥ /
ahaṃ tu nāpakārāya prāptaḥ khāṇḍikya mā krudhaḥ //
1.46.d:
तस्थौ हॄन्तुं कृतमतिस्ममाह स पुनर्नृपः ।
अहं तु नापकाराय प्राप्तः खाण्डिक्य मा क्रुधः ॥
1.46.m:
stood determined to slay him. But that king spoke again:
“I have not arrived to do harm, Khāṇḍikya; do not be angry!

1.46.s:
gurorniṣkṛtidānāya māmavehi semāgatam /
niṣpādito mayā yāgaḥ samyak tvadupadeśataḥ //
1.46.d:
गुरोर्निष्कृतिदानाय मामवेहि सेमागतम् ।
निष्पादितो मया यागः सम्यक् त्वदुपदेशतः ॥
1.46.m:
Know that I have come to offer the teacher's fee.
The sacrifice has been duly accomplished by me according to your instruction.

1.46.s:
so 'haṃ te dātumicchāmi vṛṇīṣva gurudakṣiṇām /
ityukto mantrayāmāsa sa bhūyo mantribhiḥ saha //
1.46.d:
सो ऽहं ते दातुमिच्छामि वृणीष्व गुरुदक्षिणाम् ।
इत्युक्तो मन्त्रयामास स भूयो मन्त्रिभिः सह ॥
1.46.m:
As such, I desire to give it to you; choose your teacher's fee!”
Addressed thus, he took counsel once more with his ministers.

1.46.s:
gurorniṣkṛtikāmo 'ya kimayaṃ prārthyatāṃ mayā /
tamūcurmantriṇo gajyamaśeṣaṃ yācyatāmayam //
1.46.d:
गुरोर्निष्कृतिकामो ऽय किमयं प्रार्थ्यतां मया ।
तमूचुर्मन्त्रिणो गज्यमशेषं याच्यतामयम् ॥
1.46.m:
“This man desires to give the teacher's fee; what should I ask of him?”
The ministers said to him: “Let the entire kingdom be requested of him!

1.46.s:
kṛtābhiḥ prārthyate rājyamanāyāsitasainikaiḥ /
prāhasya tānāha nṛpaḥ sa khāṇḍikyo mahāpatiḥ //
1.46.d:
कृताभिः प्रार्थ्यते राज्यमनायासितसैनिकैः ।
प्राहस्य तानाह नृपः स खाण्डिक्यो महापतिः ॥
1.46.m:
A kingdom is sought after without putting soldiers to trouble.”
Laughing, that king, Khāṇḍikya, the great lord, said to them:

1.46.s:
svalpakālaṃ mahīrājyaṃ mādṛśaiḥ prārthyate katham /
etametadbhaṃvato 'tra svārtha sādhanamantriṇaḥ //
1.46.d:
स्वल्पकालं महीराज्यं मादृशैः प्रार्थ्यते कथम् ।
एतमेतद्भंवतो ऽत्र स्वार्थ साधनमन्त्रिणः ॥
1.46.m:
“How could an earthly kingdom of very short duration be sought by people like me?
Indeed, you are counsellors here who accomplish [only] selfish worldly ends.

1.46.s:
paramārthaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra yūyaṃ nātra vicakṣaṇāḥ /
ityuktvā samupetyaiṃnaṃ sa tu keśidhvajaṃ nṛpam //
1.46.d:
परमार्थः कथं को ऽत्र यूयं नात्र विचक्षणाः ।
इत्युक्त्वा समुपेत्यैंनं स तु केशिध्वजं नृपम् ॥
1.46.m:
What is the ultimate truth here, and how is it? You are not discerning in this matter.”
Having spoken thus and approached King Keśidhvaja,

1.46.s:
uvāca kimavaśyaṃ tvaṃ dāsyasi gurudakṣiṇām /
bāḍhamityeva tenoktaḥ khāṇḍikyastamathābravīt //
1.46.d:
उवाच किमवश्यं त्वं दास्यसि गुरुदक्षिणाम् ।
बाढमित्येव तेनोक्तः खाण्डिक्यस्तमथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.46.m:
he said: “Will you certainly give the teacher's fee?”
When told, “Certainly,” by him, Khāṇḍikya then said to him:

1.46.s:
bhavānadhyātmavijñānaparamārthavicakṣaṇaḥ /
yadi ceddīyate mahyaṃ bhavatā guruniṣkrayaḥ //
1.46.d:
भवानध्यात्मविज्ञानपरमार्थविचक्षणः ।
यदि चेद्दीयते मह्यं भवता गुरुनिष्क्रयः ॥
1.46.m:
“You are expert in the ultimate truth of the knowledge of the Self.
If a teacher's fee is indeed to be given to me by you,

1.46.s:
tatkleśapraśamāyālaṃ yatkarma tadudīraya /
keśidhvaja uvāca
na prārthitaṃ tvayā kasmānmama rājyamakaṇṭakam //
1.46.d:
तत्क्लेशप्रशमायालं यत्कर्म तदुदीरय ।
केशिध्वज उवाच
न प्रार्थितं त्वया कस्मान्मम राज्यमकण्टकम् ॥
1.46.m:
then declare that action which is capable of quelling afflictions.”
Keśidhvaja said:
“Why was my kingdom without rivals not requested by you?

1.46.s:
rājyalābhāḥ ddhi nāstyanyatkṣatriyāṇāmatipriyam /
khāṇḍikya uvāca
keśidhvaja nibodha tvaṃ mayā na prārthitaṃ yataḥ //
1.46.d:
राज्यलाभाः द्धि नास्त्यन्यत्क्षत्रियाणामतिप्रियम् ।
खाण्डिक्य उवाच
केशिध्वज निबोध त्वं मया न प्रार्थितं यतः ॥
1.46.m:
For there is nothing else more dear to kṣatriyas than gaining a kingdom.”
Khāṇḍikya said:
“Understand, Keśidhvaja, the reason why it was not requested by me.

1.46.s:
rājyametadaśeṣeṇa yanna gṛghranti paṇḍitāḥ /
kṣatriyāṇāmayaṃ dharmo yatprajāparipālanam //
1.46.d:
राज्यमेतदशेषेण यन्न गृघ्रन्ति पण्डिताः ।
क्षत्रियाणामयं धर्मो यत्प्रजापरिपालनम् ॥
1.46.m:
This entire kingdom is something which the wise do not covet.
This is the duty of kṣatriyas: the protection of subjects,

1.46.s:
vadhaśca dharmayuddhena svarājyaparipanthinām /
yatrāśaktasya me doṣo naivāstyapakṛte tvayā //
1.46.d:
वधश्च धर्मयुद्धेन स्वराज्यपरिपन्थिनाम् ।
यत्राशक्तस्य मे दोषो नैवास्त्यपकृते त्वया ॥
1.46.m:
and the slaying in righteous battle of the adversaries of one's kingdom.
When I was incapable in that regard, there was no fault in me, nor was any harm done by you.

1.46.s:
bandhāyaiva bhavatyeṣā hyavidyā cākramojjhitā /
janmoparbhāgalipsārthamiyaṃ gajyaspṛhā mama //
1.46.d:
बन्धायैव भवत्येषा ह्यविद्या चाक्रमोज्झिता ।
जन्मोपर्भागलिप्सार्थमियं गज्यस्पृहा मम ॥
1.46.m:
This ignorance, abandoned without proper stages, leads only to bondage.
Such a desire for a kingdom would be mine only for the sake of obtaining a subsequent birth.

1.46.s:
anyeṣāṃ dopajāneva dharmamevānurudhyate /
na yācñā kṣatrabandhūnāṃ dharmāyaitatsatāṃ matam //
1.46.d:
अन्येषां दोपजानेव धर्ममेवानुरुध्यते ।
न याच्ञा क्षत्रबन्धूनां धर्मायैतत्सतां मतम् ॥
1.46.m:
Knowing the faults of others, one conforms only to duty;
begging is not for the duty of fallen kṣatriyas—this is the view of the virtuous.

1.46.s:
ato na yācita rājyamavidyāntargataṃ tava /
rājyaṃ gṛdhnanti vidvāṃso mamatvākṛṣṭacetasaḥ //
1.46.d:
अतो न याचित राज्यमविद्यान्तर्गतं तव ।
राज्यं गृध्नन्ति विद्वांसो ममत्वाकृष्टचेतसः ॥
1.46.m:
Therefore your kingdom, which belongs within ignorance, was not requested.
Do the wise, their minds drawn away by mine-ness, covet a kingdom?

1.46.s:
ahaṃmānamahya pānamadamattā na mādṛśāḥ /
keśidhvaja uvāca
ahaṃ ca vidyayā mṛtyuṃ tartukāmaḥ karomi vai //
1.46.d:
अहंमानमह्य पानमदमत्ता न मादृशाः ।
केशिध्वज उवाच
अहं च विद्यया मृत्युं तर्तुकामः करोमि वै ॥
1.46.m:
People like me are not intoxicated by pride, drunk on the potion of egotism.”
Keśidhvaja said:
“Desiring to cross beyond death by means of knowledge, I indeed govern

1.46.s:
rājyaṃ yajñāṃśca vividhānbhoge puṇyakṣayaṃ tathā /
tadidaṃ te mano diṣṭyā vivekaiścaryatāṃ gatam //
1.46.d:
राज्यं यज्ञांश्च विविधान्भोगे पुण्यक्षयं तथा ।
तदिदं ते मनो दिष्ट्या विवेकैश्चर्यतां गतम् ॥
1.46.m:
the kingdom and perform various sacrifices, and likewise exhaust merit in enjoyment.
By good fortune, this mind of yours has attained the wealth of discernment.

1.46.s:
śrūyatāṃ cāpyavidyāyāḥ svarūpaṃ kulanandana /
anātmanyātmabuddhiryā hyasve svaviṣayā matiḥ //
1.46.d:
श्रूयतां चाप्यविद्यायाः स्वरूपं कुलनन्दन ।
अनात्मन्यात्मबुद्धिर्या ह्यस्वे स्वविषया मतिः ॥
1.46.m:
And hear also the essential nature of ignorance, O delight of your family!
The notion of the Self in what is not the Self, and the thought of ‘mine’ in what is not one's own,

1.46.s:
avidyātarusaṃnbhūtaṃ bījametaddvidhā sthitam /
pañcabhūtātmake dehe dehī mohatamovṛttaḥ //
1.46.d:
अविद्यातरुसंन्भूतं बीजमेतद्द्विधा स्थितम् ।
पञ्चभूतात्मके देहे देही मोहतमोवृत्तः ॥
1.46.m:
is the twofold seed born of the tree of ignorance.
In the body composed of the five elements, the embodied self, enveloped in the darkness of delusion,

1.46.s:
ahametaditītyuñcaiḥ kurute kumatirmatim /
ākāśavāyvagrijalapṛthivībhiḥ pṛthak sthite //
1.46.d:
अहमेतदितीत्युञ्चैः कुरुते कुमतिर्मतिम् ।
आकाशवाय्वग्रिजलपृथिवीभिः पृथक् स्थिते ॥
1.46.m:
foolishly forms the lofty notion: ‘I am this.’
When the Self stands distinct from space, wind, fire, water, and earth,

1.46.s:
ātmanyātmamayaṃ bhāvaṃ kaḥ karoti kalevare /
kalevaropabhogyaṃ hi gṛhakṣetrādikaṃ ca yat //
1.46.d:
आत्मन्यात्ममयं भावं कः करोति कलेवरे ।
कलेवरोपभोग्यं हि गृहक्षेत्रादिकं च यत् ॥
1.46.m:
who conceives the idea of the Self in the bodily frame?
And whatever is an object of enjoyment for the bodily frame, such as house, field, and the like,

1.46.s:
adehe hyātmani prājño mamedamiti manyate /
itthaṃ ca putrapautreṣu taddehotpāditeṣu ca //
1.46.d:
अदेहे ह्यात्मनि प्राज्ञो ममेदमिति मन्यते ।
इत्थं च पुत्रपौत्रेषु तद्देहोत्पादितेषु च ॥
1.46.m:
the [supposedly] wise man thinks ‘This is mine’ with regard to the bodiless Self.
And likewise in regard to sons and grandsons produced from that body,

1.46.s:
karoti paṇḍitaḥ svāmyamanātmani kalevare /
sarvadehopabhogāya kurute karma mānavaḥ //
1.46.d:
करोति पण्डितः स्वाम्यमनात्मनि कलेवरे ।
सर्वदेहोपभोगाय कुरुते कर्म मानवः ॥
1.46.m:
the learned man assumes ownership over the non-Self physical frame.
A man performs action for the sake of the enjoyment of the whole body;

1.46.s:
dehaṃ cānyadyadā puṃsaḥsadā bandhāya tatparam /
mṛṇmayaṃ hi yathā gehaṃ lipyate vai mṛdaṃ bhasā //
1.46.d:
देहं चान्यद्यदा पुंसःसदा बन्धाय तत्परम् ।
मृण्मयं हि यथा गेहं लिप्यते वै मृदं भसा ॥
1.46.m:
and when another body comes to a man, that leads always to further bondage.
For just as a house made of clay is smeared with clay and water,

1.46.s:
pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā deho mṛdaṃbholepanasthitiḥ /
pañcabhogātmakairbhogaiḥ pañcabhogātmakaṃ vapuḥ //
1.46.d:
पार्थिवो ऽयं तथा देहो मृदंभोलेपनस्थितिः ।
पञ्चभोगात्मकैर्भोगैः पञ्चभोगात्मकं वपुः ॥
1.46.m:
so this earthly body is maintained by plastering with clay and water.
If the body composed of five enjoyments is nourished

1.46.s:
āpyāyate yadi tataḥ puṃso garvo 'tra kiṅkṛtaḥ /
anekajanmasāhastraṃ sasārapadavīṃ vrajan //
1.46.d:
आप्यायते यदि ततः पुंसो गर्वो ऽत्र किङ्कृतः ।
अनेकजन्मसाहस्त्रं ससारपदवीं व्रजन् ॥
1.46.m:
by pleasures consisting of the five sensory objects, what cause for pride is there here for a man?
Wandering along the path of worldly existence through many thousands of births,

1.46.s:
mohaśramaṃ prayāto 'sau vāsanāreṇuguṇṭhitaḥ /
prakṣālyate yadā saumya reṇurjñānoṣṇavāriṇā //
1.46.d:
मोहश्रमं प्रयातो ऽसौ वासनारेणुगुण्ठितः ।
प्रक्षाल्यते यदा सौम्य रेणुर्ज्ञानोष्णवारिणा ॥
1.46.m:
he has incurred the weariness of delusion, covered with the dust of latent impressions.
When that dust is washed away, gentle one, by the warm water of knowledge,

1.46.s:
tadā saṃsārapānthasya yāti mohaśramaḥ śamam /
mohaśrame śamaṃ yāte svacchāntaḥkaraṇaḥ pumān //
1.46.d:
तदा संसारपान्थस्य याति मोहश्रमः शमम् ।
मोहश्रमे शमं याते स्वच्छान्तःकरणः पुमान् ॥
1.46.m:
then the weariness of delusion comes to an end for the traveler in worldly existence.
When the weariness of delusion has ceased, the person of pure inner sense,

1.46.s:
ananyātiśayādhāraḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamṛcchati /
nirvāṇamaya evāyamātmā jñānamayo 'malaḥ //
1.46.d:
अनन्यातिशयाधारः परं निर्वाणमृच्छति ।
निर्वाणमय एवायमात्मा ज्ञानमयो ऽमलः ॥
1.46.m:
the substrate of unsurpassable excellence, attains supreme nirvāṇa.
This Self is indeed of the nature of nirvāṇa, of the nature of knowledge, taintless.

1.46.s:
duḥkhājñānamayā dharmāḥ prakṛteste tunātmanaḥ /
jalasya nāgninā saṃgaḥ sthālīsaṃgāttathāpi hi //
1.46.d:
दुःखाज्ञानमया धर्माः प्रकृतेस्ते तुनात्मनः ।
जलस्य नाग्निना संगः स्थालीसंगात्तथापि हि ॥
1.46.m:
Attributes consisting of suffering and ignorance belong to material nature, but not to the Self.
Just as water has no contact with fire, yet through contact with the pot

1.46.s:
śabdodrekādikāndharmānkaroti hi yathā budhaḥ /
tathātmā prakṛteḥ saṃgādahaṃmānādidūṣitaḥ //
1.46.d:
शब्दोद्रेकादिकान्धर्मान्करोति हि यथा बुधः ।
तथात्मा प्रकृतेः संगादहंमानादिदूषितः ॥
1.46.m:
it manifests properties such as bubbling sounds, as the wise know,
even so the Self, defiled by egotism and the like through contact with material nature,

1.46.s:
bhajate prākṛtāndharmānnyastastaṃbho hi so 'vyayaḥ /
tadetatkathitaṃ bījamavidyāyā mayā tava //
1.46.d:
भजते प्राकृतान्धर्मान्न्यस्तस्तंभो हि सो ऽव्ययः ।
तदेतत्कथितं बीजमविद्याया मया तव ॥
1.46.m:
experiences natural properties, yet that imperishable one is an immovable pillar.
This seed of ignorance has thus been described by me to you.

1.46.s:
kleśānāṃ ca kṣayakaraṃ yogādanyanna vidyate //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne dvitīyapāde ṣaṭcatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.46.d:
क्लेशानां च क्षयकरं योगादन्यन्न विद्यते ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने द्वितीयपादे षट्चत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.46.m:
And there is nothing other than yoga that destroys afflictions.”

Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter in the second quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
